analysis.name: Anu Taranath
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I've taken post colonial lit and the Bangalore  study abroad with Dr. Taranath and believe she is one of the most influential professors I've ever had. You learn and engage beyond readings and quizzes. She discusses race, sexuality, gender, disability, etc. in a valuable way. It makes some uncomfortable/defensive but she is kind in her approach. :)

When I read posts saying that Anu would "change your life" I was really curious...  I took her class to experience this miracle of a teacher myself.  She's LEGIT!  I learned so much from Anu.  I rated "1" for easiness because of the critical thinking involved, but as long as you give an honest effort, she's a really easy grader.  Take this class!

Anu will challenge you to be a better human being.  The class forces you to re-examine your beliefs and to view the world through a whole different lens.  I've been to private school, public school, community college, and am currently a Junior at UW. This is the best class I've taken in my entire academic career. 10/10

Amazing, passionate teacher! Anu forever changed my views of the world and how I see things. Her classes are amazing, and the literature that she teaches are outside the usual 'canon' and fascinating. Highly recommended. I learned so much from her.

Professor Taranath is warm and friendly. Essentially if you show up to class and respond to her/your classmates, you will do well. Had to read 3 books and a few other short readings. No book reports, just discussion posts on canvas and in-class journalling and discussion. Her lecture style is very engaging and she clearly cares about her students.

analysis.name: Andrea (Andy) Heald
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 80 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS EVER. Math 308 is known to be a very interesting class but it was such a big mistake taking it with her, she doesn't teach at all. first 10 mins she gives 2 theorems and tells us to do the worksheets in group, when ask questions, she rather asks rhetorical questions. Not worth it at all, please avoid taking her class.

I would NOT take Heald! Her lectures were extremely disorganized. It was very clear that she knew the material, but when it came to class, I felt she was just reading from the textbook. She would often spend a whole class explaining topics that could be summed up in 5 minutes. She is an extremely harsh grader and gets very stingy on the test.

Prof Heald is a decent math professor. Although I attend lecture, I often don't have any idea what is going on, so I watch Thomas Carr on YouTube. Exams aren't too difficult, but they are account for way too much of the grade. Midterm/Final = 82% of total grade. That said, these are a bit out of her control and rather at fault of the department

Exams are sadly nothing like practice exams, however, often reflect weekly written homework assignments. Lectures were directly from the textbook, and I often found myself understanding the material better when I taught myself. Office hours are very helpful for homework problems, and she'll directly check your work :)

During lecture, they would go through a problem and realized they messed up somewhere. Lectures felt unprepared and a lot of the time, we would run out of time mid problem and then they'll move onto the next chapter the next day. Also skips a lot of steps in the problem and assume you understand whats going on

analysis.name: Usama al-Binni
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 108 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This dude doesn't have a good structure for teaching. His lectures are scattered, homework is a pain, plus there's pre-class quizzes that he posts only a day in advance. I spent most of my time reading the book. I worked through whatever practice midterm he posted. But guess what? The tests were totally different in question type and difficulty

When he talks its like his words have no substance, it literally does not make sense. You really have to spend time studying a lot by yourself for certain topics for them to make sense. Theres a lot of homework and the textbook is also useless. His practice midterms are NOTHING like the actual test so prepared to be screwed over.
Avoid if possible... the worst... he's a new professor and UW made a mistake hiring him.

He talks in a monotone, says um and ah way too much, doesn't teach anything and reads off his slides that are basically copied from the textbook. His practice exams are full of errors and mistakes and he's overall a very frustrating professor.

Too smart. Doesn't bother to actually teach the information. He just puts it on a slide, reads the information, and makes you figure out how to solve stuff when practicing for an exam.  And then when he shows you how to solve practice problems before an exam. He solves w/o showing work and using methods he doesn't teach you.

analysis.name: Ann Frost
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: SHE'S ABSOLUTELY AMAZING!!! This was my first time taking a class with her and she had a "mom" vibe - caring and funny while giving some good lectures! She's very personable and friendly, encouraging students to send in requests for songs even. The tests were pretty easy and you MUST SHOW for lectures or else you'll struggle!

Ann is a sweetheart of an instructor. If you are considering her summer 14 seminar on wrongful convictions you should sign up. You will be graded on contribution to discussions, 2 small reading presentations, and 3 papers (3-5, 3-5, 6-8 pg). She's very knowledgeable about the subject & it seemed like every class I had something to look forward to.

Pros: 
- Guest speakers

- Warm, approachable, and funny 

- Posed questions that challenged students to think deeper

- 1-4 readings per week (mostly 1-3)  

- Class felt like a book club 

- Intriguing content 

Cons: 
- Too much time was dedicated to student commentary 

- Sometimes the lecture content felt surface level and brief

Very interesting and fun class. Had a few guest speakers who work in different fields of crime-solving and prosecution. Guest speakers were fun, & so were her lectures. If you're looking for a fun class, I highly recommend this class with this teacher. Very few assignments with easy grading. She's very enthusiastic and fun to talk to and listen to.

I love this woman. She is HILARIOUS and also so helpful if you want to object a grade or try to understand class concepts more. She has advised me on several independent study projects and written me a letter of rec. I am eternally grateful to this woman for he passion and inspirational personality. She grades medium-hard but tests are a breeze.

analysis.name: Ann Borys
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Definitely dropping this class. Very boring to listen to. Quizzes are ambiguous. She expects you to understand and remember small details that she very quickly mentions in lecture. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU WANT EASY CREDITS.
It's almost like she wants to prove people this class is not supposed to be easy by making super ambiguous tests. Do not take it.

If you are taking this class for a GPA boost, look elsewhere! The lectures are fast-paced, off topic, and confusing, and the tests are even worse!  The questions are vague and opinion based. She posts her lecture slides, but they have no information on them, only pictures, making it difficult to study.  Don't waste money on the book.

This is for class ARCH 351. Scary bad teaching style, I understand she is filling in for another teacher on sabbatical but it's astounding how little she can say on a building. The words symmetrical, solid, and masonry were the extent of vocabulary. Literally baddd tests, longest note card ever and it still won't help. So rude too.

Doesn't accommodate for anything, including the studio class most of us were taking. Most of what I learned was from the textbook. Most effort in this class was put into the note sheet for the exam because we were expected to write about details she barely covered in lecture (made it very hard to actually learn anything)

analysis.name: Anne Wagner
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Content is ok, lectures are overly long for what the content is and somehow doesn't fully cover how to do hw problems.  The autograder is useful for feedback but super problematic to be honest just based on how confusing it is.  Luckily the course load isn't bad and async is nice.  Could work on making lecture content more translational to R.

Actively in this class, but wanted to review! I'm not a stats person and I suck at coding, but I've had no issues in this class. 5-6 video lectures per week is a lot, but they cover interesting content + the homework is straightforward if you go through the content. I enjoy her jokes/comments in lectures and if you reach out to her she's so sweet!

Her lectures are long and don't always cover how to EFFECTIVELY translate that info over to R. She's kind and is helpful 1 on 1 but there're too many students to be able to always get that experience in OH. Her content isn't as cohesive and her discussion assignments are also unclear with exactly what they want making you lose points. Class is mid.

Honestly, I'm glad this class is over. There's an autograder that just sucks at grading homework, and most of the content did not even make sense. Somehow the lectures made that worse. Also, the write-up assignments are very unclear and disorganized. 
I had to take this course for a credit; if you don't have to, then save yourself the trouble.

lectures were not as helpful as it should be, had lots of unrelated stuff. my grade was only saved by my wonderful TA, he would walk through my wrong answers then updated my grade to be better which encouraged students to go to office hours to learn from their mistakes. worst 8 am ever. tests every 2 weeks in QS and the final is in lecture hall.

analysis.name: Zack Almquist
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took the 3-credit option with no lab, and there was so much work given each week that it should have been 5 credits. The content was interesting and none of it was hard, but it was time-consuming and a lot of busy work. I would take another online class for an easier time unless you need this to fulfill a specific requirement.

WAY TO MUCH WORK for the 3 credit option! Plan to spend the whole day working on the class or at least one hour a day. Consists of long lectures, 5 discussion posts, and 2 replies for each discussion + a reading response that consists of 5+ long readings every week. On top of that, there are 3 memos Basically a 5 credit class with no lab. No exams.

SOC 225 Data and Society, great course for any major programs with data science option requiring ethics component, makes broad connections, prompts own independent critical thinking. Course makes Sociology basically human-centered applied statistics.

SOC331 is probably the worst class I have ever taken. The lectures were just so boring. The assignments literally never made any sense and I don't understand what we were even doing with google sheets. I went to ask for help once and he had horrible breath and I never talked to him again. The whole class was incredibly awkward, especially the final
Lectures are prerecorded, usually a few years old, with questionable quality. However, the course as a whole is pretting interesting and focuses on modern topics of AI.

analysis.name: Bo Zhang
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is very excited and knowledgeable but he is not good at conveying information in lectures and goes off on lots of little tangents that don't contribute to the class. I ended up not attending class after the first midterm and instead watched the recorded lectures so I could skip or focus on specific parts, and that improved my next midterm score.

had fun taking his class. he specializes in electrochemistry, so there was a lot of focus given to that unit. the lecture slides are really wordy and i found them difficult to understand sometimes. the quiz sections were really helpful, and the exams were very similar to the questions on the quiz section practice packets. really good class overall.

I hesitated to take Bo Zhang's class because of the negative reviews, but I'm glad I did. All of his tests align with his PowerPoints, worksheets, and practice problems, and you can honestly just learn from his recordings. His tests are super straightforward, and he actively encourages students to ask him questions and form relationships with him.

Bo Zhang is a nice person, but is not the best when it comes to teaching content. His lectures are too wordy, with little to no explanation on the concepts. His lectures contain all the important equations, but doesn't explain coherently the fundamental concepts on using them. I would not recommend him for 152.

Hard to understand and goes on tangents easily. So far my least favorite professor but I also don't like chemistry. Hard to follow and you need to self teach a lot, he doesn't teach what you need to practice on ALEKS. Nice guy but not the best teacher.

analysis.name: Beth Traxler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She doesn't care about students at all. Never reply emails even though she said in the lecture that "feel free to send me an email if you have any questions. Her lectures are not organized at all. Sometimes I don't even know what she's talking about

410 was an incredibly difficult class intended for future researchers, not for biopre-med students. You must memorize EVERYTHING on the slides! (A few words that seem like unimportant tidbits will end up a test question.) Long and tricky exams, not graded on a bell curve. People sleep during her lectures. Take 301302 instead!

Hardest class in the department, but she's a really good lecture and loves discourse. Make use of office hours and asking questions. May seem a little intimidating but is very nice and passionate about what she teaches.

You can tell she is very interested in the material when she talks but that is not the problem. Their are clicker questions that she writes the morning off that half the class doesnt understand but they still get graded. She goes over complex material 2 days before exam. Confusing when she talks, very unprofessional.

HARD class. No lecture record so very important to go to classes+take good notes. Traxler talks fast, hard for note taking even with printed lecture slides, which only were uploaded the night before sometimes even the morning right before lecture. I asked a prof to fix this but no change! Nice & enthusiastic, but I learned more from Kendall & labs.

analysis.name: Betsy Evans
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You have to come to class on time or else you will feel targeted by her. I think she holds grudges. 8 online test that are very confusing as well as 9 online assignments. Make sure you are clear and concise with your free response answers because she grades hard. Also, its hard to get a good grade. I was there everyday, got 87% which is a 3.2.

I took Sociolinguistics, an incredible course for those interested in linguistics. She is a tough grader and there are research assignments throughout the quarter. If interested in studying under her, I recommend speaking to her about what she expects on exams because she is particular. Go to class, it'll help. Take if serious about linguistics.

rubrics and assignment guidelines all incredibly unclear. clearly passionate, but lectures were poorly paced and often boring. the only reason i didn't drop this class was because i needed the credit, and it wasn't even a hard class. despised her teaching style and every single assignment made me want to bend my laptop in half.

Quiz sections are optional aside from the midterm. Prof Evans does really care about the topic but the lectures do get boring at times. She is very nice though and quite understanding. Pretty easy class, I did not read the textbook once but I do recommend going to lectures if you don't read the textbook.

Passionate about her subject and getting the class to participate. Weekly assignments/quizzes are easy and not timed. However, the midterm was bad. Idk if that was the TA's grading, but somehow I managed to get a 74 while getting 90-100 on everything else including a 95% on the final I didn't study for. Took down my grade to a 3.6 (91).

analysis.name: Patricia Buchanan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is a very nice person but a horrible professor. Her assignment documents and grading criteria are hilariously vague, yet despite that she is a strict grader. She is very difficult to access and most of the time will not help you. She is busy with her job outside of teaching, but she really should devote more time to her classes.Class wasnt hard

This class had a midterm, final, weekly quizzes and in-class activities, so it requires pretty regular review (as with Patty's other classes!). Patty was very considerate by allowing up to 2 quiz drops. The organization of examples and information on her lecture slides can get confusing, so be sure to attend class to see how she explains them.

Yes, she doesn't record her lectures. You're in college paying thousands for the class, feel like that should be a motivator to go to class. Her lectures aren't super exciting, but I learned more about statistics in her class than any stats class I've ever taken. I hated stats in high school, and this class made me feel like I'm actually good at it

Not the most challenging IND E class but very interesting with this professor. She is the most caring and effective teacher at UW I have encountered. Very respectful and tries her best to avoid dry lectures even when the material seems miserable. Overall, I would absolutely take a class with her again, by far my best prof. at UW.

I'm an ISE major so I have taken a lot of random classes that have nothing to do with my major, and I've had a lot of bad professors. Patty is the best. Exams will only ever have things that shes covered in lectures, never any curveballs. Her slides are simple and get to the point. If you miss class, catching up is very easy.

analysis.name: Rick Bonus
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took him for Critical Filipino American History. He was a great welcome to my first ever quarter at UW. His lectures are hilarious and its easy to understand when he talks about his own experience. Though, he provides a ton of reading and quizzes afterwards. The quizzes are slightly easy if you pay attention in class.

wonderful professor!! bonus was the first professor i connected with on campus and he truly cares about connecting with his students. that being said, his course was definitely unorganized and admittedly left leaning, as many other reviewers noted. still, he is a wonderful individual and i would love to spend more time learning from his teachings

Professor Bonus was very knowledgeable and always tried to make class interesting. One thing I'll say is be prepared to read A LOT. I should've expected this for a history class but I didn't realize how it'd be difficult sometimes with other classes and stuff. You should get a decent grade if you do the work on time.

Professor Bonus assignments are not dependent on the lecture. He provides all the information you need for quizzes (which consist of vocab words and general ideas we learn in class) and isn't a tough grader, just use your own ideas and words. He likes it when his class talks.

I love the content of the class. it is very interesting. but this teacher has ruined it for me and does not want to help you at all. he is very unorganized and the midterm was unbelievably hard. there are four books to read and around 7 very long articles. pop quizzes on the readings as well as weekly homework and two huge presentation projects.

analysis.name: Brad Cookson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My comments are more related to the course rather than a specific lecturer. There are a number of guest lecturers and they come up with their own questions. Really hard to grasp what each lecturer focuses on which makes studying harder. There is A LOT of contenT. There was one lecture that had almost 60 PowerPoint slides... A lot of memorization...

he's a great speaker, however, he only teaches one or two of the main lectures and leaves the rest up to the guest speakers. the guest speakers write their own questions on the tests and it becomes super confusing with all the different formats. hardest class I've taken at UW. don't believe him when he says you need no science background for this

If you want to do well in this class, just make sure you know the general concepts and also every single detail mentioned. Dr. Cookson is an alright professor, but my god, the structure of this class is ridiculous.  If you want a good grade, memorize everything (consistent active recall!!!), and if you want to keep your sanity, avoid this class.

Dr. Cookson is pretty funny and is a good lecturer. However, he only gives about 5 lectures out of the whole class. The rest of the class is given by guest speakers. The class itself is pretty difficult with a lot of material to cover. If you aren't good at memorization, you probably won't do well. Basic understanding of micro bio is a must.

The class works by two midterms and one final. Each midterm is about 22.5% of your grade, and the final is around 44%. Each lecture is taught by a different professor, which makes it difficult to study. This is just a pure memorization class. Avoid it if possible. If you do take it, make flashcards, go to class, DON'T FALL BEHIND!

analysis.name: Tod Bergstrom
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 174 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: On average over a chapter a night plus course pack (dry, random, newspaper articles) audio homework and lecture notes, which he does pop quizzes on. He referencestests a lot on American politics. There are technically 3 exams which incorporate things from business law so if you transferred in good luck. Oh and  a 20 page group paperpresentation.

Class is alright, too much information. There is no example of past tests and quizzes, that make students have a rough time studying. He also got this penalty rule with T/F questions which is kinda annoying. Personally, I just don't like how the class structure. If you are like me, taking 4 classes and working, please don't take this class.

Tod is a fun, passionate, and very smart professor who wants his students to succeed. His lectures were so engaging and memorable, which helped me stay very attentive, learn a lot, and do good on exams. I am also more interested in law now all thanks to Tod. My one regret is not participating as much in class, which I recommend everyone to do.

Tod is probably the best professor I'll ever have at this school. His lectures are engaging, he uses his real-world experience and excellent real-world examples to teach lessons, and he really cares about his students' learning. Very knowledgable about law and always fascinating to listen to. Always looked forward to this class. A+++

this is one of the worst classes i have taken at uw. because of this class, i have genuinely doubted my ability in school because he purposely makes his class so difficult for no reason. if you cant spend every waking moment studying for this class, then dont take it with him! you are not given any practice to bounce off of for tests, just lectures

analysis.name: Andrew Loveless
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 526 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Loveless was perhaps one of the best teachers I've had in all my years of schooling. His weekly emails with homework hints and supplemental readings showed how much he cared about his students' success. His amiable personality and dad-humor lightened the mood, while his lectures were very clear and never tangential. So much gratitude for Andy.
If you do a lot of practice tests before exam, it would help a lot
Awesome professor with absolutely tons of extra resources that he makes himself and makes freely available. Never met someone who was so passionate about math. People do well on his exams.
He gives so much extra help and is super caring. Tests are easy enough that people mostly lose points for sign errors and silly stuff, which makes the curve a bit vicious.

I think the only reason he doesn't have a 4.0 rating is because students who didn't put in effort were upset at their grade. AMAZING professor, the most genuinely kind professor you'll probably ever meet, and teaches very effectively(he makes concepts easy to learn/understand). He wants you to succeed and makes it very easy to do so.

analysis.name: Tyler Babbie
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took Eng198h which was the combo class with psych 101 my first quarter. He tells you exactly what you need to do in order to get a 4.0 gpa, and if you follow his advice and aren't afraid of speaking in class, you will get a 4.0. For the more shy people or those who aren't as receptive to his feedback as others the class may be tougher. Good guy.

This guy is honestly the most engaging professor I've had at UW. He's so young too. He feels like a grad student but knows more than most professors. He seriously compels you to care about the class because of how much you can tell he cares. He does so much and I hope everyone gets a chance to take his class at least once.

Dr. Babbie was undoubtedly excellent. He clearly wants all students to succeed. He is understanding and caring, especially when unexpected things happen to you, and you need an extension. I was not very excited about the course topic, but his "off-topic" rants were very (and far more) interesting. Getting a 4.0 should be easy as long as you try.

The class itself was great. He's super passionate about the projects that we make for the class. He's a light grader and doesn't have that many standards. We were given the topics of: Photos, Audio (like music or a podcast), and a video project. He gives great feedback and helps when you truly need it.

Dr. Babbie one of my favorite professors! Be aware of class discussions and weekly discussion posts as well as papers. also, 1:1 meeting to discuss what we are planning to write about (u wouldn't waste ur time on a wrong draft + know what we were asked for) and allow us to ask as much of questions (which not all professors do). no regrets the BEST.

analysis.name: Charity Urbanski
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 71 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She is a great lecturer, her slides basically cover everything but it is so worth it to go to class and get the extra bits of information she throws in. You can tell she genuinely cares about the topic and speaks on it like it is a personal interest. She is kind about extensions and always offers extra office hours around exams and big papers.

One of the most interesting classes I have ever taken. Lectures were 2 hours long but i walked out each day wishing they ran longer. It literally expanded my worldview. Urbanski was incredibly knowledgeable in her field and very insightful; her lectures were lots of fun to listen to. Readings were like 300 pages a week, but it was worth it.

Professor Urbanski is incredible! She is super knowledgeable and this class was an absolute delight. Lots of readings and there's a lot of memorization necessary, but you can prepare all your answers for midterms/finals before the actual test. Definitely show up for the lectures--attendance isn't mandatory but the lectures are phenomenal.

Honestly I had more of an issue with the TA than with Urbanski in this class. 3/9 assignments and the midterms graded by the time the finals were done— feedback was nonsense, correcting by rewording random stuff without really changing anything. 90% of the grade is split between two essays and two tests. Wonderful content, mildly painful lectures.

The course material is interesting and the readings are (usually) interesting as well. However, she has trouble keeping her lectures on time. By our midterm she was a full day behind in lecture. This is related to her tendency to go off on random tangents and take all questions.

analysis.name: Caley Cook
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I spent the last quarter on a UW study abroad program with Caley. Getting used to life in a foreign country was stressful enough and I felt very discouraged by her teaching style. Material was not conveyed very clearly and there was no room for mistakes. If you're looking for compassion or have a question, maybe wait until she is having a good day

She is nice and passionate about the topic. But it is a hard class with a lottt of work. You do have to show up to class, and she calls on people randomly. Also sooo much boring reading. I don't know when teachers are going to understand that students do not enjoy or retain knowledge by reading 50 pages of a textbook.

I also studied abroad with Caley. Unfortunately, Caley was the worst professor I have ever had the displeasure of working with. I have never been so disrespected nor would I ever recommend taking one of her classes. Steer clear.

Caley Cook is a highly-skilled journalist and one of the best professors I've had in the JPIC program. She taught me how to tell compelling stories through down to earth, simple language, and provided constant positive reinforcement in the feedback process. I would recommend her to any aspiring journalist who's looking to improve their craft.

She's one of the best professors I've had at UW. Her lectures are engaging and she's hilarious, i look forward to coming to class everyday. The chapter worksheets are helpful to learn from the text chapters without reading the whole thing. If you pay attention in class and do work you will do great in this class!

analysis.name: Daniel Chiu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 172 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Tests are super predictable. You get a sheet of notes for all tests. For the final I figured out what type of problems he'd put on there by looking the the suggested problems. Copied them onto my note sheet and they showed up on the final and I just had to copy it back down. Pulls from worksheets too. Super easy class, super predictable.

Alright, I bombed the first midterm (48/100 or something). Got below averages on all the tests, and somehow finished with a 2.9...that means you HAVE to do the lab reports well; go to Chem Study Center and collaborate with others and do the ALEKS. You should look at the slides before going to class always, and do all the odd book probs in each chpt

His lectures are very confusing and unclear. He somehow goes both too slow and too fast at the same time, and jumps around slides before you can finish reading them. His tests were fair in my opinion. The questions are free response word problems and don't test you on conceptual ideas/definitions, just practice problems. Not a great teacher overall

The tests are open note but borderline impossible. He glosses over major concepts and then shows an extremely hard math problem application of it and expects every one to understand. If no one gets it he makes a passive aggressive comment about how we need to figure it out and then moves on. He also makes the ALEKS due at 5pm which is just dumb.

ALEKS is a nightmare. Barely used textbook. Had to use YouTube to teach myself. Way too many slides and kind of just throws solved problems up expecting you to follow along. Monotone + hard to follow. Quiz sections spent talking about how bad he is. TAs are wonderful and actually care. Better time spent watching tutorials than going to lecture.

analysis.name: Christopher Hoffman
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took MATH 207 in Autumn 2024. Lectures weren't very engaging for me, and keeping pace required significant independent learning and textbook reading. I relied heavily on the 200-level Math Lab and meeting with TAs to clarify material and stay on track throughout the quarter.

The professor is like a machine, boring and uninspirational. During lectures students have to correct his mistakes too often. Homework is hard since he did not give us enough materials, the exam is even worse with most questions having little to do with what we have learned. Recordings had no sound and were blurry. You will NEED to self-study.

This is the most entertaining professor at the UW. This guy is hilarious to watch as he mumbles nonsense and fails to solve his own problems (he even has notes to look at). I laughed so hard in the middle of class. Hoffman's class is only for people who appreciate comedy. NOTE* you wont learn anything, but you'll get a good laugh.

I'm sure Christopher Hoffman is a wonderful man, but he cannot teach at all. He speaks in a very incoherent way which makes things difficult, but also just does not know the math he is teaching. He consistently gets problems wrong and doesn't fix his mistakes, instead saying "in the real world you will just use wolframalpha". Don't take him.

This man should not be teaching. He regularly gets example problems wrong, he is unclear  and seems to get lost in class. When he did get a question right he would do so with little to no explanation even declaring several times that he "wasn't going to go into detail about it".

analysis.name: Joe Concannon
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I loved this class. Joe is one of the best professors I've ever had. He cares a lot about how students are doing in the course. Made a lot of effort to have variation in assignments. Super thoughtful and cool guy too. He used almost all physical course materials, but we only had to pay for 3 things. Classes were heavy on (productive!) discussion.

He is a chill guy but very unorganized which made the class confusing. He never came to class with clear expectations for his students so ultimately I didn't learn much from this class. He also grades based on how much he agrees with you rather than how well you argued your claim.

The class focused on a few big writing projects and a portfolio at the end. Sometimes the instructions weren't very clear, but overall, the grading wasn't too harsh and not too much work was required - I mostly did assignments the day they were due. Was anything I learned fascinating? No, but it was a good way to get composition credit.
Really passionate guy but sometimes goes on tangents that don't relate to the topic of the class. Overall good class and he really cares.

Not UW, but Pierce College ENGL&102. He is a cool, fun guy, but he is not the best at teaching. Work is light, lectures are often just free time spent sitting doing nothing. I want to emphasize that grading criteria is HORRIBLE. Nearly nothing is taught and you wont earn anything other than an easy A. 70% of grade is a "portfolio" at end of quarter

analysis.name: Sarah Collier
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is very nice but the format of the course is just one big fast-paced overview that moves too fast to learn anything. This might be fine since there aren't many stakes (no quiz section and two exams worth 10% of your final grade) but the exams expect you to recall niche facts from the lecture slides that have nothing to do with anything.

Horrible class format. You cannot take any test w/o cheat sheet. Video lectures after video lectures. She knows her area very well, but does not understand her student's lives. I might spend 54 minutes viewing assigned videos, but that does not account for the time I spent taking notes, writing flashcards, etc. Group project was my worst nightmare.

If you are not required to take this class, DO NOT! Collier is the worst teacher I have ever experienced at UW. I have no problem being that straightforward because she does not care to teach the class in a meaningful way. She uses video lectures from seemingly years ago (lazy & uninspired), grades harshly, and writes exams that are disingenuous.

Way to in depth for an intro course. Tests often asked for very specific, nitpicky knowledge, and she didn't provide good review material. Went very fast in lectures. Take a different professor if the option is available, but class is fairly easy to pass because of low weight on tests.
Dr. Collier is kind and incredibly knowledgeable about soils, and the content is very doable if you've taken the gen chem series. Sometimes disorganized, but overall a good course.

analysis.name: Claire Willing
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Claire was a wonderful professor who was both passionate about the things she was teaching and her students' understanding of course content. I deeply appreciated her constant challenging of our knowledge to help solidify the information we were learning. Great course. It was tough at times, but I would absolutely take a class of hers again.

Very caring and attentive to students needs! Cares about students' success and is very receptive to feedback; implements changes based on the feedback she receives. Is very enthusiastic and sincere. Take fungal ecology with her if you have the chance! It's an amazing class
Lectures fast but is extremely personable and knowledgeable.

analysis.name: Colleen Craig
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 342 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Honestly I don't understand why people like her so much. Dr. Craig is the definition of a teacher in a weed out class. Don't get me wrong she is a good lecturer but her exams are hard and super tricky. If you make one mistake that answer will appear on the exam as they are multiple choice. Be ready to put a ton of work into this class. I hate her

Although her lectures were okay, her tests are horribly hard. One could do well above average on lab reports, quizzes, and ALEKS but have a barely average grade because of exams. She provides practice material that is very unprepatory, because her exams end up being 10x harder. Her TAs are horrid too. I will never take a class with her again.
Makes her test as hard as possible. Gives exam reviews that are so much easier than the actual test. Would never take her again.
If you aren't medicated before taking this class, call your psychiatrist ASAP. Even God can't guide you through this class.

Dr. Craig is a great professor. She's the type of professor that if you have to move your schedule around a bit to get her, it's worth the hassle. 152 is definitely tough, but her lectures reinforce the textbook well, she gives ample study materials for the exams, and you can tell she really cares about the students. Plus, she's pretty funny.

analysis.name: Deborah Kamen
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Kamen outlines the class well and makes expectations clear. Graded on two tests (closed book) and weekly quizzes (open book). She records all lectures online so attendance is not required. A good amount of readings but she explains them all well in lecture. She is a great professor and very knowledgeable.

Amazing professor, clearly cares a lot about what she's teaching. She does talk very fast and you have to take a lot of notes. Attendance not mandatory, but if you skip you have to watch the recording to keep up. There is a textbook but you can easily get by without reading it, she covers everything in lecture.

Professor Kamen is one of my favorite professors. She's very knowledgable in Classical Greek and truly cares about her students and making sure we understand the material and do well. She's a pretty easy grader when it comes to exams as she wants to give as many points as she can. If you can, please take one of her classes!

Prof. Kamen is awesome. Class with her was a highlight of this quarter. Great organization, consistent communication, clear grading policy, and a very fair test and exam policy. As long as you attend/watch the lectures, follow the study guides and put in a moderate amount of work, you'll be able to do really well. One of the best at UW, for sure.

Prof. Kamen is a wonderful lecturer. She clearly knows what she is talking about. This class specifically covered a lot of material but Kamen did well in communicating the important things about the ancient societies at hand. Only quizzes and two exams went into the grade book, but you get the questions ahead of time.

analysis.name: Sharon Doty
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Does not have clear grading criteria and is difficult to communicate with. Insisted that I missed a lecture even though I provided evidence that I attended, which led to her not giving me credit for the class (I had an 80%) because I 'missed too many lectures' (which was not a grading parameter stated in the syllabus).

The lecture attendance wasn't required, but lab/field trips were. Show up to field trips (wasn't stated in syllabus) because you will get a 0, even when doing the required work from the field trip. Wasn't helpful when emailing and low key rude. Great and interesting class, but not great prof.

Amazing professor, very knowledgeable and entertaining. You'll learn a lot, especially about her areas of interest! Grading is a little nitpicky, and it's hard to tell why points were shaved off. Heavily weighted tests, extra credit helps. She clicks her tongue a lot, so be mindful if you have sensory issues.

Doty really cares about her students and the she's super into the content. It's much more in depth material than the other 201 profs, so it's harder to get a good grade. lab reports and 2 exams are graded harshly. Class is disorganized and they mark you off for things that you didn't know you were getting graded on.

I took the PNW Ecosystems class with her and Hinkley and had a great experience overall. She does talk quietly, so it is hard to stay awake, but the concepts taught are not all that difficult. Pros: no book, field trips, and an easy grade. Cons: you'll need coffee before class and she writes LONG, but easy, tests (one was ~3 hours)

analysis.name: Daniel Grossman
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: It could sometimes be hard to be motivated to go to seminar especially towards the end of the quarter, but I think Dan did a great job making every meeting worth going to. He is a well-organized and very caring guy.

Incredible teacher. Probably the best lecturer I've ever had. He really has good analogies and goes over things with a reasonable pace, but at the same time has the knowledge and experience from being a researcher to give answers to really complex questions. Tests are hard but in an intellectually stimulating way, as they require creative thinking

Dan is a great professor, respected and has been at UW for over 20+ years. If you get the opportunity to take his class, TA for him, anything, just take it. He has a wealth of knowledge, resources, and is one of the premier faculty at UW. He is such an amazing professor; if you have the opportunity to take a class with him, do not hesitate.

Prof. Grossman was fine, but the class itself was incredibly boring. Personally, I wish I hadn't taken the class, but I understand it could be helpful for others. He did a great job making sure the workload for this class was light and tried to diversify the material. However, I feel like the class could be 50 min instead of 80 min.
Amazing class. I think it the Programming Languages class at coursera should be required for every engineer that wants to improve a lot his programming skills

analysis.name: Anne Duncan
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: My advice would be to write poems with strange layouts, nonsensical prose, and no capitalization. She doesn't like much else. Duncan's feedback is difficult to get through, and there's a large amount of books for the class (not at the school bookstore) of which very little is discussed. Duncan's fine for the credit, but won't help you improve.

I took Engl 111, the material was interesting and thoughtfully chosen, and I enjoyed the assigned readings. I think she's a very engaging teacher; the two hours flew by. Her feedback is very clear and helpful, and if you need clarification, she's very willing to help! Great Professor.

I wasn't wild about Anne and her teaching style. While this was a workshop driven class, I felt there could have been more information shared via lectures. Poetry is also just a very subjective thing, so sometimes it was hard to understand her feedback. You wrote 8ish poems, workshopped 3, and had to submit a portfolio of 5 (I believe).

Anne seems really passionate about her and does a decent job discussing the material of the class. I would recommend taking other professors for this class as her readings can be a lot longer and tedious than other professors and her grading can also be tougher.

analysis.name: Chris Laws
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 141 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Chris is the best professor I've ever met in UW. His passion to teaching made me love this English course, which should have been boring and tedious. He said this is only a class, I want to see how hard you push yourself to do "experiments" on your paper.  If you really like this course and make efforts, you won't get a disappointing grade!

He's a great person who genuinely cares about his students. However, he is a very tough grader. I've had my fair share of essays, and he is extremely picky about how you explain the topic at hand. He makes you work for your grade. But I feel like I've learned lots of helpful writing tips from him.  Overall, this is NOT an easy 4.0 class
You didn't have to take the midterm or final if you were happy with your quiz grades. He remembers all his students names even after the class ends. Favorite prof at UW.

i took astro to get my QSR credits over with... i am SO not a STEM person and wasn't remotely interested in astronomy. laws and his truly awesome TAs made me not hate the class. lectures were funny and engaging because laws is genuinely passionate about astronomy and it's kind of contagious. shows a good professor makes all the difference.

Professor Laws is genuinely kind, thoughtful, intelligent, and engaging. My only big issue is that essentially all your grade is left up to the midterms and final, so if you're a bad test taker (like me), then your grade might be lower than in other classes because there are few ways to make up for scores with homework or other assignments.

analysis.name: Dustin Maly
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 95 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I read the reviews prior to taking this class, and had high expectations for Maly, but now, 5 weeks into the quarter, I thought I should warn other people the way I wish I would have been. He throws material at you and basically leaves it up to you to teach it to yourself & rarely does example problems and basically leaves you in the dust for tests

Professor Maly understands the course material and the exams reflect his lectures well. His practice exams are basically his old exams, which work very well for you to prepare for the midterms and final. Homework was very easy to complete so much of your grade is dependent on your exam performance. There is a drop system to help your grade too.

Barely goes into detail on material and provides hardly any practice problems for you. Tests are extraordinarily hard and there's nearly no grading criteria for them and the TAs grade the exams, so how many points you are awarded is up to them. You can get most of the question right and they will still take off 2/3 points for one mistake.

Going to be honest - I never went to lecture or quiz section after the first day and still passed with a 4.0. Maly gives so much practice questions similar to his exams that if you do those question + extra practice on your own, you will do well. His lectures are messy, and I found them never useful. Just pick up a textbook and practice lots!

Really good at teaching the mechs/rxns for the class--basically half the class, as after the 1st midterm it's almost all rxns. He loves his resonance, but it's super important for the rxns. Rough when it comes to material not about rxn mech tho. Beware of his super hard tests, do the practice tests, didn't read the textbook and it was alright tho.

analysis.name: David Hertzog
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I respect the guy hes cool and all but my god I've learnt absolutely nothing from him. Every lecture is just nonsensical and no help. I feel like everything is easy to understand until he teaches it. I don't understand the good ratings. I think a decade away from teaching has really messed him up. clearly a smart guy and passionate. Just not good

He is very passionate and funny but seems disconnected from the course, creating exams that were increasingly more difficult than practice material. You will have to spend a lot of time outside of class working on this course. His lectures felt rushed, crammed, and all over the place. While he has a fun personality, he is not good as a teacher.

Hertzog does an adequate job lecturing given how messy the 121 curriculum is. He's clearly an experienced lecturer, and does lots of fun demos. He does seem somewhat disconnected with the curriculum, especially the labs and tutorials. He writes difficult tests, and I've found the in class work isn't enough to prepare for the exams.

Lots of demos and interesting topics, but lectures felt disconnected from labs and tutorials. I had to teach myself much of the material. TAs often couldn't answer questions. Exams were harder than expected with unclear expectations on what would be tested. Overall mostly read off of slides and barely elaborated

He's very friendly and his lectures are entertaining. He seems to be more helpful one-on-one so definitely approach him or go to office hours if you need help. Other than that, his lectures lack coherence and he doesn't always know what he's doing. For tests, expect a good amount of trick questions. He's just OK.

analysis.name: Dana Dabiri
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is hard but good, & is interested in making sure you're learning. He keeps us engaged in the class by having us turn to our neighbor & discuss what we are learning.  The weekly quizzes keep us from falling behind.  The 1st midterm was hard, but the 2nd was easier. If you take this class, be ready to put good time into it, but you'll learn a lot.

EXTREMELY slow grader. Most take over 1 month from due date to be graded. If students have deadlines for assignments, someone's gotta give this man grading deadlines. No way to tell how you're doing, and no feedback provided on quizzes and homeworks. Lectures are just repeating the textbook (which is very good btw), which adds nothing.

Nice guy, TA's are pretty bad. Assgts take weeks for grading/feedback/solutions. 

Lectures straight from the powerpoint. In-person attendance dwindles from 50 people down to a syconphantic dozen that make the last couple of weeks like pulling teeth.

HW weighted as 65% of grade, 1 final takes up the last 35%, expect a C worst case scenario.

Dabiri, while being a kind person, is not a great professor. All class material is screenshots directly from the textbook and all lectures are reading textbook slides and being told to "discuss with your neighbor". Often late to class, missing materials, and late on grading.

This is a tough class, and you have to be ready to participate to do well.  I had to put up with a lot of whiner classmates, and eventually worked on my own because I didn't want to put up with others who blamed the professor for their own failures.

analysis.name: Fanny Dos Reis
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 94 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Now I finally understand why her class always have open spots, DON'T take her class, her lecture is useless and she does not care if you understand the content or not, and she is super lazy, you don't get your midterms back until the end of the quarter and she doesn't even give you the answer for the midterm. She also doesn't showup to office hour.

Professor Dos Reis is really good. As a student who has always been mid/a bit above average UW classes, I think that once you get used to her accent she's awesome. Her lectures are SO reflective of what is on the exams and the material she reviews in review sessions are actually the same material she tests on. Don't be scared by the other reviews

Prof. Dos Reis' lectures somewhat follow the structure of the textbook, but in-class proofs are often different than the text. She does not spoon-feed proofs and instead has the class work together to solve a problem. Homework is difficult but there are not many assignments. Her accent is not hard to understand.
Worst instructor ever. Only few students really listen and understand. Lots of mistakes on the notes.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Her lectures were messy and all over the place, very unorganized, and her handwriting was extremely difficult to read. She's a great person and she's very nice and flexible with accommodations when needed, but she was still a horrible teacher.

analysis.name: Elinore Theobald
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 164 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Elli's lectures were the best part of Biol 180! She really made an effort to enhance student understanding and never hesitated to answer a question. She was really accessible and was so kind inside of class and out. She made the course enjoyable, despite it being difficult, and her lectures/office hours really contributed to my learning.

Not only a fantastic teacher, but she also really makes an effort to get to know you as an individual in a giant lecture section. Super accessible outside of class, and always willing to talk science with anyone interested.

Her lecture is so focused on the interactivity and barely explain well on the exact topics. It makes me only care about will the random call happens on me instead of learning the knowledge. She even handed out the worksheet in a 600 people lecture and only give us about 10 min to do it. She should manage time better rather than doing interactivity.

I went into this prepared to work hard, but all the work you put in doesn't matter. what matters is your ability to answer random data questions tangentially related to content. Only ridiculously specific answers get credit, so your grade is up to TA kindness. she doesn't provide actual content in lecture, she uses unreliable student responses.

Theobald organized the course in a way that it was very confusing as to what knowledge would be required for quizzes. This also made it challenging to do well because they were wanting ultra specific answers on the quiz yet in class they would accept anything as a good answer. The content itself is quite mundane and I would not take again.

analysis.name: Eric Reel
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Exercises are manageable, and projects can be easy or time-consuming. Exams are difficult, and he gives little guidance on what to expect. Rubrics are vague, and asking questions usually gets “do what's reasonable.” Overall, if you're comfortable teaching yourself, you'll probably do fine, but if you rely on guidance, this class can be frustrating.

Great and funny guy. Exams are based on implementation rather than theory. His lectures are kind of confusing, so just focus on learning how to code what he talks about. Exercises build up to what you'll do in projects. About 2~3 exercises/projects a week. Very open and good at answering questions. One project late pass. Expect to learn on your own

I took CSS342 and CSS343 with Professor Reel and passed. He uses LeetCode for practice and assigns fun coding projects. The class is more exercise/project-heavy than lecture-heavy, which I enjoyed. Use his office hours and ask questions! He truly cares and even checks if exams were too hard, sometimes allowing flexibility in projects and pacing.

Reel is a great professor, but his teaching style is not super easy. Im rating him for 343 but I also took his 342 and it was the same deal. His exams and projects are based off Pisan's class but I believe his teaching style is better, especially when I cared about the class. For the most part if you focus on class youll learn enough to 3.5+

His a really great professor. Exams are implementation based but not genuinely devious. The lectures really helped in getting the theory bit of the implementation. He actually aims ensuring you are successful in the course. Would surely take him again!

analysis.name: Elena Pezzoli
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 182 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Really bad professor. She just stands there and points at things with her laser pointer. Math should be done in front of class, as you're explaining. Nope... Just stands there with a Word doc full of calculations that have been prepared beforehand, and just talks, and talks, and talks. Should not be teaching at all. Relied on my TA for EVERYTHING.

This course was unnecessarily difficult for the material it covered, I had taken pre-calc twice before this, and still found myself confused by the lectures. She is nice, lectures are recorded, and extra credit is given out, but at the core of it I feel I wasted my money taking this course, and would've saved myself time by just jumping to calc.

Elena had good lectures. One problem I had with the class was how test heavy it is. The two midterms are relativley easy but are a large portion of your grade, and the final WILL kill you (super difficult). Overall decent prof who will explain math better than highschool teachers, but either way its a very hard course. My TA was a useless nonce btw

She is very nice, but the class is can be difficult to follow as you are often working on a different chapter in the lecture, quiz section, and on the homework. Would highly recommend going to all quiz sections and office hours. Not impossible to succeed, but it can be grueling. Her lectures are fast-paced and sometimes hard to follow.

This professor seems like a wonderful lady, but her course was very difficult. I took Math 120 (pre-calc) with her, and the lectures were incredibly hard to understand. The material covered in lecture and in the textbook are extremely difficult to apply to web assign, midterms, and the final.

analysis.name: Serena Eley
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures will put you to sleep, you will doze out. Take it with Tai Chen instead for a more engaging experience; that is what I should've done. Sign up for the ECE Group Tutoring as the group tutoring sessions will serve as your recitation session and clarify every important concept you missed from lecture. Otherwise, it is use your favorite LLM.

She seemed uninterested throughout the quarter. Though the material of the class itself is pretty boring. Labs were long and tedious. I still don't know what a semiconductor is, but I'm guessing it's important. Bring some coffee and sit in the front or bring a blanket and sit in the back. Either way your grade will turn out the same.

Boring lecture, just read slides for most of the time. To many informations each lecture that make people very easy to get distracted. She don't even provide practice questions for quiz, so you have no idea what the quiz will be like and just have to prepare all the complicated and lengthy knowledge points she has covered.

analysis.name: Warren Etheredge
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This man has run through the film gambit and come up short and is grasping for relevance. Claims he has connections in-the industry-then brings in students he knows from other classes. Maybe an old drinking buddy who pities him, or, worst one, the parent of a student. Has no clear classroom structure and not a single syllabus.

If you care about film and screenwriting and you aren't super sensitive you'll love this class. The guy sort of picks favorites, I was one of them, and I didn't really do anything special besides try and if you do that I believe you'll take one of your favorite classes you'll ever take.

Holds his power in the media industry over his students. Made an environment that played favorites and put down students who weren't his favorites. He made a comment to a student that was a "joke" and it caused that student to leave class and never come back. Also urged his students to share their trauma just becasue he shared his.
Had a good time but he does grade based on "vibes." And he even admitted to that on the first day of class so if you care too much about your GPA this isn't for you.

fantastic professor, absolutely one to take, I cannot recommend him more. class is really reliant on attendance (it's not required but you Should Go), but you'll have a great time. he pushes you to be creative on your own and in a group; everything is incredibly collaborative. you'll come out of the class with friends, I guarantee it.

analysis.name: Erica Ingalls
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Was not confident about what she was teaching. Does not engage students or have them engage with each other. Lectures are confusing and clearly based directly off the textbook, does not provide examples that are not already listed in the textbook (doesn't seem to understand the material very well). Not open to feedback. No one in class is engaged.

It often feels like she doesn't fully understand the material before teaching. She frequently makes mistakes on worksheets without realizing, which is misleading. I don't understand why we have to write so much in a chemistry class, drawing structures is fine, but she has us writing nonstop, which makes it hard to focus on the actual content.

She was extremely unorganized, every lecture had 40+ handwritten slides with scribbles and arrows that made it hard to follow. She mostly reads directly from the textbook with no additional explanation, and the lecture feels redundant. Always asking if we prefer 220 or 221, I would 100% choose 220. This was the worse course in this equence.

She's very kind, but her teaching style is extremely hard to follow. The lectures are disorganized, and she handwrites everything on the slides, which makes it hard to focus what she talked in lectures. Her handwriting is also difficult to read. You're basically left to teach yourself. If you need structure, this class will be frustrating.

Literally never take her class she just writes and writes and expects u to know what shes talking about. Throughout the lectures its only the same 2 grown people who would answer her questions and people keep not showing up to her lecture bc she doesnt really teach. 0/5

analysis.name: Elise Novitski
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: You can tell that she knows a lot about the course content and she is very passionate about her subject. She is very enthusiastic about wanting to help her students, and there is a lot of support if you find the content difficult. However, she mostly just reads off the slides in lecture, and you will find that you learn a lot more outside of class.

I found Prof Novitski to be a great lecturer and very passionate about ensuring students understand content. Good demonstrations and examples in class to help with understanding concepts. Definitely recommend attending lectures and doing work outside of class as it helps your grade very much. Tests are difficult but study hard and you can do well.

I think Novitski was one of the best professors I've had so far. She's super knowledgable about physics and is a really good lecturer, I'm not really good at physics but she makes it super easy to understand. Just watch out for the tests as they are really difficult and the MCQ portion has questions that are similar to FRQs.

While she was nice and clearly passionate about the subject, during lecture I found that she read off the slides a lot--oftentimes I felt like I learned a lot more from the TAs during quiz and lab sections.

Highly underrated professor- most of the complaints against her have more to do with how college courses are run and less with her teaching. Her lectures were super nutritional and the course materials were highly organized and helpful. She was extremely open and receptive to feedback and used to tailor lectures. Don't be afraid to take her course!

analysis.name: Fahad Khalil
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Professor is fundamentally a great person and treats his students with respect. That is the first step in being a good mentor.

His teaching is entertaining, logical and oriented around economic frameworks. Game Theory is a hard concept, and he does a great job in connecting abstractions. 

His tests are hard, the class is hard, but he is good.

I was worried because of his rating at first, but he's a good lecturer who knows his stuff and is very willing to help you wherever you are in your learning. I enjoyed his class a lot, he gives memorable examples for games and makes an effort to know all of his students. Also, he is a fast responder to emails now!
No idea who is giving this guy 5.0 stars. The prof doesnt know how to COMMUNICATE.
Only tests. He doesnt respond to emails. Textbook bad prof.
He makes an effort.... thats it. Dont take.

analysis.name: Elba Garza
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The curve is crazy high this 25wi quarter. How can 2 S and 31 E in 33 letter grades be 3.8 and 1 S 32 E be 3.9? You should be perfect in all homework with your resubmission and only get at most 2 Ns to be dropped in 15 exam determined grades in order to get 4.0. lol

Elba is energetic and kind, she provides good examples for concepts covered in class and is very open to further discussion outside of class. She and the TAs are understanding of external issues that cause a need to miss a quiz, and they overall want you to succeed. If you put in the time to study and use the resources provided, you'll get a 4.0.

Elba really cares about her students, she takes the time to come up with good examples for each lecture and makes each lecture engaging and interesting. The practice resources online are incredibly helpful for quizzes and homework, and the prof/ta's are easy to reach if you have any questions about the homework. Great class, would take again.

Underrated. Elba's a delightful lecturer that's got everything you'd want from a 351 professor - knowledge, industry experience, communication skills, and humor. She's quick though, so make sure to take out time for pre-lecture readings; otherwise, you'll be lost all lecture.

Elba is an incredible professor, it's clear she puts a lot of effort and time into her lectures, and the TA team is amazing as well! The grading is sometimes quite strict, but to account for that they have a resubmission process that allows you to make changes to your assignments for full credit. It was an amazing class overall, I would take again.

analysis.name: Natalie Frank
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: What a joke of a class.  The class is extremely disorganized and too fast paced to learn anything. Literally left to learn everything on my own for the assignments, which are not even in sync with the topics being covered in classroom. I was really looking forward to this class as the topics looked cool but it has been a major disappointment

Assumed that we knew differential equation, and logical notation, even though this course only requires calculus to take, assigns a homework assignment after the final, but has topics from that assignment on the final exam. The biggest issue were the lectures, too slow and messy, and would only teach proofs and properties, not the steps to solve it

Dr. Frank is nice and cares about the subject. Unfortunately, she is not a good professor. Her lectures are poorly paced, neither her or the TAs are accessible outside of class, and the final contains true/false questions where it is possible to get -1 points. The entire class is frustrated and confused, the study guide is sparse and curve unknown.

The worst teacher ever. Can't even be called a teacher cuz she didn't teach us anything. Her only effort was to write irrelevant stuff with messy handwriting in class and give "notes" like draft papers. Piazza questions never received accurate responses. Test ur ability to self-learn. Everyone was completely disappointed. Just don't take her class

It is so tough to follow the lectures and then apply that into the homework which is like 70% of the grade. The structure of the course was also really bad and honestly even though she genuinely tried teaching the concepts there was no enthusiasm so I never really learnt anything from the class, I just had to study everything on my own.

not happy.

analysis.name: Oliver Fraser
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 104 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Fraser was an enthusiastic person with a lot of passion for astronomy. However, his unclear lectures, lack of organization, clarity, and no study guides really made this class much harder than it needed to be. His exams asked very vague, unclear and weird questions... the content is much easier if you just watch crash course videos online.

Beware. Dr O is very nice, friendly,  funny, but lectures are confusing and unclear, forcing you to spend extra time self-studying the material (and still feel lost and frustrated). He tries to oversimplify concepts which just makes them even more unclear. He also doesn't give study guides & exams are tricky. NW credit? Better off taking ASTRO150.

Dr. Fraser has a great personality, but I found the lectures to be disorganized  and unclear. He does most of his teaching orally, so it is difficult to go back and look at the lecture slides and understand. Also, the tests are very hard to prepare for because he does not give any practice tests. However, he is friendly and inspirational.

Dr. O's class was one of the best I've ever taken. He is an amazing lecturer, the material is engaging and fun to learn.  There is a clear grading system, which is very generous. There are three exams, but your lowest one is dropped. I could not recommend this course more, it legitimately made me consider switching majors to astronomy.

Awesome class/professor. Lectures were recorded, but I attended anyways. Course is more wide than deep, but when I'd go to office hours with questions, he was great at explaining content beyond the course's scope. Tests were pretty one-to-one with lectures. Review your notes and you'll be fine. There's an online textbook, but he doesn't use it all.

analysis.name: Rashenna Fountain
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This was the most frustrating class I've taken at UW. from to disorganized materials, unclear expectations with few rubrics, inconsistent grading, and her lack of response to any emails, though she is kind in person and willing to help if you meet with her directly.

Professor Fountain is an exceptional teacher who goes very in-depth about the cultural disparities in America. Her assignments gave unique insights to my learning and were very helpful. I personally loved this class a lot and it taught me many important skills. Very kind person!
I liked Professor Fountain's class a lot, it was insightful and I learned about a lot of new topics. It was not fully focused on natural sciences as the class said, but it was still very fun!

I took (ENGL 199) in the fall quarter.Rashenna Fountain was a very nice professor. There were 4 short assignments and 2 Major projects throughout the course and they were all very fun and creative. She also basically will give you 100 percent if you submit the short assignments and she is a very generous grader for the Major projects. Great teacher

analysis.name: Kathie Friedman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's a great professor. Her selection of readings will give you a well-rounded understanding of contemporary migration issues. Admittedly it is a lot of reading if you do all of them, but if you're a quick reader it'll be ok. She likes to have group discussions in class so you'll get to know your classmates better than in a regular lecture.

My favorite professor ever. While this class was quite reading dense, they are all interesting to some level, and she fits in a few documentaries that were really fun to watch. Going to lectures is a must, not only because it will benefit you in exams, but because she cares a lot about what she teaches and class time is quite fun.

I adore Professor Friedman!! Her class content was organized, interesting, and important. The books she required were well written and fun to read. Her exams were take home.
