She is also so kind, knowledgeable, and willing to help! She provides you with outside opportunities if you put in the effort. One of my favorite professors for sure!

Friedman is wonderful. She knows her stuff about the history if Jewish women and is so open to her students' ideas and opinions. It is clear she enjoys teaching and cares about her students. I recommend taking a class with her!
Her class was wonderful to take and she made learning enjoyable. The readings were always helpful, she never gave busy work, and she was always very clear on what she expected out of the class.

analysis.name: Frances Maloy
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 179 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Maloy is the most condescending and rude professor I've at UW. She makes you feel stupid for simply asking a question and constantly critiques our generation. Teaching seems a chore for her and honestly I'm not sure why she's here. She makes the material seem impossible when most of it is common sense, but she does give pop quizzes and has no mercy

Nice person, but is so unorganized. Was still teaching new material on Thursday (a whole other chapter and a half) when exam was on Saturday, all bc she was running behind + in the same week gave a useless group project due day before the exam given Monday. We had no dead week to study. And those TA's grade quizzes like u ran over their dog.

Basically micro, but 2 extra chapters. The first midterm is very easy, with a high mean sitting at around 86% for my section. We received some form of quiz/testing almost every week leading up to the final. No cheat sheets at all. Always talks about how hard her final is, gets old really quickly. Loves to talk over and cut off student questions.

Maloy is a hilarious teacher, I loved her personal and historic connections to work we were learning in the class. She cares to teach students and encourages student to keep trying. She gives a reasonable amount of work. This class is very similar to some topics from ECON 200 and there is some calculus, definitely a lot easier than ECON 200.

Hilarious teacher, I never snooze in her class. She comes in with the same iconic fit every single class. The readings were sometimes long, but she encourages students to ask questions and she does a lot of practice problems in class. Only thing I didn't like were her problem sets but it was very manageable.

analysis.name: Kendall Gray
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed this lab! Hell guide u to find answers urselfneeded to ace his lab. Important:1)Understand why need to do each step+result if miss/mess it up! 2)Use key terms on tests & reports! 3)CLEAN microscope lens x7 even lens wipe look clean! 4)Study each lab test+dilution problem daily! 5)Terms mentioned in lecture will be tested! 6)Ask+confirm!

Amazing professor, but challenging. Not only did you have to memorize the lab manual, but you had to take the time to both understand the experiment and bridge connections with other experiments (this is the key for quizzesexams). Do well on the firstsecond lab report as the fourth one is impossible. Also try to master dilution problems. GLHF!

Good lecturer. Clear in explanations. But beware! He is known to be one of the toughest professors in the Microbiology Dept. with EXTREMELY difficult exams!  If it is NOT REQUIRED, I STRONGLY suggest you don't this class! It will SEVERELY impact your GPA. Nothing against Kendall but the meticulous grading and near impossible exams are a real pain!!

Amazing lecturer, EVIL tests. Sometimes it feels like he puts the things you didn't study for on purpose. You will feel like you have the worst luck and that you might be genuinely a failure after his exams, but he is overall very good at explaining things and you will get a lot out of his lectures and talking to him outside of class.

One of the best professors at UW. His style of teaching is very clear, organized, and concise. Although, he isn't the main professor (only teaches lab) he keeps up with all the lectures and has no problem re-explaining concepts. You can completely trust his explanations, he is humble genius.

analysis.name: Giovanni Inchiostro
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Offers clear and thorough explanations to concepts in class, pauses after each question to answer lingering questions and ensure that everyone is on the same page. However, workload is heavy, and is incredibly strict and stingy on extensions. Concepts explored in class also doesn't suffice to succeed in exams, need to put in extra work to do well.

Decent prof, nothing exceptional. He's genuinely a nice guy and makes himself available for questions after each lecture. He only had one office hour sesh on monday which was kinda annoying- but he was quite prompt at answering emails about math questions or logistics. DEFINITELY take in person. Not the easiest course but doable if you're proactive

For his first quarter teaching, he wasn't too bad. I will say that he expects you to know a decent amount of algebra in his lectures, especially when it comes to simplification or general algebraic manipulation, and that he sometimes doesn't finish his lectures in time. He is very kind though and can give great feedback and help during office hours

His lectures, at least online, were nowhere near sufficient for the exams. He taught the most basic versions of the concepts and with the difficulty of the homework ramping up dramatically with only two days to do each one, so unless you hate sleep or free time be prepared to never put the textbook down if you want to do well. He means well though.

His lectures are very helpful, and he is always willing to help after class or during office hours. He frequently works problems on the board and walks through them step by step, often engaging directly with the class if students don't understand or need help. There is a lot of homework, but as long as you manage your time, you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Weili Ge
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Weili is the best! Her passion just makes you love accounting if you havent done so. Her class is very well organized and interesting. She really knows how to encourage and engage everybody into discussions. All the cases are so fun to work on although it can be challenging sometimes. I really learned A LOT from her class and from her.

Weili is my favorite accounting professor I've had so far. Her lectures are super good at incorporating real world events, class discussions, and making sure people have a chance to share their opinions and understand content. She is super receptive to feedback and I'd happily take another class with her.

Weili is the best accounting professor I've ever had! She ensures students have everything needed to succeed. Her 301 class was incredible! She makes accounting genuinely interesting and engaging. I gained so much knowledge, and her teaching style kept me captivated throughout. I highly recommend taking her classes!

One of the best lecturers I've had so far. Her classes are extremely engaging, and she uses well-known cases to help you understand class content. You can get through the class without the textbook, her lectures are enough to help you succeed!

Weili is the best accounting professor you can ever find! TAKE HER CLASS! She organizes this class very well: all the materials you need and assignments are clearly listed on canvas. Get ready to do many group projects, but they are really fun and inspirational. She shows us that accounting can be interesting and she is really nice and accessible.

analysis.name: Michael Gelb

Gelb is the type of teacher that everyone dreads. He may be smart at research and world applications of chemistry, but he should not be a lecturer. His lectures were unorganized and rambling. Not a single lecture passed without him going off on a student for asking "something you should have known. This is so easy for me." Would not recommend.

1. none of the stuff we learned was on the midterms.
2. he doesn't have lecture slides, he scribbles on his ipad
3. he talks about his time in jail SO MUCH, he thinks hes proud of that
4. doesn't wear shoes
5. doesn't show up during tests
6. doesn't provide his own practice midterms
7. class average 30%
8. all the 5.0 ratings are false
please like

If you see him outside of class he can be very helpful, but it's hard to learn in lecture. He also makes a lot of jokes and picks on students, which I also think is hilarious, but YMMV. Oh there's no homework!

Very disorganized lectures. No slides or practice exams & not accessible outside of class. Class average for a midterm was 37%. Exams weigh a lot and z-score depends on how well you do vs the average. Could have done more on my end, but also had to rely heavily on other teachers' practice tests, tutoring, and videos online. Would avoid if possible

analysis.name: Lawrence Goldman

Yeah bc I have time for that sir? You spend 7 hours in lecture/lab and then like 300 hours outside of lab. Worst time of my life

Larry is the man. He cracks bad (good) puns and makes his lectures thoroughly enjoyable. Group worksheets (not graded) are atrociously difficult, but group quizzes are fair and help immensely. TAKE THIS CLASS

DO NOT TAKE GOLDMAN! With the current grading system we have, all of our tests are out of 5. If you get a question >67% correct, you get the point. If less than 67, you don't. You can get a 65% on the test and receive a 0/5. Uses some weird token system to redeem points. Do not take him. Too complicated, unprofessional, and stressful.

33 points total on all exams combined. Miss more than 2 points, you lose your 4.0. U do get 4 tokens total to redo questions. He has an all or nothing grading where if you get 4 out of 6 parts of a question correct, you get 0 points on it. Keep in mind each test is 7 points (final is 12). If you ace tests, take this class. If not, take Forrest.

Terrible Professor, he is lazy, slides are directly from the book.  He adds nothing to the class you are better off not going to lecture.  Does not care about student learning.  Interrupts exams to ask if people are there.  The safety quizzes are bull, and SDS pages are crap.  Wish there was another option when I came to ochem labs.

analysis.name: Anthony Gill
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Gill gave a top-notch class, always with a new surprise around the corner. Lots of reading, but the books are pretty good, particularly Leeson's "The Invisible Hook". Prof. Gill makes you work hard, but it's 100% worth it.

A libertarian, and makes it clear via course material. He is pompous and rude, as others have stated. 
I was on good terms with him and received an A in the class, but that does not blind me to the fact that he openly embarrassed students like during the final, where he scolded someone for cheating on the essay loud enough so that we all heard.

Condescending boomer who somehow manages to make simple concepts difficult to understand and doesn't seem to care much about the success of his students. Essentially told everyone that our votes “don't matter” without providing much nuance at all during election season. You would be best served taking other Poli Sci courses.

I had him for the EFS class, and he was great.  Its a lot of reading but the tests are straighforward- there are no surprises.  Not an easy class, but I wouldn't call it hard.  He's nice, funny, and understanding.  He is so interested in what he teaches and that makes him a great prof.  Just get ready to read, but his class is interesting.

Funny professor with quite interesting lectures. Unfortunately the amount of books he requires in this class is just not reasonable at all. Not for everyone.

analysis.name: Stephen Groening

Just be aware that the class may be very different from what you expect, it's more of a commentary on society and technology than a study of film.

Very cool dude, his lectures are very interactive and directly correlate with the work we have to turn in. He is very flexible with grading due to the extra credit assignments. No complaints here, definitely recommend taking his class.

Steve is kind of a firecracker, really knowledgable, will change the way you think about media. Appreciated the amount of time dedicated to feminist theory. Great variety of viewings. Class discussions are kind of a drag, but if u can get thru those, you can get thru anything. Recommend to anyone with an interest in television and cultural history!

Thinks he is funny but I dont really see it beyond it being forced. You cannot use your phone nor laptop which makes it difficult to take notes especially when it gets dark outside. Lots of reading and discussion questions. Not hard, just tedious, just go to class, take the quiz on the movie and leave otherwise be bored for 2 hours. 3 Papers total
Steve is the best instructor I've ever had. He is funny and keeps the class interesting. Would definitely take another one of his classes.

analysis.name: Hannah Jordt

took autumn 2025, apparently was the worst qtr to take. exams did not match lectures and grade was HEAVILY based on group participation. prof jordt was very nice but not very fair while grading (whole class fell below curve and made us take another exam instead of curving). i guess dont take in autumn...

Going to be the voice of dissent here—Hannah is very approachable and nice, but she is extremely out of touch with her exams and they were in no way fair. analysis.name: Jeffrey Heer

Great professor!
Neat schedule, but annoying/overwhelming to see so many not-really-required "required" readings
Tips

- The Notebook is a different, interactive & free book.
- Lots of "required" reading, but if you focus on the assignments & in-class-practices (with some Notebook review) then you can ignore.

Wonderful lectures and course content as a whole are super useful for research, projects, and general data literacy. Assignments' grading is pretty hard and unclear, but you are practically guaranteed above a 3.5 if you put in just a little effort. No exams either!

What a gem. Jeffrey is one of the best profs in the CS department. He is funny, knowledgeable, and very approachable. Clearly knows his subject matter, and one of the best at Data Visualization. Makes the class fun, approachable, and easy for people of all skill levels in the domain. Highly recomemnd you take his class, you won't regret it.

absolutely wondeful lecturer. the grading system was odd and and unclear, but the assignments were interersting and engaging. very knowledgeable about the topic and created the systems we used. lots of good insight into effective design + communication.

analysis.name: Jennifer Graves
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, she was a fine professor. This class was just an insane amount of busy work and the Canvas was horribly organized. And anytime I asked for help or feedback from the TAs I was only given vague responses that were almost never helpful. Her teaching style was fine. And I value the material covered, I just wish it was better organized.

Jenny was a wonderful professor; her lectures always made the concepts easy to understand. She's very kind and helpful as well. Do every extra credit opportunity that's offered; they are so plentiful and you can easily get an A in this class with them. This class was very valuable and I intend to continue using what I learned in my future :)

She is very kind and caring. Her lectures and assignments are easy to follow along with. She doesn't force people to participate in discussions and allows cheat sheets for the exams. She is also very understanding and will provide extra help for your homework. I really enjoyed her class and almost switched my major to optmgt bc of her. TAKE HER!!!

This is my first time taking a business minor class and she made this class so engaging to where people who don't have a business/math background can truly understand the content. Retakes on quizzes are available until you get a passing grade. Tests/quizzes are open note and if you just study the material, you should pass. Very helpful and caring.
Absolutely loved her passion. She was a pleasure to have as a professor and she made sure you understood the material.

analysis.name: Kyle Haddad-Fonda

He expects high levels of dedication to his coursework.

lectures are great, but this is centered around an incredibly high level audience. Don't take this for credit- Eight assignments total, will assign papers worth 30% of your grade & grades aggressively.  Prof turns what is a very interesting period in history into a jumbled mess that requires lots of previous understanding. Needs prereqs.

You need to be able to remember everything in the assigned reading and everything he says in class, I do mean EVERYTHING. I got 40 pts off for getting the date of an event wrong. He acts cool and chill in lecture and office hours but for a 300 level class with no prereqs this course is a GPA killer. Take at your own risk.

Professor Haddad-Fonda is the most amazing history professor at the UW (Ive had him twice now). His class is extremely straight forward and all his classes follow the same structure. If you go to lecture and do the assigned readings (for this class, there were also pre-recorded lectures), its almost impossible to get lower than an A. Just study lol
No meaningful grades until week 9 so I didn't realize how harsh he was going to be until it was too late. Save yourself the stress and take something else because this class simply isn't worth it.

analysis.name: Mycah Harrold

Proffesor Harrold uses a participation scale that doesn't promote inclusivity. Students are constantly adding information that isn't useful to class discussions. Specifically, there is this girl that waste 30 minutes of class time talking.

analysis.name: Darryl Holman

Oh my gosh. 10/10. He is one of the good teachers, not a lot of those. He cares, and is always always available to help outside of class. He literally gives you his phone number. I assume people give bad reviews because the classes are challenging... lol? If a course you are actually interested in is offered with Professor Holman 100% take it :)

Dr. Holman is a good professor who cares about the content and his students' success. The lectures are boring & dry though. I got a 4.0 hardly attending class.
