I truly enjoyed this class. Get ready to ready of course and be prepare for his unexpected fun times. Dr. Holman really cares about his students and he wants you to learn. Very helpful in his office hours and he will make time to fit your hours. His persona is the best part of the class, very spontaneous. I love his style and I would take again!

I really enjoyed this class and Darryl as professor. He is very passionate about the subject and really wants you to understand. I highly recommend going to his office hours if you need help with problem sets. He's very approachable, responsive via email, and understanding. He's got some cool stories too.

analysis.name: Hajin Jun
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is really sweet and passionate. I did enjoy her lectures, but the unit quizzes were very confusing and difficult for me. I know I wasn't the only one because the TA told me so, yet there wasn't a curve or anything on the questions that most of the class got wrong which is rly weird. The final was an improvement but quizzes were worded so poorly

Professor Jun is an extremely kind and caring teacher. She always made sure we understood the content and even learned most of our names. The slides are also very clear, and her lectures are easy to understand and engage with.

Professor Jun is an amazing professor! Sweet, kind, and gives feedback that doesn't make you feel belittled. Beware though, Professor Jun is the most toughest grader I have ever had in my academic career so utilize her office hours if you are struggling.

Professor Jun clearly cares about her students. The lectures can get long but she's quite enthusiastic so they're not too boring. The reading is average for a 200 level, and outside of one formal essay there wasn't much writing. She doesn't grade super easy though, so if you're not familiar with history writing definitely go to office hours.

analysis.name: Ishita Lahiri
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I cannot recommend her enough. She is incredibly caring, easy to talk to, and deeply passionate about the material she teaches. The class itself is equally compelling, offering an intricate dive into the field of carework by blending theoretical frameworks with modern, lively examples.

English 111 by Lahiri is dope simply put. She is consistently funny and unbelievably relatable. The assignments she puts out are unique and challenging but in a way that still manages to be fun. The class forces you to grow as a writer which is a cool and wholesome experience. Overall great.
She is super chill and nice. Deadlines were flexible and graded fairly. Definitely would recommend!

analysis.name: Ian Schnee
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This is the worst class at UW. Phil 120 is not an intro to logic course, but rather a 10-week accelerated study into every minor facet of formal logic. I believe that for this to truly be an intro class, it would have to cut out content and become a series. Schnee wasn't helpful when students were clearly lost, instead just belittled them as "lazy"

I was not expecting this course to be so difficult. Although this is a "intro level" course, the material was extremely advanced. Each week the material becomes more complex, I wasn't able to understand after week 4. Prof Schnee adds questions to exams aimed to trip you up or about content we haven't learned. Avoid this course if you don't need it.
It was an absolute pleasure going to lectures! Always challenges his students and expects a lot but is also ready to help and is open for all questions.

Ian was a great professor- it was clear he loves what he does & wanted us to learn every lecture. Go to office hours- he's super accessible and wants to help you learn. You use the textbook he wrote himself which was clear & easy to follow. Assignments & tests were all reasonable as long as you put in your own effort. Highly recommend his class!

I have never seen a man so excited to teach every day. Probably the most enthusiastic professor I've had so far, and overall just teaches the subject really well. In all honesty, logic was a bit hard for me to follow sometimes, but Ian encourages students to try and be wrong which really helped. Just a fun guy honestly

analysis.name: Ileana Rodriguez-Silva
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very energetic and passionate about the subject. Her voice, however, literally hurts my ears as she screams while she lectures. Demands participation in classes of 60+ individuals. She is a very kind person and will help you outside of class if you wish. Lectures are unorganized, very difficult to understand them.

There's way too much homework and readings for a 200 level course. Ive taken multiple 400-500 level courses that had significantly less assignments. I was incredibly stressed the entirety of the quarter by the multitude of readings and content I was expected to read or view in a relatively short amount of time.

One of the best professors I've had. Grades are hard but fair and every lecture has a lot of substance but incredibly informative. If you're ok going to lectures and doing the reading she will be amazing.

Very passionate, kind, and understanding. She definitely cares about her job and her students. I struggled with my mental health that quarter but I talked with her and she helped me come up with a plan, and she checked in a few times to make sure I was doing okay and congratulate me when I managed to turn everything in. Wonderful person in general

I enjoyed her lectures a lot and her class is very interesting. However, we need to read a lot and most of our grades come from the reading reflections. It's important that you write those reflections well. If you pay attention in class and take note, it is not a very hard class.

analysis.name: Ruth Huwe
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 188 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: MGMT isn't a hard class to teach; all you do is paraphrase the textbook in lecture. If this class was important to me, I would be frustrated that Ruth wastes A LOT of class talking about useless personal anecdotes. She also throws in weird test questions, which are often disputable if you challenge her on them. Curve is toughish. Class is a waste.

I took MGMT 320 online and it was infuriating. All of Ruths assignments are meandering and incredibly confusing. She does not prepare students for exams and then does not provide enough time to compete them. Her lectures are incredibly partisan as she complains about conservatives and rambles about current news. For your sanity, find someone else.

Some say she is biased. It's true. Fortunately for me, she favoured me, which made the class easier for me. But for other students, she would get upset at them. My groupmates complained she was always mad at them. Get on her good side. Her class is hard, all reading and memorisation, not very intuitive. Quizzes and exams soley based on textbook.

Just super subjective vibes based class. If she likes something it gets points if she doesn't it wont. This was embodied one day when a student raised there hand to answer "low wages" which she claimed was wrong before showing a list of answers that contained word for word "low wages". Disorganized, unclear expectations, makes an easy class hard.

Easily the worst professor I've ever had. Ruth is incredibly rude and condescending toward students, tests you on complete nonsense from lectures and readings, and overcomplicates a basic course. I've learned absolutely nothing all quarter except how to memorize random, irrelevant facts. Please take this course with Todd instead.

analysis.name: Isabella Novik
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Excellent lecturer. Very easy-to-read lecture slide decks to review. No textbook. Topics covered aren't super challenging conceptually, but you need to know all of the theorems very well for exams. Exams have a high median, usually 80-90%, so there isn't a generous curve. Homework sets can be long (maybe 7-10 proofs) but are otherwise reasonable.

Fantastic professor, first time in a while that I felt going to lectures was worthwhile. Proofs are interactive, she uses great examples and illustrations, and explanations are incredibly helpful. Lecture notes aren't provided before classes, which is a shame, but they are still helpful regardless. Overall one of the best math professors at the UW.

Prof. Novik is the best math professor I've had at UW. She's excellent at explaining quite an abstract subject and clearly enjoys doing so. Further, she's very accessible outside of class for help if you need it, and is just as welcoming and helpful in office hours. I would take her class again in a heartbeat.

This class was hands down the hardest course I took in my undergraduate degree in Mathematics here at UW, however she is a very nice lady and helped me out a lot. Go to office hours the minute you start having problems in the class because she needs to know. Also try to find other people you can study with because it will be a nightmare going solo.
Prof. Novik is one of the best professors I had at UW. Extremely quick to respond to emails, great at explaining  concepts and is very friendly during office hours.

analysis.name: Jonathan Isaac
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Isaac's class this quarter. He is kind, He takes the time to provide helpful and insightful feedback on homework. I did not have any issues trying to meet for office hours or have to wait a long period for an email response. He is genuinely enthusiastic and cares about the students doing well.

I took ENGL 298. Workload was extremely light, no midterms and no final. Only one group project towards the end of the quarter. Attending class is mandatory and so is participation/ engagement. Extra credit was available. Professor Isaac is extremely sweet and understanding. I would retake this class in a heartbeat.

He is an incredible professor who is very caring and responsive. He thoughtfully addresses everyone's questions and brings in many interesting readings for class, making it possible to learn a lot. He invites guest speakers to share their insights. Truly, he is an outstanding professor, and his course is fascinating. Also, there aren't many works.

Best English class ever taken here. Dr. Isaac is just so cool and chill. Such easy credits since his feedback is the best and his grading is not bad at all. One thing is that this class is mainly focused on participation so be ready to talk a lot every day.

analysis.name: Mack Ikeru
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It's kinda hard to rate this one because I took his EDUC 240, but the class wasn't his. He was teaching some else's class. So he didn't make any of the assignments or anything. He is very understanding and engaging. Also only 1 class a week, but it was canceled half the time, so no one showed up. Also too much class discussion, not enough lecture

I went to a total of about 3 classes and still passed with flying colors. The content is actually very interesting for an intro but you basically learn nothing new. No exams, no essays, just a portfolio to submit with very lax grading. Not a bad teacher, just boring. Do not recommend if you want actually want to learn about education (ironically).

You can't learn anything from this class. Lectures once a week and he usually cancels the class. He just read the PPT and sometimes feels like he is not that familiar with what he is teaching. Weekly assignments are required but always been asked to write about the same thing/topics. I don't know what they are doing.

Professor Ikeru is a nice guy and very personable. Homework is very, very lax in this class, and Ikeru's lectures are not...super necessary to attend; you can do basically everything out of class. There are some cool guest lecturers though! This class is very much an intro and doesn't present a ton of novel information.

Very kind and caring and funny, although in person lectures felt very unnecessary. Class used ungrading, so we chose our grades at the end of the quarter based on how we felt we did in class, so a 4.0 is relatively easy. This class does have a volunteer requirement, so depending on the place you volunteer it will be a very different experience.

analysis.name: Charles Ives
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 60 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Charles is like an innocent little child. Has a deep affection for Platonic thought. Quirky, yet hilarious. He is quite charming, an unspoiled gem among a lackluster and uninspired Seattle Freeze. Willing to be flexible to see his students succeed. Gets excited about the smallest things. Yes, quirky, but also has a lion's heart. Highly Recommend!

The readings are kind of long but the material itself is easy to grasp and therefore going to class to discuss the reading may seem repetitive. However, the class is what you make of it, so engage in the discussion and you won't be bored! I was never stressed or overwhelmed and he is honestly easy going, friendly, and fun.

First of all, he is simply not an instructor. He does not have anything planned, ever. He babbles about how much of a "different" approach he has on teaching, and never says anything relevant. Half of the class sat in the back and did homework for another class. I barely went to class, should have, but didn't since he led such awful conversations.

Charles' teaching style motivated me to get out the door every day for this class. He's dynamic in his teaching and he exudes genuine joy doing his job. He offers a unique perspective to teaching that other philosophy professors at UW simply don't have. His classes are experiments, so be open to defining expectations as the quarter progresses.

You can tell Charles cares a lot about what he teaches, and how it impacts his students. The course itself consists of readings at home and a short summary (200 words) before the lecture. The lecture was a full class discussion about the readings, based on opinions and the exchange of ideas. He is a great guy and showing up to class was beneficial.

analysis.name: Erkan Istanbulluoglu
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Ist. really struggles with communication, IMO. I often get the sense he hasn't looked at lecture slides since he gave the lecture a year before. He once spent 50min of lecture on rain gauge under-catch. Wording on HW is ambiguous and confusing. He seems personally like a great guy, and probably a great researcher, but not a great teacher.

He's a very kind professor who is accessible outside of class a couple times a week. However, he is pretty disorganized, and his lectures can be hard to follow/understand. Definitely find the textbook somewhere.
Don't take this professor unless it's needed
Very unorganized, lectures are unclear

Just didn't seem to know what he was talking about. Needed correcting many times throughout the quarter, and never really seemed sure of himself. Class was pretty easy, but just seemed like a waste of time. I got a 3.2 only because I forgot to do a couple homework assignments.

analysis.name: Jeffrey Knight
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Knight didn't seem to really connect with the students, and it reflected in the lectures and assignments. The content was fine, but nothing could have prepared me for how irrelevant the final exam was from the class. The amount of reading wasn't too bad, but unless you memorize all of it word for word, the exam will be difficult.

Jeff Knight is a great lecturer who is clearly passionate about teaching English. Even if you don't like Shakespeare at the beginning of the course, Jeff makes the class interesting and fun. I fell behind on reading a few times but the lectures always caught me up to speed. An excellent professor worth taking if you are interested in English!

Lectures weren't mandatory but if you didn't go you would probably struggle with the final. Thankfully they were all really interesting. There can be a lot of reading at times but overall it was manageable.

Prof. Knight was awesome in so many ways. Entertaining, passionate, and kind. Participation is 25%, two essays (one graded by TA, one by prof.) and a final cumulative exam (30%). Every lecture slide is posted, but not recorded. But PLEASE attend because he is so interesting to listen to. Genuinely the best professor I've had at UW.

This is one of the best classes I have ever taken at UW. Prof. Knight is highly entertaining, and his lectures are excellent. Shakespeare is hard, but the class makes reading it way easier. I came in liking Shakespeare's works, and I know I will come out of this class LOVING them. I cannot stress enough what a privilege it is to take this class.

analysis.name: Jennifer Ruesink
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 59 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: these other reviews are lowk melodramatic. this class is def harder than 180/200 but that's consistent across BIOL 220 classes. to do well you actually have to understand the concepts + apply them moreso than 180/200 which is why its harder. going to lecture + working thru all the unit packets (and UNDERSTANDING the key) will set u up for success

THE most unorganized lecturerer ever. Unclear notes, vague questions, and difficult to follow lectures. If you are not paying 140% attention in class at all times, you WILL be lost because her notes are THAT bad. TAs carry this class. External brains are tedious, vague, and a way of getting out of teaching fundamental material. Very frustrating!

Wastes excessive lecture time on pointless group calls. Her slides are confusing and unhelpful, and exams test whether you mirror her phrasing rather than understand the material. The “external brain” assignments add little value, and her unconventional teaching methods would be far more effective if replaced with traditional readings.

I disliked the lecture style. Slides were often changed mid-presentation or ignored which made taking notes or following the lecturer difficult.

Concepts were approached in weird abstract ways where the abstract methods of flux / Nernst equation was prioritized over the actual content.

Lectures rarely covered all content, so reading is necessary.

I have never met a professor that is willing to go the extra mile like Dr. Ruesink did for me. I had life events this qtr get in the way of my studies & she really helped me back on my feet when I struggled, something you wouldn't expect a weed out course professor to do. She is so approachable & provided so many study resources to the whole class.

analysis.name: James Wellman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 98 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Wellman's teaching style is incredibly Christian centric for Western religions. For example, his example in lecture of what a religious tradition is: Donald Trump says he wants to make America great, which makes Americans want to be great. School shootings were his example of a ritual. His lectures are unclear and his style booming.

This class was interesting at first but slowly degraded into a disorganized mess. The amount of reading is ABSURD(200 textbook pgs in two days). The relevance of the reading is questionable. He didn't follow the syllabus, grading seems almost random. He struggled to remember things very frequently and I am worried he may suffer from memory loss.

I agree with the disorganization, but he was very lenient and understanding. As long as you would write about your opinion or view and what you learned that's an easy A. A handwritten reflection is written at the end of every lecture. Many books were required BUT he goes over them. Just take notes. Very interesting and diverse.

He is very passionate about what he teaches and genuinely interested in engaging students in conversation. But the assignments are poorly planned—his writing prompts are super vague and it seems that even he doesn't know what he wants the essay to be about, but then you're expected to produce a 4 page essay. His lectures can also be rambling.

Prof. Wellman is very passionate about what he teaches and is genuinely interested in engaging students in conversation. But he doesn't put a lot of planning into the class structure. The essay prompts are super vague and even he seems undecided about what he wants students to write about, but then you're supposed to write a 4 page essay from that.

analysis.name: Junghee Kim
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Kim is an amazing teacher! You will learn a ton of Korean with her and make great friends in class. She is super engaging, approachable, and kind, and classes are always a lot of fun. Of course there is a lot of work in this class, but how else can you learn a language well without putting in work? I 100% recommend taking Korean with her.

I love Professor Kim! She makes learning Korean very fun, and the weekly quizzes were good grade boosters. She is easily accessible outside of class and eager to help students do well. She always asks for feedback after tests and adjusts the following tests based off of what students say. Attendance is mandatory, but it is necessary to do well. :)

I feel that many people that have complained forget this is a language course so of course it won't be easy. If you are truly interested in the language and want to learn she is a great professor for that. There is a decent amount of homework but you have a week to do it and can finish it in an hour. The quizzes and exams aren't the hardest either.

No curves on the tests at all. Schedules are not well-planned. Unit test, a presentation, an oral exam and the final exam all in two weeks. Lectures are too boring, and attendance is mandatory. We can learn much more during quiz sections.

Lots of tests on knowledge of vocab and grammar, but expected for a language class. It is helpful to see her outside of class time in her office and she is always happy to answer questions. While she seems strict, she is a relaxed grader if you put in effort. One of the only teachers I know that listens to feedback and adapts to student's wishes.

analysis.name: James Pfeiffer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I loved this class! It was the most interesting course I have taken at UW and it was all because of Pfeiffer's passion and personal connection to the subject! If you are at all interested in global and international health, I would strongly recommend taking this course. There is one midterm and a final paper and essay with long weekly readings.

Dr. Pfeiffer is an incredibly caring professor whose main concern is students engaging and learning the material. The grading criteria is crystal clear so if you complete the assigned work and follow directions you will get a good grade. Exams were straight forward and the grading was more than fair. Low stress class with meaningful topics.

Learned a lot from his class. Well-respected, very knowledgeable with a sense of humor. Does great job explaining anthropological concepts and events. There are lots of reading! That's expected for an anth and global health class so I reccomend skimming or reading few sections if you can't get through all of it.

Prof. Pfeiffer is understanding, helpful, and kind. Class was incredibly interesting. Each week consisted of readings, lecture videos, discussion posts, and reading response summaries + a midterm, a final, and a final paper. Midterm and final were 2 essay questions. Material was engaging. Favorite class (and professor) at UW so far.

This class is really interesting and it is obvious that professor Pfeiffer is very passionate and knows what he is talking about. Attendance is mandatory and there are a couple of readings assigned each week, but as long as you show up to lecture and keep up with the readings and assignments, the exams should be smooth sailing.

analysis.name: Jordan Nickerson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Ignore the poor feedback on this website - Jordan is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He cares about his students, puts an enormous amount of time and effort into his lectures, and teaches in a very clear and direct way that builds a solid foundation for future finance classes. Quick note: the cases are difficult, but they're graded lightly.

I almost didn't take this class with Jordan due to all the reviews here, but I'm so glad I did. Jordan knows his stuff and wants students to learn. He's accessible outside of class, is a great lecturer, and encourages participation. There isn't much homework and he provides practice problems before the tests. I would recommend him to anyone.

Jordan is an amazing professor! He is a great lecturer, posts plenty of practice problems, and has fair grading policies. The homework assignments are straightforward and his exams are doable. I learned a ton in his course and think he's one of the best finance professors at UW. I highly recommend you take his class!

Jordan's cases are extremely unclear. He forgets tons of info and expects students to make the assumptions as his. How answers should be calculated is not communicated; does not do or teach clear financial modeling or allow access to his sheets. Lectures are extremely surface level and expects you already know complex ideas never taught. Nice guy

Great professor who genuinely cares about his students' success. His teaching breaks down hard concepts in an easy way. The class was hard, but you'll be fine if you do your homework and stay consistent. Learned a lot in this class, recommend.

analysis.name: Jessie Seiler
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: i think this is a hard class for some people to garble with, it asks people to take a look at systems and race and then apply those concepts to yourself. But overall Jessie's contribution came from a place of knowledge about the unjust systems that the US is built off of. I think the class super informative

The class was very disorganized. Assignments were sometimes forgotten and posted just before they were due, yet they were still required. The final project, we were assigned niche topics with no choice. Our group met the rubric, but got a low grade due to a dislike of our assigned topic. Questions about ur grades answered after they were finalized.

Everything important was graded the last day grades were official/due and she refused to answer any questions regarding grading until after the grades were official. When asked about grading throughout the quarter, she was vague. Unclear grading criterias, untimely grading, and unfortunately a disorganized/uncoordinated teaching team this quarter.

The class is unorganized. Jessie is not open to opinions that differ from theirs. The grading is unnecessarily difficult. For the final group project, you are asked to pick a mutual aid group that fits the topic they give you. My group's topic literally did not exist, and then we were told we did the assignment wrong.
Show up to class, participate, and ask questions. Jessie cares deeply about the class and her students, but you need to be willing to engage and reach out when things are unclear.

analysis.name: Jonah Ostroff
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 225 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The Prof-Stroff! Jonah is extremely passionate about math and instruction. He's personable and extremely fair. His lectures are very well structured and he provides every resource for you to succeed. The one drawback is that his tests aren't the hardest, and people are very engaged in class, so the averages can be high. Ask about his math songs.

He made 308 so easy. He has the longest office hours I've seen in my entire UW life and he is also very funny. Posts all his notes online unlike other profs but I would still recommend going to class because he can really teach. I loved his nerd jokes. The only problem is that he's such a good prof no one is lost so you can't expect much curve

Lectures were easy to follow along with, may be hard to keep on track with the videos & hw, very test-heavy, tests were challenging but nothing you wouldn't be prepared for if you studied. I recommend doing previous tests and going to his online review session because he talks about specific tricks (that I found helpful) that may be on the test.

Prof. Ostroff had us watch pre-recorded lectures on our own time and used in-person lectures mostly as review and to further dive into the topics, which I can vouch worked really well for me. He's super engaging and funny and generally just a fun person to talk with. He's also almost scarily competent--his passion for math really shines through.

extremely cool guy! would rec the online ver. great, pre-recorded lectures and minimal hw. you can and should go in-person if you want!! pretty sure he didn't know i was asynch until the final (you take it in different rooms). go to office hours (jonah has 3 office hours a week! honestly really cool of him) and it's basically impossible to fail.

analysis.name: Kai Ybarbo
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The instructor is not very responsive and tends to engage more with fluent English speakers, making it harder for others to get help. Limited communication affected my understanding, and improvements in accessibility and equitable interaction are needed.

Really cares that you know and understand the material. Lectures are easy to follow and the material that you need to know for the exam is clearly stated. Would totally recommend taking a class with him.

best bio prof i've ever had. he's very nice, funny, and accessible outside of class. loves smash bros and kpop lmao. his exams are pretty easy and straight foward. his lectures are amazing so if you just watch and review you will be fine. he rarely uses poll everywhere so you can miss a lot of classes.

Absolutely adored having Kai as a prof this quarter. Funny & overall caring. Explanations were clear and cohesive. Class organization was great. Flow diagrams --> very important to succeed!! External brains function almost as a flipped classroom model and can be time-consuming but are important as well. Would absolutely take another course w/ him!

Kai was a great prof. He was both hilarious but professional and made lectures overall enjoyable. He was quite accessible out of class with his office hours. His exam were difficult for me but if you are able to study the lecture material and do his provided flow diagrams its quite helpful for the exam.

analysis.name: Kevin Zatloukal
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 76 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Would give a 1 but he's handsome af
Be prepared to not be able to sleep and do anything else besides your homework for this class.

Kevin has a soothing and angel-like voice and his pitch is calming in that it usually goes really high up at the end of the sentence. I like him, but as for lecture, I do not understand anything and clearly I got annihilated by the tests. It is a hard class, and I don't think he does a good job teaching it.

Only 8 home-works for the whole quarter. Gives an entire week to finish the homework. Attend the lecture and you'll be able to do the hw. His lectures are well structured and he takes time to answer every questions. The midterm and final were in class but the questions were very similar to the hw and the practice problems !!no surprises :) !! .

This class has been restructured this quarter and is experimental. The class is hard and definitely requires a huge time commitment and sleepless nights, so it really should have come with warnings. That being said, the prof definitely knows his stuff, and there's a lot of priceless info he teaches: changes my paradigm. Prepare to suffer but learn

analysis.name: Wes King
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Search up what black boxing in a tech context means. We are not allowed to say black boxing “bc we can't use black or white in this class” even tho there's NO racial affiliation at all. As a liberal some insane things have been said in this classroom. Asian women are fetishized bc ppl think Black is associated w Black men and White Asian women? wut

A lot of people expect INFO 200 to be more closely related to informatics / programming - which I understand is where the conflict surrounding it comes from - but I do feel that equity courses like these are genuinely necessary for everyone, in every field.

You get what you put in - the class is incredibly thought-provoking if you want it to be.

this class is required for first-year transfers or anyone applying to the major it is manageable once you get used to the weekly flow biggest downside is strict participation with assigned seats and you can be marked absent if you do not engage even if you show up work is easy overall and your ta can really affect your experience.

What a waste of time. Attendance is mandatory for two hour lectures where the professor rants about topics that have absolutely nothing to do with informatics. The quizzes are very hard because they include questions about specific details mentioned in a video or book or a comment that the professor made a week ago in lecture. Don't take this class

Wonderful Professor. Dr. Kim is very caring and inspirational, inspired me a lot and make me want to peruse in Informatics major. Completely changed my life, one of the best class I've ever taken. I feel connected to people, and I was motivated a lot. Appreciate Dr. Kim's support throughout each assignment and reading. Highly recommend! Easy 4.0

analysis.name: Kenneth Sebens
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: professor is very enthusiastic about invertebrates. labs and field trips are very fun, but after lab drawings and worksheets can take a while so don't fall behind. tests are pretty easy and you get a bunch of cheat sheets.

There was a decent amount of homework which got tiresome halfway through the course. Labs are fun, but there is a lot of things to cover sometimes. The lectures are SO boring, but you have to go bc there are random in class assignments. Slides have no words on, just read the textbook and you'll be fine. Not enough organization for a zoology class.

Quizzes are extremely difficult - you need to know the stuff or you won't pass.  All he does in lecture is drone on for two hours (better off studying material in your own time). Very poor communication (no office hours for prof or TAs, organization of field trip planning is unpredictable and short notice, does not reply to emails). Good luck...

Terrible at lecturing, I can literally read the slides on my own and learn without wasting time with his boring lectures. good luck trying not to fall asleep. So much work for so little credits, very unorganized and unclear. Ken should just stay as a researcher and not a professor, he is probably the worst I have had.

The class content was not hard at all, he did have midterms which were fairly easy as well. However lectures were long and difficult to get through. There would be random days that will have in class activities that are graded so attending would be smart.

analysis.name: Kyle Thayer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Overall the class experience was optimal. Thayer was a great professor the lectures were clear and thorough. The lectures covered 110% of the work in the assignment as he often completed the same thing needed in the lecture with a different dataset. Was always eager to answer questions and help students if they needed it.

Though Kyle seems a bit frazzled at times, he is kind and goes through demos in class which are very helpful. He is understanding when it comes to due dates and the regrade policy is great. For a first time coder it was tough (Google is ur BFF) but make sure to talk to the TAs and ask questions in class, and you should be okay and will learn a lot!
I learned so much in this class. Thayer is a great professor and as long as you follow his code during lecture you will do great.

Lectures were clear and posted online (both recordings and slides) and optional readings provided. Easy to ask questions during lecture. No tests, grade is mostly the weekly assignments, weekly review, and final group project + extra credit opportunities. Many check ins for group project so you won't have an unfair grade. Great professor!

As someone who had no experience coding, I was intimidated going into this course, yet it turned out to be my easiest class. Thayer makes the class EXTREMELY beginner-friendly, with TA's always willing to help. No exams, only a final group project that consists of joining datasets (it's pretty short and easy with a decent group)

analysis.name: Leila Norako
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's late to class every single day, even to Zoom ones. She also has a habit of ranting about her political views for at least 20 to 30 minutes per day. Also, contacting her is nearly impossible: she never responds to emails, misses her own rescheduled office hours, and rushes off if you try to talk to her at the end of class. I do not recommend.

She's literally always late, even to online class days. Most of the time, she talks about her political views, then acts surprised when there is no time left in class. Her lectures are mandatory, and we have very long handwritten assignments every week, but they are disorganized. She's a nice person, though, and has good thoughts on the readings.

Late to class every day. Was late to a zoom class. Will talk about random stuff that isn't related to the course materials for 10-30 minutes a day, eating up a good quarter of the class. Secondary reading that were impossible to read as there were incorrect page numbers with little to no instruction. No feedback on writing at all. Fine lecturer.

Overall, you can tell she's a nice person who truly cares about her students. However, she simply isn't organized. Consistently late, would cancel class at the last minute, and would talk about her political opinions the majority of the time, with only a handful of time dedicated to class content. She's kind, but in all honesty, a bit too much.

I know that comments like these can be personal, but putting personal feelings aside, she is always late. The last minute Zoom meetings we would have, she would be at least 20 minutes late. She doesn't believe in slides and what's worse is that she assigns you to reflect on the lectures...but she just talks about literally whatever during lecture.

analysis.name: Laura Little
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Little is very nice, kind and happy to help, which are great traits for a professor. Expect that she is very bad at teaching. I disagree with reviews saying "stats is hard but Laura makes it easy" because for me stats is easy and Laura makes it hard. Her exams are also super confusingly ambigously worded. Prepare to self teach if u have her.

Prof. Little is amazing! She truly wants you to understand and she is always open to questions. Its clear she cares about all her students succeeding and is open to talking in and out of her office hours. She also holds zoom reviews the night before the exam and has no time cut off so she makes sure everyones questions get answered.

Professor Little is a really attentive and caring professor. I feel like the harsh comments have to do with how hard the coursework is. Attending office hours and putting in more work in your own time will be what you have to do to get high grades in any statistics class. She's an amazing professor! Don't miss the chance on not having her teach you

Rep is for being nice, not for teaching ability. Tests don't reflect course content but your personal problem solving ability. If not already statistically literate, avoid her class. While nice, she's unclear and distracted, and she demands more than most. You must be excellent at teaching yourself if you are to succeed. Skip lecture. Not worth it.

Tests are open book/notes. Lab worksheets cover exactly whats on the test and is almost a step by step instruction. That said the tests won't be easy if you don't study. Lastly, she and her TA's offer A TON of help. I enjoyed this class and would GLADLY take any class Dr. Little offers. This class is only hard if you don't put in a little effort.

analysis.name: Larry Pierce
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Larry is honestly the best math professor I have ever had. He truly cares about whether or not students succeed. He never acts like a question is stupid and always responds with enthusiasm. He's also very funny. He cares about students learning applications and connections, which really makes the material feel relevant. He made me like math again!

Larry is so great! Definitely one of the best professors I've met. He can explain things in a very logic and clear way. His class is super amazing as well ! The lecture is organized very clearly and highly-structured. Very Friendly for note-takers. Highly Recommended ! I would definitely take it his classes again !

If you work through the past exams and make sure you understand everything in the textbook, you'll do really well and get a nearly perfect score. Larry is very willing to answer your questions and friendly. The final grade cutoff ended up being high, but that was because the exams were easy and the awful median 3.0 policy.

Great professor! Kind, great at explaining things in multiple ways, and more concerned about student success than anything else. He was happy to go out of his way to help students, and on a couple occasions I invited friends to his lectures. The friends also felt that he was a super great teacher. I will be looking to take classes with him again!

Truly cares about student success; was willing to push back a lot of the homework due dates. Math dept is stifling him. Truly a nice human being and a great teacher, if only he was given more power to do what he wanted with the lecture time. He tried to make the midterms as easy as possible lol.

analysis.name: Louisa MacKenzie
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The professor is very passionate about what she teaches and she's also very open-minded. She cares a lot about people's personal interpretations of things, so you don't really have to worry about being wrong. The class itself is well structured and the grading is lenient. The only thing she cares about is whether or not you're engaged/interested.

This was an interesting class that she made engaging. She is very clear on assignments, grading, and is generous with make up. The quizzes were very easy and had extra credit occasionally. She gives you all the resources to succeed and if you watch the movies, you will do very well.
PLEASE take this professor if you need an A&H, DIV, or both. Very easy class.
Awesome professor. Worth your time.

This class changed how I view everything in the world- I've become a much more aware person. Prof Mackenie is the best prof I have had the pleasure of taking at UW, and I hope to take classes from her in the future(even though French isn't my major). She's just great.

analysis.name: Yulenni  Venegas Lopez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The grading was extremely harsh and felt excessive for an undergraduate class, with expectations that didn't always seem clearly explained or consistent. If you're considering this course, be prepared for very strict grading and unclear expectations. It may work better for students who are comfortable figuring things out independently.

Having Yulenni as a TA really helped me improve as a writer. Essays are usually the hardest part for me, so this class was definitely challenging, but I found her feedback to be super helpful. If you're able to take the time & really apply her advice you'll see a lot of growth

The professor for this class and lecture were great but Yuleni was the worst part. She's tries way too hard to be funny and doesn't know what she's talking about. The only good thing about having her be the TA for this class is there wasn't section.

Yulenni is a great TA! I was having a hard time but she helped me a lot in office hours. If you care about your grade and want to understand the material, just go to office hours and don't be afraid to ask questions! She's a fair grader.
Yulenni is really funny and caring. She engages the entire section, and is really helpful during office hours. She also gives great feedback on assignments.

analysis.name: Louise Kapustka
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very easy class. Makes her 8:30 worth going to. Midterm and final are easy, group project can be difficult if you get assigned a bad group. Would recommend starting that ASAP.

Louise is EASILY one of the best profs I've ever had. She GENUINELY cares about your well-being and success. She gives great tips and tricks for your professional life. Her class is so unique and she makes it so much fun. I swear, my 8:30 class didn't feel like it... You learn the content but in a practical way. Love her!!! (also a super easy 4.0)

Louise is fantastic. She is extremely organized, quick to respond to emails, and kind. Structure is a lecture with one pretty chill team exercise per class. Participation matters - she'll call on you or your team to share. Tests are SUPER easy if you have the textbook - remote, it's open-note and open book. Overall, it's a really chill class

Great Teacher, one of my favorites Ive had in Foster, however she will assign points for in class participation assignments that will end up being a huge determinant of your grade in the end. I wish I could only say good things about Louise but her horrible grading scale for in class participation left me with a very bad taste in my mouth.

Louise is a fantastic professor. Highly recommend. Her lectures are very entertaining, and the classroom activities relate to the curriculum. There is a textbook which I rented BUT you don't need it. Her lectures provide more than enough information. Would take any of her classes!

analysis.name: James Long
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 102 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: readings interesting but tedious; Long is well versed on the subject matter... It's the way he lectures I could not get past. He frequently pauses for effect in the middle of saying the most basic concept. He could be telling me my own name and still reveal each letter like I've never seen the alphabet before. Tone of condescending self-importance.

I do not know how it's possible that this many students have had such great experiences with him. He is seriously rude to students. Ask the wrong questions in class and you'll pay for it. He will shame you if you don't understand things. Moves way too quickly through the slides and he knows it.

He's kind of intimidating but the lectures are great and the readings are all really interesting except for the Rose Ackerman textbook which is pretty dull. This class is a lot of work (about 100-200 pages of reading a week) but I learned a lot so it felt worth it. 

30% midterm, 40% final, 10% short response, 10% short response, 10% participation

Okay, so i'm not sure why Long gets such great reviews. His ego is overtly inflated and he's rude to students. He's condescending when questions are asked. Furthermore, he goes off on tangents and his whole 371 syllabus appeared disorganized. He made really out-there connections with no substance. It wasn't rooted in content but his own hypotheses.

I'm honestly surprised that he managed to receive such high ratings from some students. Professor Long seems to enjoy making his classes unnecessarily difficult. He speaks fast on purpose and each slide is full of paragraphs, making it difficult to take notes and keep up. He also tends to have a condescending attitude towards students

analysis.name: William McGovern
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Best maths professor at UW, easily.  Pros: Clear, focused, organized lectures. Doesn't stray far from the book. You know exactly what to expect on the tests if you go to his review day. The theoremsdef's he hammers home is only what he tests on. Easy grader Cons: He speaks very quickly and tends to stand in front of his writing. TAKE HIS CLASS!

Passionate and knows a lot about math. Talks very fast during lecture so I recommend going over slides before class. Homework is difficult but exams are not bad at all and he usually gives practice exam problems similar to the real exam. Tends to go on math tangents that won't be tested just for fun, which can be a bit confusing. Overall cool prof!

Had him as my two week lecturer in a math camp over the summer at UW (I'm a high school student). Although he was challenging from time to time, he would help if anyone needed it. Moreover, he is such a kind, genuine and caring person. You will not regret taking his class. I promise

Math 506 with Monty was by far the hardest class I have ever taken. His homework is tough and interesting. The lectures are almost impossible to follow if you don't thoroughly read the material before class, but fascinating and entertaining if you did. Final was brutally difficult and not generously curved. I learned a ton and would do it again.

The way he teaches online classes is by reading slides for 15-20 minutes (for a 50-minute class). Extremely hard to follow. I playback at 0.75 speed in order to "listen"(not understanding) to what he is saying(compare to the 1.5 and 2.0 speed I use for other Profs). He gave high grades, thus a high rating. But not recommended if you want to learn.

analysis.name: Marek Wieczorek
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 71 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Don't get fooled by the title of the course, we do not talk much about Lady Gaga. This class isn't an easy A, theres so much readings to do and prerecorded lectures to watch before lecture and there will be quizzes about the readings. The lectures are very long and boring. I wouldn't take this class if you need an A&H credit.

Marek is great. The ideas he taught are powerful, readings are intense for 200level class and all pdf files, but relevant to modern art issues and beautifully selected. If you have the ability of abstract thinking, you will find this class gradually turns itself into a ladder that allows you to climb on and reach the sublime beyond your presence.

I would suggest only taking one of Marek's classes if you're really interested in the topic. The lectures are not very engaging so it's easy to get lost and lose track of what or who he's talking about. The multiple choice on the exam was also very wordy and hard to understand. I did learn a lot in this class but more from the textbook than him

Lecture was so boring + quiz every class. Sometimes I'd get 100% on a quiz, other times I'd get less than 50% even though I read and understood the material. I hated all the reading and how we were expected to memorize/prioritize written interpretations on pieces instead of encouragd to make our own.

This class is HORRIBLE, if you are interested in art history then it might not be that bad but he assigns SO MUCH readings it's insane. Quizzes aren't too bad, they;re all online and only 2 exams he assigns and all multiple choice but definitely boring in my taste and kept falling asleep especially since it is in a dark room and it's a 2 hr class.

analysis.name: Marjorie Olmstead
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Theres no doubt Prof. Olmstead knows her stuff, but it feels like she expects you to know everything she does. She is very organized, in the wrong way. Information overload in some lectures, often times she will not finish the lecture and have to skip material. Expects you to read textbook before classes, which is fair. At least she is friendly.

She has an amazing capability to make even the most simple physics concepts confusing, even if they are things you already know. She also loves to throw in completely useless information about the world of complex physics and does lots of useless demos that take a lot of time.

Olmstead is quite nice but sometimes boring, sometimes interesting. Lecture participation is 10% of the course grade. I supplemented with an edition of Halliday & Resnick from my mom and had some prior experience with the material so can't accurately judge the difficulty of the class. Exams are on the more difficult side.

Lectures are dull and unhelpful compared to reading the textbook, professor always flops demonstrations. Labs are unhelpful to concepts taught in lecture yet tested on in exams. She cares more about seeming smart than actually teaching the class and fails in both.
Great professor, Incredibly kind and Caring. Lectures are okay and typical of what you will find in the 12x physics courses. She always does her best to explain things when you ask questions.

analysis.name: Mandy Schivell
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 139 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: BIOL 240 Intensive Introductory Biology: Human Health Emphasis It is 15 credits and all of intro biology in ONE 10 WEEK SUMMER QUARTER! It is not easy but doable. Schivell was one of three profs. Her lectures were clear and test questions were ok, she needs to work on making test questions clear about what she is asking which she self admits.

Dr.Schivell is honestly amazing. Her lectures are easy to grasp and she's good at explaining hard topics well. Her public exams are a lifesaver and definitely helped me study well. The only gripe I have is that the exams can be very tough despite the public exams, but there are enough outside opportunities to compensate.Take her section if you can!

While Mandy does come to class excited and tries her best to be a good lecturer, I personally found her slides a bit disorganized. And when she is teaching, it tends to get very messy with her drawings and descriptions. However, I believe this is just a matter of personal preference, as everyone else I know has liked her a lot. She was consistent.

Releases exams beforehand with redacted values to reduce test anxiety. If you work to understand the content these are basically godsent and will get you the grade you want. You can drop 1 of four exams including the final, so I got to prioritize my other finals. Challenging content, but fairly good explanations and very sweet person overall.

Dr. Mandy does a great job explaining all of the content, however, her slides are very disorganized and she often doesn't post the annotated versions of her slides after class. Labs are very helpful to reinforce content and the TAs are great! The public exams were the best part about this class, they help teach you how to study honestly

analysis.name: Nicole McNichols
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 290 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. McNichols is the rare combination of incredibly well-educated and versed, yet humble and kind. Although the long lectures can be a tough, she is always there to clarify any concepts you don't understand and very obviously cares about her students. This class takes hushed or taboo topics and encourages students to explore their preconceptions.

Easy credit but god awful teacher. Major ego and terrible lectures. The content is pretty interesting for the first half of the quarter but she really fell off in the latter half. I feel Professor McNichols is only liked because she is pretty funny and social.

Attendance mandatory for students but not the prof, who only taught maybe 1/3 of her own class. Grad student who took over/TAs did great. Note the $100 textbook she wrote and you have to buy outside course fee. Doesn't respond to email reasonably or want to engage with students. Cares about her social media/getting a book deal but not her teaching.

Dr. McNichols is among the most adored psych profs at UW by psych majors, and she's my favorite prof of all time. If you care about the class content at all, take her. In class, she used engaging jokes, demos, and stories to help you understand, apply, and remember complex content. She prioritizes your deep learning AND wellbeing. She's the best!

She's alright! She mostly lectures near the computer though. Make sure you read the articles and do practice tests! The tests involve so much memorization so just reviewing the slides is not going to cut it. Go to the review session, do extra credit, and retake your tests! You won't regret it. I jumped from 2.6 to a 3.8 after retakes

analysis.name: Marko Madunic
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 106 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: never gives proper definitions and explanations for any concepts, he spends most of his time talking about irrelevant real-world situations that make the content 10x more confusing. have to go to useless lectures to see the answers to example problems because he only posts recorded lectures and answers to class problems 2 days before an exam >:(

Picture this: your parents are going through a divorce while you are taking this course and it affects your mental being so you can't keep up with the class.

Then you take the midterm because the tuition was alr paid for. You get the worst score ever and he posts everyones scores on the test to the whole class

This is the kind of professor he is.

I disagree with his tests being easy to study for. Usually practice exams alone are enough for me to get 4.0's in classes, but not this one. The actual midterm was so different from the single practice exam he gave, I'm not even sure what/how to study for the final.

this class is an easier version of ap stats. the lectures were a bit boring because i knew all of the information, but the prof was nice and i found him to be pretty funny. quizzes and exams are just like the practice ones he gives. the team activities did seem a bit pointless though, but they were easy and nothing to really worry about.

Great professor... don't really understand the negative reviews. His exams/quizzes are super similar to the practice exams/quizzes. You are also allowed notes sheets on which as long as you have the correct formulas it's really hard to get the problems wrong because they are almost always formulaic problems and not conceptual.

analysis.name: Natalie Naehrig
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 162 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Heard such great things about her so I took her class. I can honestly say she's not that great. During lectures she would mess up so much that even she wouldn't know what was right & what was wrong. I felt like going to class was pointless since I learned nothing during lectures. More of a self teaching class but the material isn't that bad
She isn't good instructor for 424. She is organized, but lectures aren't really helpful in improving your understanding in mathematical concepts.

Professor Naehrig is excellent. She carefully prepared videos before class to ensure that students learned the material. The lectures were very accessible outside of class time. She meticulously ensured that everyone could watch the lecture. You can earn extra credit if you actively participate. Midterm were easy, final can be a little challenging.
She really does care about her students doing well and thoroughly explains all topics. Definitely recommend!

Professor Naehrig is caring and passionate. She welcomes questions and wants her students to succeed.

I found the class very manageable, considering it's multivariable calculus. The content can be hard, but I felt prepared for the midterms and final. They were like the review material :)

I'd love to take another class with her!

analysis.name: Nikolai Tolich
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 113 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Physics is the hardest sequence at UW, it cannot be escaped. The professor doesn't even matter, the material is hard no matter who teaches it. Tolich is a caring guy and obviously knows his stuff.

Tolich is hands down the best professor I've had at UW so far. The physics course material is extremely difficult, but he manages to teach the core concepts in a clear/intelligible manner. Going to lectures, office hours, study center etc. will help you understand the topics covered. If you have the choice, I would highly recommend taking his class

He is very approachable and not condescending when asked questions about the material. If you give enough time to Smart  Physics before lecture and at least try the smart physics homework, you will stay on top of things and probably do pretty well in the class.

I took Daryl Pedigo for 121 and Tolich is much better. HIs lectures are better and he is a lot better at explaining concepts. 122 is a hard class in general and it moves quickly but Tolich does a fairly decent job teaching a hard subject

Professor Tolich delivers clear lecture. Lots of in-class quizzes and guiding-through examples. Based on my experience, while targeting 4.0, stay above 2 standard deviation over average on each exam and make sure getting nearly full points on all other things, you'll get what you want. Exams are based on homework and what you learnt in class.

analysis.name: Rose Novick
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Don't take her Ancient Chinese Philosophy class if you are not interested in analytical philosophy. She is understanding about late work and she is easy to communicate with outside of class (in that she is accessible, she is not particularly warm or approachable). Lectures were very boring and the concepts were hard to engage with because of that.

The lectures are really not interesting and I wish I had chosen another class for W credit. The readings are not long at all but you do get quized on them in sections. The TA gives the first 5 minutes of class for the quiz and if you are late you don't get extra time. I just wouldn't take this again, it is not that hard it is just so boring.

Her lectures are very boring and the homework is lots of reading but honestly the readings were decently interesting and when you go to drill section to discuss them it's never like a quiz. It's just talking among friends about weather you liked and agreed with it or not while making sure that you know what's going on and what the core arguments.
Prof Novick is a wonderful instructor and her lectures are both inspiring and thought-provoking.

Phil 100 is a great class which, I think, can never go wrong. Professor Novick's lectures were kind of dead but 8:30s (when I took it) can do that to a class. Overall the content was super amazing and sections were always tons of fun discussing the material. Great intro to Philosophy / Class is what you make of it.

analysis.name: Nicolas Wittstock
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Took him for PO141 at Boston U, lectures were very long but informative. some of the material seems like it's common sense, but the readings might make it sound more complicated than it is. to study just reread through the lectures and know the 2-3 most important readings, most readings are summarized in the lecture anyways.

POLS270 is a very intuitive and inspiring course for those interested in economics and politics. However, the problem is that I have always received no feedback regarding point deductions from the grader (I don't know if the grader is Nicolas or someone else), which provides less emotional support to students.

I loved Pol 270 with Nicolas as my TA! Teaches concepts incredibly well and knows how to expand on teacher lectures. Very responsive to emails and questions. Office hours were always entertaining and constructive :). If Nicolas is a TA option for your class, choose him!!!
For sure recommend. Really good TA - one of the best at UW in polisci

analysis.name: Norman Wacker
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Seems like a good guy and cares about his students, but the course was a waste of time.  Directions are confusing and he doesn't give due dates in advance.  Group work for almost every class meeting.  The few lectures we had were rambling.  He does give thoughtful comments on papers but ultimately doesn't provide a lot of insight

Norman is a very kind and caring teacher. However, for English 197 his wife taught the whole class. She made the presentations, led the class, and graded our papers. That would be fine but she isn't an English professor so she seemed unqualified. Every class had one to two discussions which we shared out loud. There are 4 essays with no prompts.

Typical class day:
1 bro stands right in the middle of the projector screen, facing it, reading each word at a snail's pace and making 2 mistakes per sentence
2 we consume some text
3 everyone reads their discussion post word for word
4 we get an annotation for homework
Felt like elder abuse, wife (whose first language isnt english) ran everything

Good person, but hindered cognitively so his wife essentially teaches the class. Could tell he was interested in content, but he just couldn't convey it verbally. The course was 3 essays, 1 poster project, annotations, in class activities. Fairly chill grader, especially if you go in person to classes, lenient on extensions, pairs well w/ bio 200.

prof has health issue. he slowly reads, shakes, and sits quietly. wife runs the class. It was not hard, but an odd structure given the prof.
Class was discussion posts, random calls, and annotations. hw was often short notice and essays were under-explained. repetitive assignments were unhelpful to my overall education. no main idea for the course

analysis.name: Margaret O'Mara
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Love her!! Aside from being a very nice person, she is also clearly very knowledgeable in the content she talks about making her lectures very interesting and enjoyable. Had a great time in this class, not to mention it was also very easy to pass! Currently looking forward to being able to take another class with her in the future.

I took her class three years ago and I really enjoyed it. I never did the readings and never talked in discussion session, but still managed to pull off a 3.7. Not sure how that happened. You will learn a lot of American History, though. The outlines that she provided at the beginning of each class were helpful. Study hard for the final.
Great instructor and very interesting class! Very knowledgeable and passionate about content, would absolutely recommend this class!

Ambiguous rubric/ no release of rubric to hold leverage over your grade.

when i die i want professor viray and her TAs to lower me into my grave so she can let me down one last time

I would recommend taking another professor. Her lectures sound as if she's reading them directly from the book. She has unreasonable expectations on tests. It felt as though we were writing proofs to theorems that we would learn in the next math class in the series. If you haven't been accepting into your dept, steer clear.

analysis.name: Vincent Schleitwiler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He structures the class as a typical lit class. Expect lots of reading, sitting through two hours of him lecturing, and two papers that show that you "get" the material. It's honestly pretty easy to zone out bc he's monotonous and doesn't engage students well, but he's very open to office hours if you need any help. Show up for daily participation.

Was looking forward to my class topic, but was very disappointed. The lectures felt endless, class was mostly listening to him go on about multiple diff subjects, only a few of which would seem connected. Outside of class was a ton of reading. The assignments werent difficult, but I definitely dont look forward to class. Would not recommend.

Vince is a nice guy, but his class structure isn't really effective: If you skip class twice, you could lose credit for class. Baseline grade of B+, need to complete lots of EC for a 4.0. SO MANY READINGS, and he basically recaps them in 2hrs. Daily reflection assignments. Everything marked either incomplete/complete. Easy for 300 but also dry :(
insane amount of reading, difficult to keep up with. the grading system is ridiculous, you can't see your grade until the end of the quarter.

This class is built upon discussions about the readings that were assigned, so it was difficult to understand what the Professor was talking if I didn't do the readings the previous day. His grading is labor-based grading which was difficult to understand at first, but if you just do all of the assignments on time it shouldn't be difficult.

analysis.name: James Wilcox
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 59 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: James is very engaging with his concepts and explains the topics in a way that is easy to understand, allowed me to fully grasp the content just soley by listening during lectures. James's lectures are not boring but indeed very interesting and almost like a story, it gets super intresting and made me love the class so much

I echo the sentiment of the previous reviews. You don't have to attend the lectures to do well in the class, but they're def useful for stuff that you don't really learn in high school. The grading's tough cause of the TAs, but if you use your resubs wisely then it shouldn't be much of a problem. Overall good intro course and James is a great prof.

I can tell he cares but the grading criteria is extremely unrealistic and his lectures are hard to follow as the class progresses because he rushes through topics and oversimplifies them (which we later faced the consequences for during project completion). The grading for the projects is absurd as resubs can hurt your grade even for minor errors.

Entertaining and engaging teacher during lectures! Although homework is graded extremely strictly (and I mean extremely), resubmissions are allowed once per week for assignments. This works well because there is typically only one assignment per week, so you can ace all the assignments if you get them right within at least one resubmission.

He is a great lecturer and is good at breaking complicated topics and explaining where they fail and succeed. He has significantly changed my understanding of how Java works. Homework is reasonable but get started early! You always know what to expect because everything is planned out at the beginning of the quarter, and rubrics are explained.

analysis.name: Joshua Vaughan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 76 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: wasn't a huge fan of the lectures, but the amount of outside help and support he provided was impeccable. try to read the textbook or you will be playing maze runner. quizzes were a time crunch, but managable with a reasonable amount of studying (3 hrs). idk i just rly liked him. he emailed me at 4 am after i emailed him at 3 am. why is he awake.

Dr. Vaughan genuinely cares about his students and shows it. From providing super detailed lecture notes, to answering discussion board posts late at night, to even holding an exam review session over a weekend, there was no doubt that he was willing to do anything he could to help his students succeed. I definitely recommend this professor!

He made things so unreasonably difficult. All practice problems given were much easier than tests. Although you didn't need coding experience, coding assignments were very difficult and little to no help was given, was told to google how to do it. Spent full lectures discussing his research then told us to learn topics on the exam via google.

Josh is awesome, if you have a chance you should definitively take his class. He teaches with such clarity and is extremely easy to understand. He really cares about you as a student and wants you to succeed.

Josh is so funny as he likes to blow stuff up, and he's very dedicated to teaching. But he sometimes went over unnecessary stuff in lecture and filled slides with long equations. The hw and Python do take a while, so utilize his office hours. The quizzes were pretty hard, but not impossible, but you def need some calculus knowledge for this class.

analysis.name: Xi Ma
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: 马老师 is one of the best professors I have had at UW. She has a professional attitude while maintaining a kind heart and helpful nature. Her lessons are concise and I think she has mastered the pacing of an introductory Chinese class. She is a generous and fair grader. I am lucky to again have her for CHIN 102, and I think very highly of her.

I knew no Chinese going in to this class so I was very nervous, but Ma laoshi is SO sweet and soft spoken, she was not scary at all! And she's very understanding, like if you have to turn in something late. It's a pretty fast paced class (I think all language classes are tho) but you will get used to it and it will get easier!!!

She's very sweet and cares a lot about whether you learn. It is sometimes easy to get lost during lecture, but she creates assignments that help you to preview everything that will be covered, so as long as you put in the effort, this class will treat ya well.

She is nice with grading on oral exams and on quizzes that are given 2-3 a week. Bit of studying required but it builds up as you go so things can get easier.
