Don't memorize pinyin for exams, characters are better in long run as it helps reduce chances of losing points due to wrong tone marks. She's very understanding about personal circumstances.

Xi Ma is one of the best professors I've ever had the opportunity to study under. I took the series of Chinese 101-103 with her and it has probably been the only class I will never regret taking student loans for. If you are at all interested in learning Chinese, I urge you to give her a chance.

analysis.name: Vivian Xiao
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's energetic, but talks for the whole class. 40% of your grade is exams where it covers all the previous content for it, but curveballs are thrown at you for the questions. Other 40% group projects for a final presentation, where you can only do it outside of class time. Marks you for the littlest of things. I would rather take other professors

Great prof well educated. Lectures are actually interesting. There are some clicker questions so you need to be in class or have a friend that will send u the link. One final presentation but not that hard. Just listen during the lectures and you'll be good.

I took her during her first year teaching, she was very passionate about what she was teaching but didn't have the best class structure yet. Midterm and final were online, timed, with multiple choice and free responses. The grading criteria was unclear and easy to loose points. She likes to grade to the hundredth of a decimal like 19.87/20.
She was great. Her lectures were super interesting! Her exams were pretty easy, the group project counts for a lot of your grade, but she was always happy to help.
Nice professor, young, energetic, humorous. Love her.

analysis.name: Fei Xia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She knows the content but struggles to convey the key concepts. Her frequent grammar errors make lectures even harder to follow. Slides cover a lot of content but unorganized. Homework instructions are unclear, and workload is excessive, seemingly ignoring that students have other responsibilities. I learned better from online resources.

Professor Xia is clearly very intelligent. However, I feel she has a hard time explaining concepts in lectures. For example- my class was very new to machine learning. Rather than framing the domain- we launched full long into a term long project, with little guidance. The same approach happened with each lecture (push forward regardless).
Very good professor. Sets a demanding pace. Sometimes the assignments include pretty tedious technical components around data ingestion and output, but I suppose that's good to have to do.
she is a great instructor who really knows the domain inside and out.
very good lecturer.  Learnt a lot from her class and I'm using the algorithms I learnt from her class in my job now!

analysis.name: Xiaowen Zhu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Xiaowen might be one of the smartest people at UW. She knows the material inside and out. All questions asked in-class were answered quickly and in a helpful manner. She is also helpful outside of class, has a fun sense of humor, and presents the material well (she relies solely on the whiteboard, so sit towards the front). I recommend this class!

Prof. Zhu is one of the best Math professors at UW. She is an amazing lecturer and has a good sense of humor. Her exam is very fair if you practice and do her assigned homework. When you have any confusion about any material, the professor and the TA are always available to help you resolve that confusion. Overall, Prof. Zhu is awesome!

Prof Zhu is so awesome!!! Currently tied for my favorite math prof at UW. Super funny and gives really good explanations. She gives step-by-step strategies for solving problems that are easy to follow. She spends most of class going over example problems that are very similar to what's on homework and exams. So so great! Would highly recommend!!

I loved MATH207 with Professor Zhu! She didn't follow a textbook; all content was taught via very information-dense, fast-paced lectures instead. Her tests (except the final) were pretty straightforward and similar to lectures. She seemed to genuinely care about us and was super nice and understanding, not to mention hilarious too, recommend!

One of the two best profs I've had in my entire life! Inspiring and super funny, she was kind and interested in student success. While she'd cover proofs and definitions a little, she mostly spent class time doing practice problems. You'd never see something on homework or exams that hadn't been covered in some way in class. She's so amazing!

analysis.name: Xu  Lu
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professor I've met in uw, she is so passionate in the class, and tries to make the lecture as clear as possible. Each of her lecture has a brief summary and some practice questions at the end. She'll also provide revision lecture before midterm and final, and also give some very helpful practice question. Only 4 very easy HW!

I believe this was Xu's first time teaching at Foster. She is very knowledgeable, but a lot of solo work is necessary to grasp the concepts of the class. Lectures were confusing and lacked interaction. Xu was very nice and I'm sure her classes will quickly improve.
Professors should have to take an exam or something to prove they can teach. If they did have one, Xu would not pass.
Take literally any other finance elective. Do not put yourself through this. Lectures are unstructured and confusing.

analysis.name: Xiangqian Meng
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: If you have a choice, do not take her. Prone to emotional outbursts, goes incredibly fast with minimal explanation, slurs words, heavy accent. 2 midterms worth 20% of grade each and final worth 35% so 75% of your grade is 3 quizzes. She is lenient with late work and seems to care about teaching, but shes just not good at it.

She gets confused at herself a lot. She gave three pop quizzes which were okay. Some of the questions on the midterm were like the ones she provided but there was at least one question that we never went into depth about. If you are okay with learning Calculus 3 on your own you will be fine. I would not rely on her. She is not sympathetic either.

Meng's lectures are in-depth but often struggle to actually impart any information on the students. There are quizzes on recent materials without notes or critical formulas provided. If you struggle with quick memorization it is very easy to fall behind in her tempo. Her accent (length as lens, etc) makes it tricky to follow unfamiliar topics.

I wouldn't recommend her. Her strong accent makes lectures hard to follow, and students must learn most material on their own. She may also put students on the spot if they don't know the answer, which can feel discouraging. This approach can make it harder to build a solid foundation in math.
for the love of God, avoid her for any class. her lecture is a waste of time

analysis.name: Dianne Xiao
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I don't have enough space for the praise I want to give this class! Prof Xiao makes orgo/inorgo super digestible and teaches in a way that makes her passion for the material evident. There are no trick questions on her quizzes, the TAs are amazing, she's an effective lecturer, and the assignments challenge you but are graded reasonably. 10/10 :)

I am seriously not sure why she has such high reviews for chem 312. She is such a passive aggressive lecturer and her quizzes are so difficult. She loves to have quiz questions that are not at all similar to the ones for her practice quizzes and picks out topics not discussed during class. The TAs were not very helpful either and very arrogant.

Prof Xiao had great lectures that were engaging and easy to follow along with. The class and the quizzes are hard but the content is really enjoyable! Attending her office hours is great to get more help with the material/ask questions. The only issue was that the 2024 quizzes were a lot harder than practice quizzes from previous years.

165 was worth the terrors of 145 and 155. Xiao made the curriculum digestable and enjoyable. I did not dread going to chem as I did in the past. The changes to the homework and quizzes lowers the stress of this class. I would absolutely reccomend everyone in the chemistry department to take a Professor Xiao class; she is awesome!

Prof. Xiao is a great lecturer-- answers questions very thoughtfully, organizes her slides neatly, and gives a lot of practice material. However, the exams are much more difficult than the practice, and this is very frustrating come quiz time. Art project was super fun, and this felt like a typical UW Honors class: basically a graded seminar.

analysis.name: Yael Midnight
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: You can get by without going to lecture because everything is posted on slides, however you should go to office hours to get the concepts explained and to work through the problems. Homework is a fair bit difficult and tests even more so. Your TA will be your saving grace so make sure to attend all office hours you can.

Prof is very enthusiastic about Econ but not the best at teaching it. Going to lectures definitely matters; all notes and some practice are posted to Canvas so there is content to study-- however, the final did not reflect this content well and was really hard. Overall course content wasn't too difficult but somehow the class was hard anyways.

Teaches basic concepts in lecture that are easy to understand, but puts things you've never done in your life on the exams. Studied more than I ever have for the final, and none of the problems were anything we had ever gone over in class or TA section. Provided us with 13 practice tests yet none of them looked like the final. Absolutely unfair.

Midnight's lectures were meh + prof has a grating voice. Textbook is written like an opinion article not an actual textbook. Way things were taught varied from book to lecture to section to homework to exam.
Previous exams vary greatly from what is put on these exams.
Not impossible to get a good grade but its a poorly designed course overall.

The first half of the course was well curated and easy to understand when work was put in, but the final was very hard and full of things we did not learn in class. I studied 15-20 hours preparing for the final and none of the questions correlated to the practice tests or the lectures. Do not take this class if you do not have to.

analysis.name: Yoav Duman
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Yoav was an amazing lecturer.  He is amazingly unbiased and presents material in a very organized manner.  Going to lecture and doing the readings are critical to success in this class.  He inspired me to major in Political Science.  I highly recommend Comparative Politics.

He genuinely cares about the topic he's teaching. He is very knowledgeable, and easy to approach if you have any questions. The class was almost like a history class LOTS of background information. Textbook is not necessary, just do the article readings, he'll explain everything else in lecture. Follow the study guide & you'll do well in the class.

I took an American Government class at Green River College and it was very interesting. The most important thing was showing up to class and engaging in the material. Not particularly difficult if you do the work. Instructor is interesting and understanding.

Amazing professor. He is from Israel himself and teaches the class in a surprisingly unbiased way. Presents all sides, always focuses on pros and cons. Exams are fine if studied for! Keep up with readings.

THE absolute best lecturer I've ever had, very very organized, really passionate about the subject (Arab Israeli conflict). He is thorough and clear, he organizes the class material chronologically so it all makes sense, and he explains cause effect relationships very well. no confusion at all as to what happened, when, and why it happened

analysis.name: Yutao Liu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very messy and disorganized hand writing, doesn't really explain what is going on and doesn't explain the true geometric understandings behind every concept. Extremely thick accent which makes it even harder to understand on top of his bad handwriting. I would say he is better than Koblitz but ideally avoid this professor if you struggle with math.
Prof. Liu was pretty good. I had him for Modern Algebra (MATH 402) about a year ago. He gave good examples in class and spoke very clearly. Overall, decent professor!

Not the greatest teacher I've had but I didn't really attend lectures. He has a strong accent and really bad handwriting so it is hard to understand what he is actually getting at in class. His tests are pretty straightforward although I failed the final so. he isn't great at explaining concepts or answering questions so wouldn't recommend.

lowkey this professor isn't that bad, his first midterm was based off of what we talked about in class. wish he would slow down during lecture but I just go back to the recorded lectures. 2 hw assignments per week including skills problems that are on completion, and conceptual problems are half correctness/completion. also has a heavy accent.

Do not be deceived by the good ratings on this guy. I had Professor Hoffman the quarter before for math 207, and I thought he was bad since everyone complained about his every day even though I good a good grade in his class. But Yutao made that dude look like an angel. 100% the good reviews are fake; this is the worst professor I have ever had.

analysis.name: Xiaosong Li
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 140 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Li is so funny and genuine. He makes his lectures fun, although he tends to skip through the "easy" material really fast. His tests are different than his practice tests that he posts online, pay attention to clicker sessions because those questions will be on there! Labs were easy and TA was a lot of help.

I think Professor Li is a solid choice for Chem142 especially if you have some chemistry background (he skips the easy parts). His tests were straight from his lectures and if you pay attention in class, you can definitely ace it. He puts a lot of focus on the tests, and he does demos a lot. His sense of humor is amazing. The TA (J) was cool too!!

This has been a terrible experience, from the past reviews prof Li seems to be a good & caring professor in person. But with the current circumstances of online classes he has been one of the least involved professors Ive had. Chemistry is a subject that should be practiced in repetition to master. With weekly timed quizzes learning is impossible.

Prof. Li is great! I found his lectures pretty informative, and he's not hard to follow (his accent is really not a big deal). He loves helping out students and his test review is basically the test - examples on his slideshows are really helpful too. I will warn you that the exams are tightly timed scantron exams and you need to be ready for them.

Li doesn't get enough credit. He genuinely cares that his students do well. He gave 15% of my class 4.0s and his love for demos made every class enjoyable. Yes, you have to study outside of class to do well but it's not so bad. Compared to other Chem teachers, Li gave out the least amount of work and the highest grades. He also bumped up our curve

analysis.name: Yang Song
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Yang is an engaging & funny lecturer that does an excellent job explaining the content. He is also happy to answer questions and truly cares that his students leave this class with practical knowledge. My only gripe is that 85% of your final grade is based on the midterm/final. Overall, he is a great professor and I would highly recommend him.
Great lectures, enjoyed seeing real world application and examples. Tests make up a significant portion of your grade but practice materials are sufficient.

Genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had. While participation was not mandatory, I recall that nearly everyone participated in a meaningful way because he made it interesting and engaging. Unfortunately, I have not encountered many other professors like him, so take his class if possible.

The class is incredibly easy. Three assignments and two tests. The tests are practically given to you, so curve is insane.

Prof. Song is a good teacher; however, he has a lackadaisical approach to learning.

Put simply, 460 is a little nuanced version of 350. If you don't have to take it, I would say take something more interesting.

Yang is absolutely hilarious, it is a joy to listen to every one of his lectures. His lectures are filled with stories, examples, etc- plenty to learn difficult Finance concepts. There are a few easy homework assignments spread out across the quarter, and the exams aren't too challenging either. Absolutely take this class if you are able!

analysis.name: Melike Yucel Koc
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Turkish is a hard language, but Melike hoca explains it in easy to understand terms! Very easy grader as long as you try your best. There is a lot of homework but she's very generous with giving extensions. Attendance isn't required but it is a language course so it is fast moving and you fall behind easy if you miss too much. Very caring teacher!

all of her assignments have no clear expectations, which sounds like a decent thing until u realize she doesn't have any clear instructions of the rubric (has no rubric at all) and she seems to grade based on how she feels - literally a lottery. she doesn't even tell u why u got the grade u did. no office hours,avoid if u can and take w better prof

Melike hoca is an amazing professor! she is so caring and she cares about her students. Her class is fun, she gives lots of extensions, and her grading is not harsh at all. You learn a lot from her! Definitely take one of her classes if you like learning about the Turkish language and Turkey

analysis.name: Yue Huang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: DO. NOT. TAKE. HER. Her lecture notes are borrowed straight from the textbook, are confusing, and she spends more time rambling than anything else. Quiz sections are amazing, but only because of the TA. Lectures do not align with the textbook, and I'm convinced she used ai on both her Midterms + the final. She does not care about teaching, AT ALL.

Dr. Huang was a top-notch professor. She is VERY knowledgeable in both MSE and big data/ML, providing relevant perspectives and avenues for pursuing this subject in academia and/or a future career. You can see that she cares for her students and their success, making herself available to help/guide them. I highly recommend her and this course!

Really enjoyed this course and Dr. Huang's teaching. I had a limited CS background prior, so this class really opened my eyes to a new world within engineering. The format (hw, hands-on, lecture, office hours) kept me engaged and interested, so I learned a lot. Awesome professor and subject, definitely take her classes if you can!
Luna seems closed off at first, but she really cares about her students! She tells you what you need to hear, and believes in student growth.

Her lectures did not make much sense as she pretty much read over each slide on her power point she got from the textbook. In order to succeed in this class, you actually have to read the textbook. Also, the homework assigned were not really relevant to what she was teaching in class.

analysis.name: Yomi Braester
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Not a super hard class, but insanely tedious. Lots of lectures, lots of assignments, and the professor seems to believe that this is the only class students should care about. Way too much work for a 200 level class, but the only actual hard things are the creative assignments cuz he assumes you have access to editing software (and friends).

I cannot express how ridiculous this class is within RMP's 350 letter count, but all I can say is while it is an "easy A," there is a LOT of tedious work. 2 hour lectures could easily be condensed to 45 minutes, and there are additional 2+ hour online lectures to watch in order to complete homework assignments. AI will be your friend for this class

Although an "easy 4.0", this class has been nothing short of miserable. Mandatory lectures that basically regurgitates information introduced in the mandatory several hour pre-recorded lectures. Weekly creative assignments that are tedious. Just a ridiculous set of standards; don't waste your time.

His lectures are super slow and annoying because it takes him an hour to explain a 10 minute concept. Can't space out during class either because he and his TA's like to randomly pick on people in class so I would do the readings and skip lecture. The whole class is on one Chinese director, which means a lot of subtitles and hard names.

This professor is oblivious to the fact that students only take this class for the A&H credit. He is so paranoid of AI, that he progressively makes assignments obnoxiously tedious each week, with the most unnecessary requirements like timestamps strictly from the Panopto recordings and refusing to post the in-class assignment question for students.

analysis.name: Shiheng Zhang
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He gave fair quizzes and good study guides. Homework was manageable. Sometimes hard to understand in lecture but he is happy to answer questions. He also explains how course material is used in his research which was nice.

Messy notetaking that was hard to follow in class and fully uninterpretable when not combined with verbal explanation. Which was made worse by his lack of recordings. Canvas resources consistently late and disappeared right after finals. 
Very harsh grading, including a 12% deduction for an arithmetic error on the final that never got regraded.

I found that the take-home exams don't always pertain to the content covered in class. Additionally, my TA is extremely harsh on HW grading. The class has a challenging grading system. While it is relaxed depending on the classes' overall performance at the end of the quarter, the most challenging scale is a 98.3% for a 4.0 and an 88% as a 3.0.

This was my second time taking a class with Prof. Zhang, and he's much improved. His lectures are clearer, the homework aligns well with the material, gives in-class extra credit quizzes, and his pre-exam guides are accurate and helpful. I wouldn't hesitate to take him again.

Zhang can be tough to understand, leading to me not attending the lectures often. He references the textbook in lecture so I ended up just reading from the book most of the time. When I took the class, there were only 3 take-home quizzes and a take-home final. I will say he's great one-on-one / in office hours.

analysis.name: James Zhang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 122 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Zhang, while a nice person, is not a good lecturer. He writes and projects while teaching which is extremely difficult to see even in the front rows of class, he is hard to understand, and clearly doesn't care much about the class. He has very few resources posted online and what he has is not up to date. His lectures are also not recorded.

Professor Zhang demonstrated a gentle, uncompromising devotion for the math that he showed in class. Admittedly, however, his lectures require some labor to understand - if you struggle in math classes, do not forgo the readings. He is also markedly old-school: he often opts to not use the microphone and diagrams everything by hand.

He seems to be a decent professor at the beginning of the quarter. But midway through, it fell apart for him. He crammed multiple lessons into one because he had to be gone many times throughout the quarter without planning for a sub, so it ended up with him giving us equations without really explaining what the equations do and how to use them.

He's a great person, not a great teacher. Things you need to know: 1)He is not easy to understand, you lose focus while he speaks especially 126 is different. 2)Exams are hard(different from students). 3)Quizzes are hard. 4)just doing homework not paying attention in class will not work. 5)although he's 3.9 now, do look for other prof for 126..

No Panopto recordings or slides from lecture so you have to be in lecture. Some might not like that but I prefer that to pre-lecture videos and it also forced me to go to lectures. Manageable class, just do Webassigns and you will be fine. Jolly guy, always smiling, put a smile to my face. Wasn't smiling when the final was excessively hard though.

analysis.name: Mark Zachry
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Teaching style is very fast-paced with little to no check-ins on student understanding. Lectures often are one sided. More structured delivery and periodic comprehension checks would greatly improve the experience.

Doesn't provide grades throughout the quarter on Canvas. Never answers questions directly and can't teach any of the primary sources in his own language and regurgitates quotes throughout the lecture without any clarification.

Top notch instructor with a class perfectly tailored to graduate work. He respects your time and intelligence and provides a well-structured challenge. I took him a few years ago and still feel the benefits from his class.

If you're in TC, Mark's class is the type of experience that called you to grad school. He edits one a premiere journal of our field, and his knowledge shines. He gives freely of his time within and beyond office hours.  When you're done, you will likely recreate your understanding of the TC field. Expect to spend 30-40 hours a week on TC 501.
The class is well organized and engaging, the readings are relevant, and the coursework is instructive.

analysis.name: Zhixu Su
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 80 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Taking Professor Su will be one of the highlights here, especially if you take her in Autumn. Lectures just fantastically organized, super clear notes, very helpful office hours, and overall just a wonderful human being who is passionate about math. Really inspiring work. Tests are difficult and more conceptual than computation, which I liked

Dr. Su was one of the best professors I've had. She puts students success first, you can tell by the way she gives lectures. Although this course is very difficult, her lectures and explanations were very clear. If you have the chose to take this course with Dr. Su, I definitely recommend!

This was my first math class at UW, and I'm so glad I picked Dr. Su as my professor. The course material was challenging, but Dr. Su explained it well. I definitely would not recommend taking this class autumn quarter because most people in this class already know the material and are try hards, causing the curve to be horrible.

Very caring and encouraging professor she really cares about you are doing in the class and goes over difficult topics again. Lectures can be fast but she revises the notes after and is clear. The homework and lectures align with the exams perfectly and her exams are very doable just practice and attend class. Best prof I've taken for math so far.

the goat! professor su has well written exams + reasonable hw assignments. lectures are a little slow but very thorough. she's also really funny and great in office hours, cares that her students are actually learning. super active on ed (discussion forum) and has office hours 3x a week. take 207 w/ her! she makes it easy to do well

analysis.name: Zoran Popovic
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: In case someone needs to hear this, it's not the worst thing to take a class with Zoran. If you're interested in the subject, you will enjoy the project content and appreciate some of his tangents in lecture. If you don't have the bandwidth to deal with Zoran being late or leading unorganized, questionably relevant lectures, then avoid.

Quite literally the worst professor I've ever had at UW. He encouraged the use of AI to build games, emphasizing quantity over quality, and then would proceed to mock students for random bugs in their generated games. Ridiculed games for being uninventive, but didn't bother to invest any time into teach us how to make inventive games. Don't take.
Constantly showed up to lectures late, didn't seem like he cared or wanted to teach. Good luck trying to get ahold of him. Would avoid him.

I want to preface by saying that Popovic is clearly very knowledgeable in and passionate about his field.

However, he does not seem to be very interested in teaching. He will get to class late and leave as soon as it is finished, and has no patience for "incorrect" answers/questions in class. I mostly learned from the TAs and external textbooks.

The class is about coding a video game from scratch: should be amazing, right? WRONG. The professor somehow takes all the joy out of it, publicly reprimanding students who do not adhere to his requirements that he does not state. Take literally any other capstone, avoid this one at all costs.

analysis.name: Abigail Harward
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: So far, I have had an amazing experience in BIO A 101: Human Biological Diversity: Sports, Movement, and Activity! This class teaches you so much about the human body and why we function the way that we do. Abigail is extremely helpful and passionate about the topic. If you take this class with Professor Kramer, take Abigail's quiz section.

analysis.name: Abigail Swann
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the most interesting classes I've taken at Washington. she clearly knows her material-- if you ask her a question she will give extremely detailed and helpful responses. There is a book for the class, but you can get by without it. She very clearly WANTS her students to pass, so if you're struggling, ask for help.

Professor Swann is a wonderful professor. She truly cares about her students and is clearly very knowledgeable about what she teaches. I'm an English major, so I struggled a bit initially, and she was so helpful and patient. I highly recommend going to her office hours; I found them to be very beneficial, especially for the problem sets.

I only leave a review to counter the bad one. This class is super easy, the textbook was a waste of money for me (I only read about 5 chapters), and Dr. Swann is excellent at replying to questions and clarifying during lecture. If you're looking for an easy and clear NW credit with interesting information, I recommend this class.

This course is pretty easy, but she asks way too many clicker-type questions that are worth whopping 20% of your grade. Then again, intro classes seem to cater to those who at least showed upShe gives about 20 seconds to answer for some questions and passes onto the next one, indicating some of them aren't even thought-provoking/discussion-worthy.

Professor Swann was an awesome teacher. I took her ATM. S. 111 class and loved all of it! Her exams are very straight forward and as long as you study the slides, go to lecture, and pay attention in class, you'll be fine. The only thing that I didn't like was that homework was worth %25 of your grade, so that brought my grade down a lot.

analysis.name: Abby Schamp
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Overall, it's a good class and Abby is clearly knowledgeable. Wasn't too stressful as long as you're okay at writing essays on time and did the homework. The HW is pretty easy, and any mistakes can basically be erased with extra credit. Lots of extra credit if you go to class.
Really passionate lectures and clear instructions. Her slide is easy to understand and got extra credit opportunities. (Although I took ECON 435 but did not find in "select course code"

Abby is so sweet and quirky! She genuinely wants everyone to succeed. Attendance was mandatory but her lectures arent the worst and she had us do activities. Way easier than the large lecture version imo. She only had us write one paper and do simple homework like four times. Make sure you study, and her office hours are super helpful!

Abby is a great teacher! Her slides are easy to understand and she moves at an easy-to-understand pace. Amount of work is totally reasonable. I went to all the lectures and only studied for a few hours before the midterms and was able to do well. Her fun personality makes lectures more engaging, especially for an econ class.

analysis.name: Zhi Lin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is a great artist, but not a great professor because he  is racist. I don't understand why he is so rude to Chinese students but he is also a Chinese! He would be a lot nicer to native students. I understand that he might have personal issues with racism, but having prejudice against students shouldn't allow him to be a teacher.
DO NOT EVER TAKE HIS CLASS!!! He was very strict and has discrimination on colored nations!!!

Should not be teaching basically. However, if you decide to take this class, make friends fast. Don't miss any days. Seriously. He will change things on purpose for the skippers. Don't expect him to email you back for anything period.

Zhi is awesome. He definitely makes you work for your grade but helps you significantly along the way. He may come off as blunt, even rude, but he is genuinely a very kind man who wants you to succeed and become a better artist. Try to look past the intimidating exterior and take in his advice/critiques. He will certainly make you a better artist.

If you are able to take critiques and know how to not be affected by words, you will like this class. Deeply, Zhi is a very nice person. He is very experienced in this field. Be sure to work really hard. Three hours per assignment is considered not lot of time. It can be from 4-15 hours.

analysis.name: Abhinav Gupta
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Worst professor I've had. Spotty coverage of complex topics. Extraordinary work load/minimal time allotment. Grading has been a disaster. Policy says "good" grade is 2/4 or 2/3 and grades aren't curved. So a "good" performance gets a D or F? Says wont know grade until posted on MyUW at end of quarter. I created this account just to rate Gupta.

I also created an account just to state that Gupta's been my worst experience at Foster. This site has usually been good for telling if a prof is bad, so I felt blindsided by how much this class has sucked. Loads of time-consuming busy work combined with horrible grading policies. Hopefully more negative reviews come in to actively reflect reality.

Lectures are limited (1-2 hours a week max) and really ineffective. Course is very "quantity over quality" with unreasonable grading expectations. Professor has a passive aggressive attitude - course starting off each lecture with what we are doing wrong as students rather than accepting feedback for his ineffective teaching. Last&Worst class at UW

Avoid if you want quality, fair, and rational instructor. Professor Gupta appeared like a nice guy initially but soon demonstrated his inability and incompetency of being an instructor. Directly told students that he has no time to grade their work during peer reviews. Instructed students to avoid giving high scores which encouraged grade wrecking.

Overall a great human being, but not a good professor. His lectures are extremely boring, and he has a horrible time management skill. Gupta will spend more than four hours on a 2h50min class. He told us that we need to care about our time management and be in the classroom on time, which is hilarious, that he never did his time management well.

analysis.name: Abed Shalabi
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Cool guy, bad teacher. There were multiple projects in which students were told to "look up a youtube tutorial". He's generally understanding if you don't have any prior art experience, but it is clear that he favors experienced student's work more. Absences and tardiness affects your grade. 3 absences is an auto fail.

The professor made the projects accessible for everyone including students with no experience, some of the assignments early in the semester were too easy, but it got better. The lectures really open my mind and made me appreciate art and understand it better
Be ready to have to teach everything yourself! I never really felt respected during my time with Abed.

analysis.name: Edmundo Aguilar
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class was quite easy. You're required to do at least 18 hours of volunteer work for the entire quarter. The class had interesting elements to it but I didn't feel engaged. Some of the work in class is quite repetitive but easy to understand. Edmundo is a great and funny person but I didn't feel like I learned much when taking this course.

He tended to go on tangents that didn't make much sense for most of his lecture time. There were a lot of assignments that were all essentially asking the same thing, and I don't feel like I learned much.
took 280 this quarter, he had an amazing TA and brought a lot of interesting views and communities to light.

Eddie is super kind and caring, you could tell he is in teaching for the right reasons. That being said the lectures always felt all over the place and a little awkward. I didn't really feel like I learned anything from being in class. Lots of writing assignments, which all were easy but felt never ending.

Was passionate about the topic, had great lecture guests that were also featured in the class content. Flexible with attendance but it's better to go in person. Option to do two credits for an extra project that wasn't too difficult.

analysis.name: Robert Abrams
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: 3 assignments: 2 essays and one PDF of a summary of each reading and lecture for every class. Don't know how much they are worth for the total grade. Lectures were interesting, but also hard to remain engaged. Prof knows a lot, but lecture can come across as rambling. Don't take if you aren't disciplined to pay attention.

Abrams was absolutely the highlight of Zoom class. He's super old school but clearly an expert in his field and great lecturer. Truly cares for his students and super easy to talk to. Syllabus and assignments were extremely accommodating. A wholesome, bushy-bearded, east-coast accented joy to talk Melville with. Unexpected gem of my time at UW!

Very smart and well educated in his field and it's obvious he cares as to whether or not his students are learning. As long as you go to class and pay attention and follow the readings, his classes are challenging but very doable and enriching. Talking and commenting on readings is very beneficial! Really enjoyed his class!

This is my second class from Mr. Abrams, and both experiences were excellent! Lectures are engaging and insightful. Graded based on two essays and a set of lecture summaries (1.5 pages per lecture). Abrams is very caring and fun to talk with after class. A few "rants" in class, but nothing that subtracted meaningfully from the class. Overall great!

He loves to ramble and while sometimes his stories make you chuckle, his rants make it difficult to follow; he likes to drone on and on. A bit creepy ngl ... I overheard him mentioning how he looked up a student outside of class. He's passionate and well versed in what he does though. I wouldn't take him again if I had the choice. He's a bit boring

analysis.name: Nidhi Agrawal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Nidhi was an approachable, energetic, and kind professor. Attendance is "mandatory" because you do activities in class for participation, but it is up to you if you care about those single-point assignments. The only other assignments were group project-based, so that was the bulk of the work. Tests were based on the lecture slides.

She was such a sweet professor! Every class had an easy participation element but a lot of it was groupwork where only 1 person in the group had to turn the assignment in. Make sure you have a good group for this class because you have group conversations a lot! But this class was easy, all multiple choice midterm and final.

she's really nice but her lectures can get boring sometimes. however, go to class to get all the class participation/assignment points. one thing is that her instructions (esp on the group proj) can be vague and unclear so make sure to ask her. would def rec taking w Martha instead.

She's incredibly nice and genuinely cares about her students' well-being. Every class, we had a worksheet that served as our participation grade, which was always done in groups. No midterm and final, instead we had two concept checks throughout the term and it was all mcq, fairly easy.

She's super sweet and bubbly and cares that her students are engaged and learning. Group project instructions can be confusing at times due to ambiguity, recommend talking in person for help. Overall an easy class if you come to lecture and study the slides.

analysis.name: Eric Agol
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Agol is nice, if a little shy. He will help students who reach out to him. Lectures are mostly clear, but also kind of boring (it doesn't help that class is 80 minutes long), but you don't really need to go to them because he posts slides w his markings online. I hardly felt the need to use the textbook, I wish I'd just torrented a copy.

Has a quirky sense of humor that is great in the middle of a lecture. Just an all-around awesome guy!! Class is simple, and still really cool. Simple math skills for the exams, otherwise, not much effort required and his slides are the reason to go to lecture, if you don't find astronomy interesting, that is. (Im a CSE major)

While the class content was pretty interesting, Prof Agol's unenthused voice made it difficult to stay awake sometimes. The work is generally very straightforward. I used a lot of quizlets online to study, and barely used the textbook at all except when the online homework directly cited when it would be useful.
Fun class with awesome materials. Nice person, but grading (in absolute scale, not curve) makes this class very difficult. Take astr323 when Gelco(Zeljko) is teaching.
The class is pretty straight forward; I'd recommend studying for testsquizzes, but they're not impossibly hard. Eric is a great guy, but his lectures are very dry.

analysis.name: Jameel Ahmad
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Jameel Saab is fantastic! He's an easy grader as well. If you want a GPA booster... take this class. Very fun!

Jameel Saab is an amazing teacher. I've never learned a language so quick as I did Urdu. His guidance makes the difficult concepts easy to learn without being overwhelming. Through this class I developed a love and interest for Urdu. Truly a wonderful class and Professor.

Best professor at UW. I love Jameel Saab and hope everyone interested in Urdu takes it with him!

He is compassionate and calm and most importantly very good at teaching Urdu. His knowledge and passion in the subject is extremely admirable, he truly cares about Urdu. He is also available outside of class and is flexible if things come up.

Probably my favorite teacher here at UW. Incorporated history into his lectures which I deeply appreciate and made learning a new language an exciting experience. This is coming from someone who couldn't read or write Urdu script at all and spoke it like a plebian. Very wholesome and caring, overall 11/10 experience.
Jameel sahab is my favorite professor at UW. He makes classes fun, interesting, and low key. I wish I could take his classes forever.

analysis.name: Khalid Ahmed
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: hes a great teacher, his lectures are very clear. makes jokes in class here and there. i wouldn't consider the class hard if you attend class and ask questions you don't understand and he'll  take the time to go over it step by step. tests aren't that hard if you do homework and readings, which aren't bad.

I love prof. Khalid so much, I'm in 102 right now and already dreading moving onto the 200 level without him. He is so funny and jolly and going to Arabic is easily the best part of my day. Khalid is very accessible through email and office hours and if you put in effort into his class, he's more than willing to help you succeed.

Starting a new language is intimidating, but Prof Ahmed is so fun and a really good educator. There's definitely a lot of assignments and work that goes into this class but it's manageable. He's always willing to help and does his best to make things clear and stress-free. Assignments come with feedback and you can resubmit for full credit.

He makes Arabic feel simple. So kind, funny, and believes in all of our abilities. He made me laugh at 9am pretty much every lecture. Daily homework but takes no longer than 15-30 min. Most quizzes/tests are online, and he preps you so well you won't feel too challenged. Put in the hours outside of class to really master the material.

This man is a literal angel. I took 101-3 with him and have never loved a prof more. I was having a really rough year, and he was the reason I was guaranteed to smile at least once daily. I could not imagine learning Arabic without him, and am sad that I'll have to go on doing so. Do yourself a favor and take anything he teaches!!!

analysis.name: Kamal Ahmed
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: About one quiz per week, two tests, three field projects, and two software labs were present. Each field project had a few labs. Eight homework assignments were due throughout the quarter. The deadlines for the quizzes were before the end of the lectures. I recommend opening the quizzes before the lectures start, so you can start them quickly.

Content of this course isn't hard but the prof makes it as hard as he can. All lectures are is him reading off badly-made slides that are a struggle to understand/sit through. No actual exam review material given. All content is reused every year, test answers are locked so you never know what you did wrong. No guidance at all for GIS/AutoCAD labs.

Gives decent lectures and explains concepts well, but his lecture slides aren't great and the canvas page is terribly organized. The grading weighting is also not great, like an in-class canvas quiz got the same percentage as a final project that we were given weeks on. All in all, not bad for 424.
doesn't explain how to use any software/programs so you just have to mess around with stuff or look it up in order to do half the homeworks. nothing is explained clearly. nice guy though

He reads off old slides and reviewing the slides outside of class is difficult, so pay attention in lecture! He doesn't give us any information about what will be on the exam until the day before, so there is little to no time to study.

analysis.name: Sama Ahmed
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Although this was Sama's first quarter teaching the course, his deep passion for teaching is evident during class. Lectures feel more like conversations between him and the students, and he makes an effort to learn your name if you participate by showing up and raising your hand. I highly recommend him for any of his courses, especially Psych 300.

While he is super engaging and hilarious in his lectures, he's not very accommodating if you have any disabilities or hardships. He is difficult to reach outside of class and lectures are not recorded. The syllabus is not clear either, the course is very quiz reliant, and he doesn't really communicate what weeks will have a quiz or not.

Great human being, one of if not the most engaging course that I've ever been apart of. Professor Ahmed finds every way to make the course as engaging as possible. He completely designed our class based around what we wanted and made the content incredibly interesting. Highly recommend!

The best! Super discussion heavy lectures where participation is very much encouraged, but Sama creates a very warm and welcoming environment where talking in class feels easy. Super kind and easy but thoughtful class where insightful learning is more important that quizzes.
I shouldn't have favorites but professor Sama is the best professor I've ever had.

analysis.name: Mal Ahern
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Mal is so enthusiastic and encouraging. I always enjoy their lectures. They are very knowledgeable and passionate; they really seem to want their students to understand and succeed. I struggle with understanding a lot of the content in Mal's classes, but I take them anyways because their teaching makes it so enjoyable. Highly recommend!

This class was very confusing for me, but Professor Ahern kept me invested in the coursework! I could tell that they were very passionate about the subject matter and were available to answer questions in person or online at all times. She explained things thoughtfully and thoroughly, taking extra consideration and respect for her students.

Lectures can be a bit boring sometimes, but they are informative for quizzes and tests. Try not to skip the class too much, as the lecture slides she provides would be useless without the context of the lecture. She is a really nice professor, but grading and email reply times can be frustrating. Be ready to take notes and review them before class.

I took this class for A&H credits as it was open for all majors. This class requires a lot of time commitment however, which feels very taxing as a commuter especially since it was a morning class. Weekly memorization quizzes in person first thing in the morning, along with a handwritten multiparagraph essay for both midterm and final was tedious.

In the middle of the quarter I was taking this class in, I got into a car crash and ended up losing my mother and Professor Ahern was so incredibly kind and empathetic. She made sure it was clear that my health and grief was a much higher priority than her class. She checked in on me multiple times and i'll forever appreciate and recommend her!

analysis.name: Ashfaq Ahmed
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great lecturer who tries hard to accommodate questions. Uses real-world examples from India and surrounding regions often while discussing topics, especially on populism. Super crazy looking blackboard notes, think red string map. Depending on the class's engagement, quiz section can be a delight. I look forward to them, but I do participate often.

Ashfaq was a really great TA. He went deeper into the topics from the book and lectures and he is a great source of deeper insight into important ideas. He is a very good person and he genuinely cares about his students and their success. Don't be afraid to go to him for help. He is super smart and I feel lucky to have had him to enlighten me.

Incredibly kind and open to all student's opinions (very patient). Extremely knowledgeable and is always open to questions, and always provides a detailed explanation when answering students. Sometimes it's difficult to follow what he's saying, but if you pay attention you'll learn a lot.
Very knowledgeable and cares about his students learning. Goes over topics well and is invested into what he teaches.

Ashfaq was a very kind and passionate teacher. He expanded on concepts in multiple different ways to help students who were confused. He was very excited about student questions and ideas and incorporated them into the lectures. I felt confident in his knowledge. I would take a class with him again and would recommend!

analysis.name: Sang-gyeun Ahn
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Worst professor I've ever had. Could've learned the same amount from a YouTube video. Consistently weeks behind on grading but also gives ZERO feedback on any assignments. Assignments are long and tedious and final (50% of your grade) uses none of the skills learned in class. If you're reading this you probably have to take him. Good luck.

Awful grader, an awful teacher, simply did not teach the class. It's required for the major so you have to take it, so prepare to not enjoy ten weeks with him. You learn maybe one or two things about drawing and the rest if not helpful. If you are already good at drawing you will be fine. Everyone else I wish the best of luck.

Prof Ahn is an incredible instructor. While communication can occasionally be a challenge, his expertise in drawing, CAD, and ID is truly unmatched. His passion shows through in every lecture and critique. Before graduating from UW ID, I highly recommend taking at least 1 of his classes, I promise-you won't find a professor who is as knowledgeable.

Incredible instructor. Was hesitant to take his class after reading reviews, but I'm glad I did. He's an exceptionally talented designer, and I am privileged to have learned from him. While the class was definitely intense/challenging, it taught me a lot abt design and the professional field. Prof. Ahn is not only funny but also genuinely caring.

Unclear expectations of assignments and extremely critical. If you do something different than what he would do, you get called out in front of everyone. Goes way too fast during "lectures," harsh even on beginners, and tends to copy some student ideas. Communication is just not there. Poorly facilitates and fails to provide a creative environment

analysis.name: Shannon Affholter
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This isn't even a real class. You pay $75 to buy a required "textbook" which is essentially just a bunch of videos someone talking to a camera. All the work is weekly discussion posts and multiple choice quizzes (sometimes twice a week which can take multiple hours), and a final project. Prof seems nice, and the work is easy, but it's a lot.

Hours worth of lectures to watch with often 2 discussions and 2 quizzes to complete every week. Way too much work for a 3 credit class, I spent more time on this course than any of my 5 credit courses this quarter. Wouldn't recommend taking unless you're minoring or majoring in RE

Didn't learn anything in this class, honestly learned more just doing my own research; not worth the money. The professor was also rude and did not explain course expectations accurately. Not an accessible course for everyone.

Professor was the textbook. Learned less than I would've by simply doing my own reading and research. Save yourself the time and money and just learn about real estate on your own time. Useless class.

Shannon is a-mazing!! Sometimes we would start our Zooms by jamming out to his fav songs. He had a mid-quarter survey and he actually listened to students and made the workload a little less. Such a caring instructor and was a ray of sunshine in this super sad pandemic time. Mainly everything is in Connect/ Canvas discussion. Good for real estate.

analysis.name: Afroditi Psarra
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Even if you try really hard, Afroditi will go out of her way to tell you that you did not try. Which is hurtful due to the fact teachers have access to see exactly what their students do on canvas, and for how long. Telling a student they arent trying without seeing that they spent three hours trying to understand the advanced readings sucks tbh.

The online class was structured really well with asynchronous learning, and all the class modules were really easy to navigate. I definitely put a lot of effort into this class and was glad to have done so, since it made her feedback a lot more specific and useful for me. Lectures were super important for the quizzes, and readings not so much.

Contents of the lectures are interesting, but the ways that she and the TA present are super boring and hard to understand. They could've just put the key points of the contents in the Power Point instead of just reading their scripts and letting us watch their face. Tough grader.

The class wasnt an easy A per se, but its definitely possible to get a high grade if you put in a fair effort. Lectures are kind of dense and its super obvious they are reading off of a script. Some of the assignments felt like busywork but overall the class wasnt bad.

You can tell she knows what she's talking about. I wasn't super interested in the topic, did minimal work and the class was easy. If you're interested in this topic I can only imagine how awesome it would be.

analysis.name: Afra Mashhadi
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This teacher is extremely condescending and unhelpful. She becomes defensive when our class brings up her shortcomings in terms of giving back our midterm grades on time. She is unclear, unorganized, and hostile. Heads up, the lab attached to 225 is a coding lab.

This was the worst and hardest class I've ever taken at UW. The professor is terrible at explanations and goes way too fast during lecture, and the TAs are condescending. I had to S/NS this class because the averages for the midterms were around 60%. Do NOT take this class unless you have to. For 3 credits the pain and suffering is not worth it.

This is the hardest class I've taken in my 4 years at UW. Most of theclass did poorly and had complaints/questions for her (which she did not address). Grading criteria were unclear all around. Day one she said "this is not a coding class" but surprise! that's the entire lab. Do not take this class unless there are literally no other options!

This is 5 credit class felt like 3 classes in one. The amount of work required is ridiculous. Lab was completely irrelevant to lecture, had to do R assignments in lab. While exams were heavily based on readings. She is the laziest and worst professor I have ever had. She recites the assigned readings, doesn't give out study guides and grades hard.

3 homework assignments, over 300 pages of reading, 2 midterms and 1 final. Test grades average around 60 / 100. The test questions are made by TAs who pride themselves on difficult questions. The readings are not clear and the lectures are quick while having little summary of the readings from the previous day. Professor is condescending.

analysis.name: Martin Afromowitz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Homework and midterms are moderately difficult, professor just goes over the textbook examples. My TA was terrible, so that didn't help either. I worked so hard in this class only to be killed by the final which was mostly on material that we very briefly covered in the last lecture...  Okay professor, difficult final exam.

Class size was around 20 people so his teaching style might change during the regular school year. He was a pretty good, never was confused on material went over in lecture, tests are alright. One of those professors that like to put a "thinking" problem on each test that messes a lot of people up. Homeworks mildly difficult. Study for his class.

Found this class relatively easy. His lectures made me sleepy. Concepts are fairly easy so you can learn from textbook and hw. The 2 midterms are reasonable and easy if you do the hw and study a bit. Make sure to get 100% on the quizzes as there is no partial credit for the problems. HW was mostly from textbook. Lab depends on your group and TA.

Lectures were clear but all he did was go over the example problems in the textbook so going to them wasn't necessary to pass. Concepts weren't too hard just do problems out of the book for practice. The 3 quizzes add up to 15% of your grade so don't mess up on them (no partial credit)

analysis.name: Barry L. Aaronson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Class is relatively easy other than the fact that lectures are 2 hours +. Prof is really passionate about the subject and knowledgeable about the topics. Class uses textbook that is on Canvas so it's free, there are three exams but one gets dropped. Overall, really good class that was fun, but it's a history class so it's long.

Genuinely one of the best professors I've had so far, super easy grader, and is passionate about the subject. There are 2 tests, and he drops the lowest grade for one of your tests. a lot of the credit is based on in-class video watching worksheets, so participation matters

Such a chill professor. The only actual "bad" part of the class is the length of the class in time (2 hrs) every Tuesday and Thursday. The classes are easy all you have to do is fill out one paper of questions as information is being given out or while you're watching a documentary/movie. He brought pizza, salad, and cookies for the last class too!

Barry is a solid professor. He provides the entire class with all of the notes you could possibly need, which you can just copy down. He encourages textbook, worksheet, and note use during all exams. All test questions are taken from students and the notes. He is an easy grader on worksheets and the final project. Show up and it's an easy 4.0.

Very thorough lectures, you can tell that Barry is extremely experienced and puts time and effort into his teaching. Open note tests and clear grading. If you show up and participate you’re golden. He’s pretty funny and entertaining too.

analysis.name: Angelica  Aamezcua
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: taking this course with her highlighted rightful terminology when ‘utilizing' languages/multilingualism from considering it as an valuable asset rather than a tool or a box to check off. she put got examples from the asian and latino community, giving grounding examples to clarify concepts. highly recommend to take a course taught by her

This class was supposed to be about the advantages of being bilingual but she only talked about Spanish/only gave Spanish examples. Was biased toward her own perspective, implying that struggles not related to race are somehow less valid. There were so many mixed/opposing messages, she makes spelling errors frequently and is somewhat unapproachable

Class was great in professor's Aamezcua's class. She tries to make everyone participate in class and generally cares about the students. Also tries to make everyone participate and always gives good feedback (although grading is a little slow) and is always accessible outside of class. Would recommend her class.

analysis.name: Aaron Wirsing
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Someone who's truly meant to teach. Participation/attendance is counted, but I found myself wanting to come to class each time because his lectures are interesting and his passion for the material is contagious. Will totally be taking more classes with him in the future if I can.

Dr. Wirsing is truly a god among men. I'm 4 years into my degree and he's the best professor I've ever had. Friendly, available, perfect Canvas layout, recorded lectures, balanced workload, clear rubrics. His experiences in research are both educational and incredibly inspiring. Also his vocabulary is massive, bring a dictionary to lecture.
Passionate and engaging. A professor you can not help but listen too.

Aaron is a great teacher! He has basically done everything ever and has a vast wealth of knowledge. You'll benefit from speaking up in class. Tests are straightforward, based almost completely on the lecture slides. Just come to class and you'll do well!

Aaron is a great professor, and he's got so many cool ecology examples he's worked on to talk about during lectures! It's hard to be bored in lectures, and discussion sections will really depend on how talkative your classmates are.

analysis.name: Aaron Wirsing
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures run long or into multiple days, labs are more lecture with little student input. Tests are 75% of the grade and 25% is attendance labeled as "participation". Tests seem clear but he grades strict looking for precise wording to get full or partial credit. He takes days to respond if he responds at all and office hour is a yap sesh....

Waste of time unless you need a class to nap through. Discussions are an extra 90 minutes of him lecturing without any useful information. Lectures offer little other than review from 100/200 level courses. Shares his opinion and rambles on with stories that aren't useful and wastes your time.

Good luck ever getting him to reply or meet with you.

Hands down the easiest class at UW. Have been thinking about majoring in ESRM after taking this. Lectures can be a bit repetitive, but he had good examples to explain everything and showed videos and whatnot. His enthusiasm for his field and research is awesome. Section and section work was easy and interesting, too.

Amazing prof and I love how engaging the lectures are! Loved hearing his personal experiences and many stories. I enjoyed how passionate he is about his work and if I have the opportunity I would love to take another class with him.

Dr. Wirsing is my favorite professor I've had! Wildlife isn't even my focus, but I continue taking his classes as his clear communication, approachable nature, and deep knowledge and enthusiasm for wildlife biology/ecology have kept me coming back. He is well-articulated and great at answering questions. Has done super interesting research as well!

analysis.name: Aaron Jamison
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: A teacher should be someone open to new ideas and a diverse array of opinions and students. Flint loves diversity of skin color but hates diversity of opinions. He was the most close minded teacher I have ever had. He thinks he is woke and open minded but is only able to see things from his own perspective. Complains way too much Not a good leader

Flint is insufferable. He spent most discussion groups crying about how he feels bad about being an authority figure/position of power, yet is a harsh grader, condescending, and completely inaccessible by email. Hypocritical, much? All the artists who he invites to lecture are similar to him (academic, conceptual) and the readings are difficult.

Currently on my third class with Flint and honestly I cannot say enough good stuff about them. If you want a teacher that will meaningfully change the way you think about AND create art then he's your go to. You have to be passionate about your work though and not looking for an easy A. Also his taste in music he plays before class is a big plus.

This entire class is based on attending weekly evening lectures at the Henry Art Gallery. If you're looking for an extra class that has an easy workload (and if you're free Thursday evenings), then this is for you. Flint is a cool guy, and you get free coffee and pastries for attending quiz sections.
Flint is pretty chill and has a really good sense of humor. I learned a lot from this class, mainly from the assigned readings.

analysis.name: Aaron Zhao
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great TA, makes effort to go around to every group to check in with your progress. INFO200, particularly the section, is project-based and Aaron not only gives good feedback during the section but is very accessible outside of class - especially before big deadlines. You're in good hands if you have Aaron as your TA.
Truly cares about his students, giving useful feedback to ensure you don't lose points when graded on group projects. Accessible outside of class via email and office hours.
Loves to take off random points when grading the assignments. Loves group projects so just hope you get a good partner.
He cares a lot about each student and just wants everyone to succeed! Always excited to teach and very down to Earth!
Lots of group projects with very clear grading criteria, but it is easy to get points taken off

analysis.name: Aaron Ottinger
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Aaron was a great professor. He helped us understand the material learned, helped us with our writing, and was a fair grader. Every class plan was made to make sure we were doing well in the class.

Topics were abysmal. He's rather an interesting grad student. He'll try to help you, but if you don't write it his way your writing isn't good enough. Would not take another class with him simply because his topics were boring and very uninteresting in comparison to what my other friends were writing about.

Really cool guy. I think he did a pretty good job teaching the fundamentals of college writing. He likes to connect other academic disciplines with English, such as philosophy and biology. Looks for improvement. Likes to philosophize, sometimes goes off on tangents, jokes often. Overall liked the class.

Aaron is the best professor ive had at uw so far. He is funny and obviously knowledgeable about the subject he teaches. His specialty is british literature, so expect a bit of discussion on that even if it isnt your assigned text. Very forward thinker, tries to get students involved.

Class/essay topics were not very interesting. Professor made the class worth while. He was really chill and down to earth and kind of funny. He talked about things that he did over the weekend on Mondays. Participation is 30% of your grade but you just have to say something once a week for the weeks points. I would take another class with him.

analysis.name: Behcet Acikmese

Did not stick to one book but bounced around several sporadically and diverged from book notation.  On occasion tried to bring the point home.  Very few examples. Stay away.

Lectures were full of useful and practical information, but the consistency in the notes and the varying math notation definitely made the class harder to follow. He does include reminders and (on occasion) summaries which are really nice.
Very knowledgeable about subject matter.

analysis.name: Acquanda Stanford
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: She does not give clear idea of expectations, grades extremely poorly, and spends no in class time relating course content to the assignments. Do not take her class!

She is very passionate and enthusiastic about medical anthropology. She tries to engage the class with materials learned in lecture or readings by doing different activities such as free-writes, small group discussion, and large group discussion. She genuinely cares about what students have to say about the course content/readings. Shes organized!

This teacher's teaching style is good but she expects a lot from students. You will learn a lot in class if you are serious, but if you think you can just pass without really trying and expect a good grade. You wont get it. She has high expectations and if you work hard you will do well and learn a ton about writing. being there is required.

She is not very helpful at all in class. Assignments don't instruct very well at all. Will get on you for talking too loud with a classmate when doing a peer review with that person. Also knowing that she said its okay to talk. Overall just not a great professor with bad communication skills with her students. Also teds to miss class a lot.

Papers have little to no direction and you must follow her writing style or points will be deducted. Overall one of the worst english classes I have taken at UW. She's more worried about making sure the students know she is a feminist and breast feeding activist than teaching how to properly write an essay. Unless you have to, do not take.

analysis.name: Chethana Achar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

She is articulate and a good teacher. Is accessible outside class and helps understand course materials.

Chethana's class is well-structured and has appropriate course load. You can get an A if you pay attention in class and follow guidelines. She has an intelligent+dry sense of humor that I found engaging in class. There is a lot of group work, but she is very liberal with grading those.

analysis.name: Tom Ackerman
