Ackerman is an awesome guy. May be a little intimidating at first, but really a good guy all around. Go to the extra credit he offers, it will really boost your grade. Overall, class was easy but you need to put in a little effort.
He's really nice and really fun and really good at explaining stuff.  class was awesome and interesting.

analysis.name: Rebecca Aanerud
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Aanerud is awesome. Her lectures are interesting and worth going to. My only complaint about the class was my TA. The Friday sections are mandatory, making it hard to avoid wasting that time. The exams are easy, however the written assignments are graded on a "how you improved" scale which was rather ambiguous. But overall a great class!

Professor Aanerud is an awesome professor! Her enthusiasm in the subject really showed when she taught the class, and it is because of all that she has experienced that she is able to teach the way she does. Her tests are really not that hard, just attend lecture and she'll basically tell you what's on the exams (1 midterm, 1 final). Life changing!

Rebecca Aanerud is one of the most wise and fabulous teachers I have ever had.  She is inspiring and I took every class I could from her.  I learned so much from her and her classes have forever changed me for the better.  She has a powerful and quiet way of bringing everyone into the dialog and a patience with learning and a desire to reach you.

Easy class, though the grading system is a little ambiguous.  Lots of reading, and lots of pretty dense texts, but the lectures cover a lot of what is needed for the quizzes. Dr. Aanerud really tried to make everyone in class happy, which I thought actually might have hurt the class a little, because it wasn't structured enough, but a good class!

prof. Aanerud is such an amazing profesor. Her lecture is well organized and teaching style is effective. Her senior level course is very well structured and all the readings assigned really make me think deeper on intersectionality of race, gender, class, sexual orientation,etc. I am super sad this quarter has ended because i admire her so much!

analysis.name: Adam Leaché
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: He isn't a bad professor, just don't think this is an easy class. It's a lot of content to memorize and apply. There's no homework so the only things that count are quiz sections and tests. The tests can be hard, not a lot of practice material for the exams. Overall I didn't expect the class to be that much.

The class is alright if you make sure to show up to lectures and quiz sections. His practice exams are mostly irrelevant because he switches up the contents of the class often. He is nice but a not personable.

He reads from his slides a lot, but his lectures were fairly interesting (especially compared Dr. Janneke Lambert who taught the 2nd part of the quarter). He seemed to care about whether the students learned. The only thing that really irked me was that he posted his notes 1 hr before class, so I'd have to run to Ode to print them between classes.

Professor Leaché's lectures were straightforward. Anything on the lecture powerpoint is fair game, including tables. Class is boring at times, but memorize the lecture slides and pay some attention in class and you'll get a good grade. Quiz sections don't require much effort either. I would recommend BIOL354, specifically with Leaché.

He's a really good lecturer and has a good sense of humor. Be sure to be on top of your reading because he does random call-outs and you want to be prepared. The tests are tough, you HAVE to know your stuff inside and out because the grading is really strict and you have to get everything exactly right in order to get a good score.

analysis.name: Adrian Salguero
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

He is a good professor that genuinely cares about his students.
His lectures are very clear, and his grading criteria are not strict.

analysis.name: Adam Moore

This quarter has made me seriously reconsider staying enrolled in the MSIM program entirely. Such a waste of money.

This course provided zero value to my degree or career. The material was completely irrelevant to my career. The exams were deliberately obscure and inaccessible, making it nearly impossible to demonstrate actual understanding. This quarter has made me seriously reconsider staying enrolled in the MSIM program entirely.
Online summer class. Totally chill asynchronous, everything was set up ahead of time, so you could work at your own speed.
Solid all the was around.  Well built class, not overworked, and provided lots of feedback.

He would always give some pretty interesting examples of philosophy with regards to how it can be applied. Class wasn't too bad, you end up studying off lecture notes instead of doing the reading. Exams were kinda tricky where, "all the answers were false and you get worried." Oh and the class wasn't curved so you have to work hard to that regard.

analysis.name: Kemi Adeyemi
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class was hard because the readings were difficult but also because it challenged a lot of my thinking. I thought I understood queerness pretty well before but the class sort of exploded my ideas about it, which I actually liked. It wasn't hard to pass, and assignments were fun- final was a card game- but it really made me think.

Prof. Adeyemi's really funny, smart, and nice, but by her own admission we were reading graduate level texts by the third week of INTRO to queer studies. The class is way too advanced for an intro class, which led to a superficial understanding of complex topics and made me feel like I was trying to catch up constantly even though I wasn't behind.

I actually took her for GWSS274 but it won't give me that option.
She is amazing!! Her lectures were super engaging, she always answered questions thoughtfully, and her assignments were creative and intellectually stimulating. Would totally take a class from her again.

Dr. Adeyemi is probably one of the smartest prods I've dad the pleasure of having. She tries her best to help you understand something that doesn't make sense, but also relies on the class a lot for their opinions, as this was a seminar/discussion style class. She keeps it real and is passionate about what she's teaching. I would definitely rec!

This professor understand students. She relates and understands how important mental health. 2 hour lectures are tough but you do get a short break in between. Kemi is open to question. The readings can be a little long but doing them helps you follow along in the lecture. Attendance was optional, but the lecture really is important for passing.

analysis.name: Adam Drewnowski
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: NUTR classes with this guy are incredibly chill. You pretty much get 4 homework assignments (for the whole quarter!), 10 minute quizzes (which is usually 1-2 straightforward questions on lecture or reading. He's a funny, wise old owl type of professor. Highly recommend! Incredibly reasonable too which you don't see much at UW. You won't regret!

Good lecturer, but I found his assignment requirements to be very confusing at times. However, it was a good class and I learned a lot! His pop quizzes are the 'minute quizzes' which are two questions long and quiz you on readings. There were 4 assignments overall, which were graded pretty easily.

Ok so the class wasn't that challenging, but it became harder because professor Drewnowski lectured for almost 2 hours in the most slow, tiresome and dull tone. He's so kind, but I couldn't even sit in class or attend lecture after the first week because I couldn't pay attention. The class was interesting itself, but the teaching was not good.

Dr. Adam is a very specific person; he is adorable and very knowledgeable. The course is a little disorganized but very interesting. His lectures can feel very long, but if you are willing to collaborate during class, it makes them much better. He is a little slow with technology but really tries his best for the class.

Interesting class materials. He also invites a lot of people to give fun guest lectures. Only 8 small quizzes given unannounced in class, so attendance is pretty important.  There are 4 writing assignment in total, and his TAs gives really good grades on them. I almost got all hundreds on them. Recommended!

analysis.name: Adrian Andelin
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: At some point, you will realize that he doesn't know what he's talking about. In class, he seems to be knowledgable, funny and approachable, but towards the end of the quarter, you'll know what I'm talking about. He doesn't accept alternate answer even though his answer is DEFINITELY wrong and if you don't see him reply to your email -> rejected

Great teacher, kept classes fun, very clear on what your grade was on, transparent on grade logistics, exams are vocab-heavy, but as long as you study them there won't be any surprises. Overall a very nice and informative class! Also drops the lowest test grade (and for other categories), and there was a lot of wiggle room for your grade.

Loved the professor; he was clear, and you could tell he really understood what he was teaching. The class itself was very note-heavy, not a fluff class. You'll want to actually read and take notes on the textbook and the lectures. Quizzes allowed one note card, but even then, you really had to understand the material. Regardless, I loved the class

He is absolutely amazing and you can tell he loves what he does and cares about his students. The content of his classes is very daunting and can be difficult, he explains things great. This class can be tough and require a lot, but he drops a lot of assignments. The biggest assignments are multiple-choice exams, but he gives detailed study guides.

Adrian was super nice, however it was obvious how desperate he was to be liked. His lectures were interesting but it was obvious he read the book last night and was just going off of that. Sometimes, I felt as though he didnt really understand the experiments he was explaining to us. Also, he never shuts up about his dog.

analysis.name: Stuart Adler
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Before I took this class I had a cactus and a girlfriend. I spent so much time doing HW that my girlfriend left me for an art student and my cactus died from neglect. I'm more neglectful than a desert.

Flipped classroom approach: comprehensive and clearly articulated video lectures supplement reading assignments and give you everything you need to solve weekly problem sets. Exams count for most of your grade but are straight forward and well represented by problem sets. Very responsive to questions. Great environment for learning the material!

His self-described "Socratic" method of teaching just means his lectures are SO boring. With his soft quiet voice, I know for a fact it wasn't just me that would fall asleep during his lectures. Homework and tests were tough, but not impossible. He couldn't make me care about the subject, even though thermo is really interesting on its own.

Beware! Stuart Adler exams are incredibly difficult and you may or may not have enough time to completely figure them out in 50 minutes.   They are so tricky and unlike the textbook, it is not even worth studying for them in the traditional way (like "practicing problems")... BUT you better hope you understand the concepts.

this class lowkey sets you up to fail. his lectures are on youtube (which are 7 years old by the way), and that is his primary source of teaching. to compensate for that, he assigns a LOT of homework (individual, group, and quizzes before the start of the week) and readings. overall: difficult to understand and does not put enough effort to teach.

analysis.name: Adam Summers
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Just don't. The 3 and a half hour lecture should've already steered you away from even thinking about the class. Not an engaging lecturer, and the homework is pointless. It's an easy A but at the cost of extreme boredom. Kinda surprised the university even lets him keep teaching this course? Also  got marked down sometimes for stupid things so...

My favorite class until I lost 8 points on homework due to a Canvas issue and went from an A to a B. I reached out to Adam, who replied rudely, accusing me of lying. I showed him canvas grading and grade calculations done by hand, showing how 8 points tanked my GPA. He then ignored my emails for the rest of the class. Ridiculous grading

I am shocked by the bad reviews. He is really enthusiastic, his homework did not take long at all as long as you took notes in class and the grading is so damn fair.  This class was the lightest class of my whole STEM career.

Summers is very knowledgable and an overall nice guy. HOWEVER, each weekly homework/essay writing assignment will take you 5+ hours to complete and the only feedback you will get is a number. No comments at all. Then when you email them to ask why you got that grade you'll never get a response. Class is interesting but the logistics need work.

not really accessible outside the class. have many poll eve questions nonrelevant to class materials. be prepared to take a four-hour class with five minutes break. he has tons of calculation questions. and no feedback for homework. does not have a grade scale in this class, so be ready to feel confused when you are anxious about low graded dues.

analysis.name: Adair Rounthwaite

no. just no. unclear materials harsh grader bad feedback and boringgggggg lectures. if you are not interested in art, do not take it or else you will be so bored. only graded by a few things so if you do bad then sucks for you. also tas don't really help much

You can tell he's trying really hard to get students excited again for biochem after his sorry teaching partner. Tests are super hard but it is a 400 level class so its understandable. I like him. Keep it up.

Dr. Ailion loves what he does and it shows. He really cares about the material and wants you to think like a scientist (a lot of test questions are highly hypothetical). Watch the video lectures - they are very engaging. Lower exam averages but the questions are genuinely interesting imo.

Partner professor was not the best lecturer this quarter. However, I wouldn't just blame the partner Professor. I think Professor Ailion could have stepped in and helped make the course better. Taking this class after BIOC 405 was upsetting.

It is a 400 level course so i totally understand why this course is hard. What made it even harder is the lectures. I felt like I wasn't getting enough information, and the exams were a lot more difficult than the lecture content.

He's funny. He sounds like a decent guy. He seriously needs to work on his presentation. I don't doubt his knowledge but most of his slides are just empty. No clear explanation of what's going on. Whatever comes out of his mouth doesn't really help much either. Exams were ridiculous. Considering how much he teaches you in class, he expects a lot

analysis.name: Caitlin Ainsley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Really, really smart professor, and genuinely wants you to learn. Highly recommend for anyone who wants to learn R!

Caitlin goes above and beyond to craft engaging lectures that convey complex subject matter in a digestible way. The examples she uses are extremely useful and easy to remember, and her lecture slides are the best I've ever seen - posted online with links to each subheading making them easy to return to when exams come around. Absolutely recommend!

Professor Ainsley values her students learning and chooses to structure her curriculum in such a way that prioritizes active discussion over heavy coursework. That being said, this class really depends on your group involvement; you are split into breakout rooms every class and those groups go on to work on research projects. Highly recommend!!
Talk too fast and doesn't change her tone at all... Materials are way too easy than my expectation which makes taking this class a waste of time.

Very organized. Professor Ainsley did an amazing job of getting students to interact & collaborate via zoom with a very well-designed structure for lectures and class discussions. She is extremely knowledgeable and intelligent but genuinely interested in your learning, so the work is challenging, but she is supportive and encouraging!

analysis.name: Aimie Shaw
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Yassss gurl shes the bomb shes just an awesome french teacher. shes got a little attitude to her sometimes but it's not bad just don't be one of those retarded students who is annoying. She's Canadian and talks about it a lot it seemed like. She says "about" funny. But she's pretty gucci overall would rate 10/10. Hate the book and online work.

Aimie is a solid choice for learning French.  She will cover all the things you need to know for a test and the things you should know if you're traveling to French speaking countries.  She also provides handouts with a quick run down of new terms/ grammar / etc.  She's a very organized and thorough teacher.

Shes aweeeeeesome! She explains everything throughout and always makes sure you're on track. She's never rude (maybe because she's Canadian). And she pretty much makes the class as fun as possible with as much information as possible. She will cold call on you so be prepared, if you don't like to participate in front of the class, skip this prof.

Took her class  back in 2014 at UW Bothell. It was BIS 390 Special Topics - Francophone. Anyway, she was fairly new then and didn't have a rate my professor yet. She made the class fun, though the writing and tests were brutal especially if you did not read the book. There were class discussions about the book too. So make sure you read guys!

Aimie Shaw is an amazing professor! It is always a struggle to get a French teacher that has a good accent, is patient, and covers all of the course material well--and Mme Shaw met all of that criteria! I feel like she genuinely cares that her students learn and enjoy the class. There was homework assigned almost every night, but it was easy.

analysis.name: Aine Heneghan

Also she sends all class materials by email to be printed, often times late at night.

Excellent instructor. She's very passionate about the material.

She's very passionate and no nonsense.  Her classes are well organized but move quite quickly.  If you don't have a decent grasp of the material to begin with, you'll have to work very hard to keep pace.  On the other hand her explanations are good and she's quite patient outside of class.
She is very tightly wound, but a great teaher and she is really really passionate about what she does. She is also one of the top Schoenberg scholars in the world.
She's demanding at times, but passionate and clear. She is highly available to her students and actually wants them to succeed.

analysis.name: Akshay Gadre

review_highlights.comment: Majority of the class complained about the prof during the Mid-course evaluation. Imagine learning calculus but the professor never shows you how to evaluate a integral. This man should not be allowed to teach. HW was so hard because he taught close to nothing in class. Shows you a bunch of random equations and expects you to apply it somehow on the HW. Class is easy to pass but don't expect a high grade whatsoever. I would avoid him if possible.

Professor just reads off slides most of the time. Example problems were rarely done by hand and instead were put on power point with some of the steps skipped.  Lectures felt like a complete waste of time.
Really nice guy and accommodating but his lectures were almost impossible to follow. Tests and HW were pretty hard since the lectures were hard to interpret so expect to look online for help
Very difficult to follow the lecture. Both labs and lectures are difficult. Tests cover homework materials that are due three weeks from the exam date.

analysis.name: Akio Takamori

He is kind and encouraging, but also helpful and honest about your work and ideas. He isn't overbearing and is a great person to simply talk about art with. Is also pretty funny in his own subtle way.

Great prof!He's really funny as well.He's very humble and kind. I highly recommend the class. It's creative and fairly easy although it's a little time consuming but other than that it's one of the best classes I've taken so far.

Akio is my favorite professor ever. He is truly interested in helping his students learn and improve. He is humble despite his achievements as an artist. He will take time with students and actually teach techniques.

Fun fun fun!!  He teaches you the basics and then lets you use your imagination.  He's picky about cups (since he had to do hundreds of them a day when hew as in Japan), but he's fun and a great person to learn from.
Akio is wacky-packy! He has lots of interesting things to say and he's funny. During critique, though, I definitely get more nervous with Akio than with the other two.

I had Iwata for lectures, but never for section. I thought she was a really good lecturer and was surprised by these ratings. I had her for Japan 301, not 201. She was an amazing teacher and really cares about her students learning. Definitely the best professor I have ever seen in my academic career. She was very reachable, flexible, and she had asked us if we were doing OK when we missed the deadline. 

She CARES about her students so please never hesitate to ask for help from her. 

I hope I can be a professor like her one day.

I did not find her teaching style effective at all. I felt that she emphasized on things that were not really important so that we can really learn and enjoy the Japanese language. Too grade conscious.

analysis.name: Anne Kalkbrenner
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: One of the sweetest professors! You can tell she really enjoys what she teaches and she always comes to class with a really positive attitude!

This class was tough but the professor was amazing. She's so passionate about the subject, it's inspiring. Definitely use the study guides even though it's online. The tests are tough. Overall, I would reccomend the class. It was super interesting and Professor was genuinely such a great teacher who actually cares.

By far the nicest and most caring professor out there. She deeply cares about each student's well-being. You should attend class because there is a group assignment each time but they are very fun and straight forward. She is always very positive and wants each student to succeed! perfect intro to the nursing major!!

probably one of the most passionate and caring profs I've ever had. I loved listening to her talk. she was so engaging, patient, and took time to get to know us. would have her as my prof 100 times over. loved it!
Anne is a great professor. During lecture, she is always sweet and she cares about all the student during lecture. I recommend taking this class and this class is easy.

analysis.name: Alec Kroll
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 74 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: KROLL IS THE BEST PROF I'VE HAD AT UW. The friendliest man on earth, go to office hours, it's a fun time, and you can tell he cares about his students. I learned a lot because his lectures are bite sized and conversational. He knows what to say to make the info stick. He's so passionate and has inspired me a lot, I'm now considering a chem minor.

Took Kroll for all three gen chem courses (142, 152, 162), and he was my first STEM professor. He's a great professor, teaches well, and actually cares about his job and his students, which isn't too common for weed out courses like this one. Tests aren't too bad if you study, and he doesn't curve the course so no one else's score impacts yours.

I took Kroll for Chem 142, 152, and now 162. I don't read the textbook because it's much easier to digest the information in his lectures. To do well on the exam, review lectures & do the practice questions, concept tests, and quiz section worksheets. Although I didn't meet him outside of class, he seems like a good person and cares about you.

I've taken Kroll for 152/162 and I can say that his lectures are way easier to understand than reading the textbook. I gave up on reading and only attend his lectures now, and it's made my life so much better. His tests aren't super hard but not easy at the same time. He will totally answer your questions, so ask!

Kroll is a really kind professor, and he cares so much about chemistry that his excitement really carries through into his lectures. He explains things really well and he gives a lot of examples in his lectures. His tests are really fair, too. At the end of the last lecture for CHEM 152 the class burst into spontaneous applause for him.

analysis.name: Alexander Mamishev

Extremely confusing google sheets system for course organization and subjective “XP points” that count for 24% of the grade.

This is the most disorganized and confusing professor I have ever had. None of his "lectures" were structured and were mostly either irrelevant rambling or taught by TA's. He speaks like an ancient god and his headphones are his true identity.

This class often left me speechless, laughing in disbelief, and learning more from nyt games than anything the professor ever taught us. I have never met anyone who worships chatGPT more than this man which would have been funny if he weren't a communications professor. I called this class Rage Bait 101, and it lived up to that name all quarter.

analysis.name: Ali Karimirad
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style

Stay on top of assignments, watch the pre-lecture videos, and use the resources to do well! 😊

Not a great lecturer, hard to understand, and tends to go through his slides far too quickly. The problem sets take forever, and many of his questions tend to be worded strangely. first module of the class was very easy, second and third modules were quick-paced and much more difficult. his lectures were confusing, but the textbooks helped. class was not the worst if you made sure to keep up, but exams can be harsh as they're not worth many points. did a good amount of self-studying because my TA was not super helpful

Nice guy, taught all the material well. Participation not required, but recommended as it counts for 5% of your grade (polleverywhere). 3 main non-cumulative tests that are pretty hard and only have one practice test each. I didnt read the textbook, not necessary. I recommend going to lecture, quiz, and watching the videos for a good grade.

Ali was a great professor for this class, especially because he was good at explaining the content in detail without brushing over important parts. Attendance was mandatory through poll everywhere, but there were some you could get dropped. The tests were difficult for some people, but I found that if I studied ahead of time they weren't that bad.

analysis.name: Alex Anderson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Alex is literally the nicest professor ever. This class was so easy and definitely a GPA booster. Although the lectures are long, it is WORTH IT! There are 4 online exams, open book and there are 2 assignments which take like 5 minutes each. Plus it was interesting learning about the buildings of different civilizations.

It's two discussion posts a week. Two homework assignments the entire quarter that are maybe an hour each. The videos are actually interesting and like 5 minutes long. I got literally full points in this class without the textbook but it's technically there. Tests are all open note and online sooooo

This class consists of discussions, super easy quizzes with unlimited tries, readings, a few assignments, and a few tests. You can get extra credit by doing more than the required amount of discussions. Personally, I thought this course was quite interesting, but it is very history and architectural design elements heavy, which may not be for all.

Arch 150 was really chill class. You just do the discussions and modern focus quizzes on canvas for homework. Take notes on canvas lessons consistently because they can stack up and that wasn't pleasant. There's textbook but it's useless. Study buildings on study guide before tests. Overall, 100% manageable.

Professor Anderson is a very knowledgable and passionate professor who really cares about student learning rather than just grades. Class is very easy if you review the lecture slides before quizzes and complete the assignments.

analysis.name: Naomi Alterman

review_highlights.comment: Naomi was a pretty decent professor. She was funny and explained concepts decently well but the exams were challenging and I often felt very out of my depth on homework. Expectations for homework were a bit unclear and the instructions were frequently quite confusing.

Lectures were good, definitely learned a lot in this class. Gave 3.0 instead of 2.0 because Naomi was very active, detailed on edStem. Class was easy except for the final.

analysis.name: Alexis Drouot

review_highlights.comment: MATH 318 - Fantastic lectures; showed up to lecture every time to hear his beautiful French voice. Lectures will make you love lin alg. Even though technically not proof based still try to understand the logic behind all the proofs anyways as they WILL show up on exams.

This is for 394. Does not record lectures, makes it impossible to find and understand material, tests very hard as well. Note its 10 percent HW, 25 percent per 2 midterms, and 40% for final. If you get a bad grade, definitely drop the course as it will screw your GPA

Do not take his math 394. No recording and no homework feedback. He didn't even want to bother himself with providing the content of the homework questions, only left with page numbers. You will need to buy the textbook and read the questions yourself. The "most responsible" teacher I have ever seen.

For Stat/Math 394. Probably the worst prof I have ever had, ridiculous grading and unbelievably unclear lectures that focus on proofs the whole time rather than conceptual knowledge. On midterm 2 there was a question that only 3/80 people got full credit and everyone else got 0/10 points with no partial credit. Awful prof, avoid if you can.

He is an ok teacher. His 394 class is rather boring/ difficult. He somehow manages to make seemingly simple concepts very hard to grasp, things like probability and distributions were a struggle. He also basically gives you the homework problems and just tells you to do them. You can look towards a textbook, it would be as, if not more helpful.

analysis.name: Alexandra Nichifor
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 209 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Fun professor with clear lectures. Super accessible for help and office hours. Only downside is class difficulty didn't match the final: lecture and homework felt much easier than what showed up on the final, so it was tough to earn a strong grade. I'd recommend her, but find harder practice problems early so the final doesn't blindside you.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Prof. Nichifor really cares about her students and wants them to do well, and is available and willing to meet with you to make that happen. Her tests were hard but very fair; wouldn't test on anything we didn't explicitly go over. Do whatever you can to get into her class, she is amazing!

Her midterms weren't overly difficult, but since it's Calc 2, you either understand the material or you don't. The department final was noticeably harder than the midterms, which felt like a big jump. Overall she was a solid teacher, though there's still some room for improvement, but I would recommend taking her over other teachers.

She's a really good professor who truly loves to help her students out. She was willing to stay in the hall even after the lecture ended to answer questions or to clarify concepts for me. Her structure for the class was clear, and her lecture was also fantastic and easy to understand.  She also gave out notes and outlines for the class. LOVE HER!

LOVE NICHIFOR! Her accent is lovely, and she really cares about her students. She is clear about everything, screencasts, and her tests are certainly not torture. She is clear about what things you should know and what you will be tested on.

analysis.name: Alexander Paredez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Be independent and prepare for lab before coming in, even if he doesn't explicitly tell you to. Lowkey probably has adhd, he's a little unorganized but he obviously cares and loves to teach. Can be a little blunt but I think that's just how he talks. Easy to succeed in class if you put in some effort. Criteria is not hard. Huge dad energy.
Lectures, journal club, quizzes. Not impossibly hard but the quizzes were a kind tough so study. Journal clubs were fun and lowkey, graded for effort.

Alex is super chill. 402 is a lab class it is all hands on with a "weekly" quiz on procedure so that you read it. But he only gave the quizzes on about half of the weeks. Great class to take if you want to get into research bc it gives you all the practical skills you need in a lab. Class is LONG tho sometimes going overtime. A good and easy time

This was a lab course that basically allowed students hands-on experience with lab techniques such as western blotting, imaging, gel electrophoresis, and making medium. There were only three quizzes which were fairly challenging but doable if studied the lab manual thoroughly. The grading of the class was fair and participation was worth the most.

Because 402 is a lab-based class, be sure to take it with a friend lest you be partnered with someone you don't know all quarter. Alex has pretty low expectation about students' previous experience in bio labs and takes the time to walk each student through common lab procedures. Lab classes can be long but satisfying if you do them well

analysis.name: Amelia Wirts

review_highlights.comment:
*414*

Prof Wirts is stellar! Very engaging and enjoyable! Workload is fair, lowest 3 quizzes are dropped, AND automatic extensions are included for every paper. I adjusted next quarter's schedule so I could take a course with her again. 

She teaches uni-level philosophy courses. IDK why people are complaining about having to read and write...

Even if you're a good writer, essay grades are basically a dice roll. Professor was extremely rude and refused to elaborate when I asked a question about the feedback on my essay. TA was even worse — severely lacked understanding of the material and yet graded essays on how well they conformed to her misinterpretations.

414** I loved her class! She was able to grant extensions and was very caring and flexible, which I really appreciated. She grades fairly, gives good and thorough feedback on assignments, and made class fun! I would absolutely love to take another class with her again.

Really great lectures, they're super engaging and she is passionate and is very knowledgable about what she teaches. You have to be so locked in to succeed though, compared to other classes, the difficulty felt like a 300 level, not 100.

analysis.name: Amanda Friz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Nice professor. But the class is okay, work is not too hard, but not too easy. She isn't really in touch with the class; everything is through TA and old recorded lectures. My TA is pretty nice. Really strict on grading and late penalties. Honestly the work didn't feel relevant to the class

Weekly quizzes, Canvas assignments from quiz sections and lectures, and 3 "exams" (3 take-home essay prompts). Pretty easy but the most boring lectures I have every heard in my entire life. I never thought it would be this hard to focus. When I would walk to Kane 120, I would think of the desire to be ran over by a car at the roundabout outside.

Prof. Friz is nice and helpful at office hours, but in an online format I am not a fan of her classes. Some of this is due to luck of the section draw; my TA was an incredibly harsh grader. The assignments mostly consist of busywork—easy busywork, but often feels pointless. Exams are difficult. Lecture material is politically infused.

The course I took with Professor Friz was online but still you could see her care and knowledge through the lectures as well as the assignments. All the assignments were very reasonable with a lot of information and resources given to succeed, would love to take an in person class with her.

Friz wasn't bad. Definitely passionate about the subject and makes lectures interesting and interactive. Be ready to write. Doesn't give much feedback on essays, just marks you down. Friz is helpful and wants the best for students, but makes it difficult to achieve.

analysis.name: Amelia Lehosit
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment:
Genuinely the best English professor I've ever had - Amelia's passion for writing and literature is evident in the way she teaches, her assignments, feedback, and day-to-day classroom activities. She's a very caring person and puts in a ton of effort to make sure you feel supported throughout the course. 

A++ professor!

She is amazing. I took her English 281 course and it was about fiction and fairytales. In the end 
 write a paper on your own fairytales after reading articles  and watching short films throughout the class. We signed up for  1 on 1 mandatory meetings which I appreciated.

I cannot think of a single bad thing to say about Amelia. The fact that her ratings are stellar on a website where people come to complain is very telling. She is caring, honest, and so understanding. Every single lecture was engaging and the material was fascinating. She is eager to help students and wants every student to succeed. Thanks Amelia!!

An extremely kind professor, Amelia cares about all of her students. She is very aware of how busy people are, and as a result makes sure that she is being reasonable with her workload. She gives very thorough feedback on writing assignments, and is very transparent about how she grades. 4.0 is easily attainable if you turn in all assignments.

Ms. Lehosit made the class very fun and interesting. She made it easy by grading using a grading contract, meaning that as long as you turn work in, then you would be guaranteed a 3.0 and then you can do extra stuff for a better grade. Ms. Lehosit also gave really great feedback that truly helped to improve my writing. I highly recommend!!

analysis.name: Amal al Wahish

Homework website is held together by two lines of code and a prayer

She is the kindest professor I have encountered, exceptionally helpful with excellent lectures. Professor Wahish provides pre-lecture notes in advance and schedules all in-class quizzes at least a week beforehand. Amal suggested various student resources at UW, and following her advice, I reached out to DRS for assistance with my anxiety. She's an excellent Prof

i wouldn't wish him on my worst enemy. he said to the class before the last exam that if a few of us got similar grades he would select certain students to get certain grades based on who he likes as students better.

analysis.name: Apryle Craig

If I'm a sophomore or junior taking his 337 class I'd just quit the major honestly, his class was so boring and the fact that he was forced to teach this make me so sad. Most boring class I have ever take in UW. The course content is so important that the lectures shouldn't be presented by professor like this. He's just look at a single slides talk about whatever he thought about, and test it in the quiz

She's SO funny I love her, lectures were always so engaging and you can tell how passionate she is about the subject matter. I loved this class and Prof. Cansunar. Never did any of the readings as everything you need to know is in the lecture/slides. Professor Cansunar was actually very good! She is very excited, friendly and has a lot of knowledge. It's not a class with many assignments, so really study for midterm and final, otherwise your grade will drop easily.

He is intelligent, cares about student opinions, and is so funny. He offers rebuttals to your opinions to get you to think deeper but not insultingly. I 100% recommend him!

Prakash is awesome. The best professor I have ever had at UW. Always encourages respectful debate in an academic environment that is often hostile to independent thought. The lectures are long, but he is a very engaging instructor.
Amazing professor. Great lectures and thoughtful class discussions. This is what the university experience is supposed to be like.
