Amazing prof. Took a super late class, and she structured it in a way that worked for all students. Wants to make sure you understand the content and all of the content is available at all times. It is a lot of information, but expectations are clear of what you should know.

I thoroughly enjoyed Bebe's class and she is clearly incredibly well-versed in her field. Lectures were easy to follow and she always gave the class good idea of what exams would look like. Although she does not provide practice exams, concept check questions were always very similar to the actual exam and I did not have a hard time studying.

I only used 2 weeks to study mgmt200. One week before midterm and one week before final. I got a 3.5 but her class is the most time efficient one I've ever taken. The homework are 19 quizzes but only count 10. They are all due a few days before final. I recommend taking quizzes before exams.

Bebe was rlly chill. The class was pretty straightforward and she only tests off her lecture content, so I would recommend reviewing the slides instead of the textbook for exams. She talks pretty fast and there's A LOT of content so make sure to frequently review. Graded based on midterm, final, and 3 short canvas quizzes + textbook chapter quizzes

analysis.name: Daniel Bessner
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are very clear, they do tend to have a lot of content at a fast pace, but he always encourages questions from students. Homework is super managable only brief readings each week, with weekly quizzes on lecture/reading content. Professor really cares for each student. One of the most intelligent professors I've had at UW. I RECOMMEND!!

Super fast and dense lectures with almost no notes on his slides. I honestly think he writes his lectures beforehand and reads them like a script. That said, he's funny enough that I genuinely didn't care about that. He's also willing to answer any questions that you might have. Exams are pretty easy too.

Very, very intelligent and accessible.  The class was lecture-heavy, but asking questions was heavily encouraged.  Graded on very few meaty assignments, but prep was easy to do.  Cares a lot about learning and current affairs, definitely a class to take if you can.

Bessner is such an amazing professor. His class was my favorite class at UW. The class was discussion based, and every discussion was incredibly intellectually engaging without being too difficult to understand. His lectures were also super interesting, and I really appreciated hearing his perspective on a lot of current events. Take his class!!

Easy grader, but he talks really fast, doesn't use slides, and if you don't take notes you will struggle. Make note of overarching concepts and events but don't worry about the details of the events, just note what caused them and their overall impact. Do the readings and take notes on them, referencing them boosts your exam grade.

analysis.name: Janet Bester-Meredith
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She switches up her exam style throughout the quarter. If you ask her to clarify what she was talking about in class she doesn't know what she meant by what said half the time. This is a physiology class and she barely ever tested us on mechanisms but rather transport proteins. She is awful, UW needs to fire her, NEVER take her class!!

Extremely demanding class that requires you to be constantly paying attention and remembering every little thing she says in lecture and in quiz section. 
She does give a little extra credit but the expectations for the tests and presentation are so unclear and yet very specific where you will always score lower than what you think. Don't take....

I missed a quiz section at the beginning of the quarter by accident, and it seems like she has had it out for me since then. Completely unaccommodating, doesn't want to work with you, and won't help you with questions if she doesn't like you. She reads from her lecture notes, which disconnect from her talking, I doubt her knowledge of the material.

I took this class 2025 Fall and loved it! It was taught by Dr. B and Dr. Gilbert. Although there was an exam every other week, you got one drop and were all multiple choice. Slides are posted and clear to read. I never read the textbook, just rewatched the lectures and review the slides. Do go to PF sessions and office hours if you have time.

The content is a lot and it is hard, but Dr. B does her best to make a conducive, welcoming, and supportive learning environment. There are lots of practice exams and questions (from her and from the PF workshops) and plenty of extra office hours to get you help if you need it. The classes do revolve on participation and active learning.

analysis.name: David Bachman
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Bachman is incredibly intelligent. Everything he says is important, which makes note-taking hard. If you are struggling go & meet with him! He is so helpful one-on-one. unless you are interested in IS, don't do it. The TAs are REALLY hard but REALLY helpful. They want u to learn & gain skills & engage. Meet with them one-on-one too! Really helpful!

Bachman is extremely knowledgeable and very thorough in his lectures. However, he does not use lecture slides, but rather a word document with a few key points. This, coupled with he monotonous voice and occasional mumbling (although he was generally eloquent) can make it difficult and boring to follow lectures. This is the hardest class I've taken

Bachman ran our "Task force" group and I have to say he didn't seem to enjoy doing that. He hardly ever said a word and he struck me as just a  professor who clearly wasn't very good at hiding the fact that he didn't actually want to teach students. Probably he enjoyed the pay and lifestyle of being a prof. but he just seemed pretty burned out.

terrible class. Lectures were dry, and we hardly went over discussion questions for 100+ page readings assigned every week. He also stopped putting out discussion questions after week 5 so it was hard to know just what he wanted you to get out of the readings. Super harsh grader and your grade depends on three assignments. Would not recommend

Professor Bachman is extremely knowledgeable when it comes to China. He knows just about every single event down to the exact date and specific details. This class has a lot of reading that requires a lot of time. It's a bit tough, but definitely worth it, especially for those interested in China and US-China relations!

analysis.name: Benjamin Feintzeig
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great professor; great at explaining complicated topics in a way that inspires you to want to read more in your free time. Reading responses are graded very generously, but the lectures are so interesting that he makes you want to read closely anyway. I learned a lot about philosophy of science in this course and was pushed to think for myself.

His lectures were great, just a little long. He answers questions well and is very helpful during office hours. The class is also difficult, but he does a really good job teaching, so it's not impossible. Also, the final was a take-home, so do with that information what you will.

Excellent lecturer, truly knows his stuff! Homework's and Final were fairly difficult but graded very leniently. Very interesting material presented in an effective way where often you will prove parts of results shown in lecture.

Fantastic professor, class content is diabolically hard but very possible to succeed in. I don't really do STEM which is probably why I struggled, but I still scored highly consistently. Just make sure you turn everything in on time!! Feintzeig is actually the goat though, incredibly intelligent and really easy to work with outside of class.

I have so much to say about Professor Feintzieg. Not only is he incredibly knowledgeable, but is also incredibly accommodating -- his class was difficult, but difficult in the way that you leave the course with a completely changed mind and as much passion as him. I absolutely recommend him for PHIL470 (and honestly for anything else) :)

analysis.name: Katherine Beckett
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: AMAZING PROFESSOR. My favorite who made me de ide to major in LSJ. A difficult class with lots of reading, but WORTH IT and that is coming from a stoner. Interesting concepts of war on drugs and criminalization of the minority. Super relevant to today and its common knowledge that she is a tough class so don't let that think that affects too much

Best class ive ever taken and amazing professor, her lectures were great and the readings were extremely interesting. 
Two essay-based exams and about 5-6 quizzes, you can take the quizzes 3 times each. In class assignments are easy and given about once a week. Discussions with other students are encouraged in class.
Professor Katherine is amazing!

I LOVE Prof Beckett! LSJ 200 was an amazing class and made me want to major in LSJ. Beckett is well-spoken, articulate, caring, and passionate. She engages students in discussion, which is interesting in a large lecture hall, but I enjoyed it. The class is organized well into 3 major units, with either a test or paper at the end of each. Take it!

Overall, do not take this class if you do not plan on minoring or majoring in LSJ. While Katherine and the TAs are all great, the class content is very repetitive. The reading responses/assignments honestly feel like busywork. All in all, I feel like way too much work is asked for from a 200 class. This class made me stray away from the LSJ dept.

intro to law. class format: 3 essays (2-3 pages each; each worth 10% of final grade), a midterm (very easy, class average was 88%; worth 20% of your final grade) a final (10 page essay; worth 30% of final grade) and sections grade (based on small quizes and participation in discussions; worth 20% of final grade. class focused on immigration law.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Kirk
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 98 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Kirk is super knowledgeable and her lectures are very well-paced and informative. Tests are online and open note. I typed notes in class so when I took tests I could "control F" and search through my notes super fast. I never had to read the book. Her supp du jour quizzes are super easy, she gets her questions straight from the text.

Her lectures are great but can get repetitive and boring if you read the textbook ahead. She's very passionate in what she covers about in class so it's very easy to stay engaged. Class was easy as long as you did the work and paid attention. I would recommend this class to anyone for an easy A (assuming you take good notes).

Professor Kirk is super caring, respectful, and passionate. She really cares about what she is teaching and is super flexible and easy-going when it comes to grading of assignments, quizzes, and tests. The class was not very high in intensity or effort, but did require reading, participation, and attendance.

only 50% of attendance is needed for full participation credit. exams are online and open-note. the only "homework" is doing a 10 question quiz with your learning group in quiz section which you can ask other ppl for answers or just look back at the slides. amazing professor and TA's!!
She is the GOAT. She genuinely cares about her students and their learning. The lectures can drag on a bit, but she is an amazing lecturer. The coursework is really easy and everything is open note.

analysis.name: Stephen Bezruchka
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: We had 2 group projects, 2 reading responses, and one open notes final which is open for one week so in terms of workload this class was manageable. You often discuss with your group and sometimes will do fun activities depending on the lecture. 2 professors and 2 ta's we had and all of them were chill and understanding. Not a stressful class.

Dr. Bezruchka's classes are very hands-on, but you won't be doing busy work. HSERV 476 did have some readings, but you could get a good grade without doing most of them. Your grade is based on a few moderately-sized, but fun assignments. No participation points but still worth going to clarify assignments and get help. Lots of time to work in class

Professor Bezruchka makes his class very interesting. My perception on public health has changed and learned a lot from this class that I can apply to my life outside of school. He actually cares more about you learning than the assignments you do. In quiz sections you deliberate a lot about the topics. Would recommend for diversity credit.

Very clear requirements to get a good grade in the class. Make sure you understand the key ideas that is being repeated throughout the lectures. Don't skip too many lectures as it's a part of the grade. Are able to be creative in how you do projects, and tests are very easy, no studying required if you show up to class and listen.

I loved this class! This class is really interesting and teaches a lot of skills that I use in everyday life. This class is really easy you just have to follow the grading criteria. You basically get graded on one group project that you present at the end of the quarter. There aren't any tests either which is great!

analysis.name: Davinder Bhowmik
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Coursework is manageable however grading was unclear and most assignments had little to no feedback. Instruction and expectations extremely vague especially with the final. Class participation is essential every class.

The class was super easy and requirements were clear. But she had multiple non emergency class cancelations and didn't seem to care at all about the class. Small group discussions were nice but the way she responded back to peoples opinions seemed very passive aggressive and blase.
Davinder is a pretty good teacher, but the class was extremely boring. As long as you do the readings, the class is cake. Only 2 tests, with study guides given. However, it is a REALLY boring class.

Professor Bhowmik runs a very solid discussion-based class. JAPAN 435 leaned heavily on theoretical texts, which were harder to discuss than literature, but the central ideas and themes were very interesting. I also enjoyed seeing her research interests incorporated into the class, as well as her openness to learning from us as well as vice versa.

Do the readings and participate as much as possible and you'll do fine. Something I really love about Prof. Bhowmik is that she's not biased and actually likes when people play the devil's advocate. She's also very accommodating if you need to take your final early for studying abroad which was awesome.

analysis.name: Alisha  Bhimani
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: this professor initially proclaimed her interest in mentoring and supporting students, however she would often show up to class late, didn't provide feedback for assignments until the end of the quarter, spent the class on her phone, threatened to fail students, and often did not know the answer to questions and would direct students to look it up
Alisha was very dedicated to preparing us for real-world practice and making sure our time in class was spent on the most high-yield information.
Best global health class I've ever taken!!!!

analysis.name: Siddharth Bhogra
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Just simply amazing. Try to take a class with Siddharth if you have the choice.

I am a stem major and took ENGL 131 because I had to and was planning on putting in the bare minimum effort. However, Siddharth made me want to show up and put in effort because he is a really interesting person and an engaging speaker. I always looked forward to this class and was never stressed about it because he is so chill and understanding.

This was such a fun class to take and I really enjoyed having Siddharth as my professor because he was so nice and accommodating and just generally made the class super easy to stay engaged with. 10/10 would recommend taking 131 with him if given the chance :)

What a guy! He's such a character, and I love to hear about his life stories as they make me believe that it will all work out. His assignments were relatively clear, and I enjoyed his one-on-one feedback. A great prof to have for a mandatory class.

analysis.name: Arunima Bhattacharya
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Literally cannot understand half of what she is saying because she goes so fast, she will erase stuff off the chalk board after letting you look at it for a total of 4 seconds, hard tests, will not respond to your emails, just overall rude and unapproachable. Would not recommend, avoid her class if possible.
Writes way too fast on the board - gives 10 seconds to complete class problems. Not very clear to comprehend material. Assumes that you have strong Math 126 knowledge.
Arunima is a fantastic instructor! Loved this class.
Honestly, the best math prof I have had at uw!

analysis.name: Deepa Bhandaru
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Deepa is a great instructor. You leave the classroom feeling the energy of the many political theorists. The class was not easy, but manageable. The essays are graded harder than your standard 200 level class. I highly recommend you talk to Deepa outside of lecture, she will clarify questions and greatly add to your overall success.

Deepa is the smartest and hottest professor I have ever met throughout my entire college life. If you have the privilege to take her classes, you should be glad because you are going to engage in classroom discussions everyday and you will learn the most important part of Liberal Art studies, how to "trouble" the world with your knowledge.

Deepa was a great teacher! She was engaging, knows what she's talking about, and very helpful because she has much experience in her subject. I had her for Eng 198 joined with Poly Sci 201 and she helped SO MUCH in understanding that lecture as well as how the Poly Sci TAs would grade. Great person and really helpful essay feedback!!

It was my first political science class, and I took it based off of her ratings.  And she's great!  By far the best professor I've ever had.  I dragged my friends to her lectures to see her present.  Fantastic public speaker, incredibly engaging, intriguing.  Could not recommend her more. And yeah, she's also pretty hot.

Deepa is a great professor! She is very helpful in discussion and clarifies everything in lecture.  Deepa is incredibly engaging and intelligent and it's very refreshing to have a discussion leader that is very aware of her students and the information she is presenting.  I hope I can have her in the future!

analysis.name: Amy Bhatt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Amy is a very helful and knowledgeable instructor. She shows genuine care for the understanding and education of her students. She also does a great job mixing up the class so it is not all lectures. She has small, interesting class assignments and also does a great job striking interest in students for fun class discussions.

Amy is a very helful and knowledgeable instructor. She shows genuine care for the understanding and education of her students. She also does a great job mixing up the class so it is not all lectures. She has small, interesting class assignments and also does a great job striking interest in students for fun class discussions.
Amy is an engaging TA who takes a sincere interesting in her students.  She is a very professional teacher who is incredibly knowlegable about her field.
Amy is always prepared and willing to help.  She is a great professor.

analysis.name: Jeff Bilmes
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is hard to get in touch with. Never respond to students' email or discord. He wants to teach 16 weeks contents in 10 weeks. If you are not ready to spend 20+ hours a week on his course, then consider carefully before taking his courses.

Great guy with a lot of knowledge on the subject. However, the class was poorly managed by the TAs. You have to ask many questions and spend dozens of hours on assignments that are posted late and revised several times just before the due date. I felt cheated by the unprofessional environment. Lectures are 4 hours.

Bilmes is the best professor I've had. EE 514 covers dense material like entropy, Huffman coding, and Gaussian channels, but his intuition-first approach makes it click. He remembered my exact confusion from two weeks prior at office hours. Problem sets prepare you perfectly. 10/10, do not miss this class.
Lecture is like reading the handout material.

The professor, while very knowledgeable about the subject, fails to bring it down to a level understandable by those that haven't spent years in machine learning. The homework is extremely hard and his class sessions do nothing to help you get it done. Expect to do a lot of google searching in order to complete your homework. Frustrating & tiring.

analysis.name: Laada Bilaniuk
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Laada is really nice and always ready to help. She really loves what she teaches, and her interpretation really made me became interested in Anthropology. Textbook really unnecessary, because everything is on powerpoint and she records every class. Clicker questions are used to check attendance, but do not cheat or you will die.

Professor Bilaniuk is an amazing professor. She knows her material and is willing to help her students at anytime. Participation and attendance matters. Only one test a final exam and one 6-8 page paper. There is a presentation based on your research project and a lot of in class assignments for attendanceparticipation grade. She is a fair grader.

Although her lectures tend to be a little boring, she is a great teacher. This class was a breeze and I learned a lot (which is how I think school should be). All you have to do is take good notes (which is basically just copying from the slides) and study the list of terms before each exam. I never even had to pick up the textbook. Great class!

This was the first time she was teaching this class and the usual time allotment was basically cut in half so she did very good with what she had. Lectures were interesting, engaging, and thought-provoking, and the final project was very fun and free-range. Highly rec for an extra few credits. Dense reading but easy to skim and still participate.

Memorization is key in this class. Make sure you show up to lecture, as she often says things that are explicitly on the exam. Take notes!!! Talking to her outside of class is easy, and you also have helpful TAs in case she isn't available. She's very sweet, but don't take that to mean she's a pushover. Had a wonderful time overall. :)

analysis.name: Bingni Brunton
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I would like to speak up to warn others looking for a PI for grad school programs. Administration has confirmed that Bing's behavior is unacceptable and not reflective of the values of the school. All students in her lab have confessed to crying at least once due to an interaction with her. It is common for students to leave her lab.

One of the best lecturers, professors, and people I have met. Flipped classroom with long-ish YouTube videos, so be aware of that, but it's worth the watch. Her communication skills are out of the world and she knows so much. You ask her ANYTHING and she will be able to keep up. Changed my perspective on biology forever. TAKE HER CLASS. FAIR EXAMS!

Was not the best professor. Shes a tough grader not giving you proper feedback and she can be quite condescending if you dont understand a concept. She is not helpful either. Avoid this prof if possible.

No structure to the class, would tell you something to your face (like your answer was correct) and then grade you opposite. Nothing was ever graded in a timely manner, when I asked her about it she was extremely hostile. I'm hoping to be able to work with administration as this is never how I've had interactions at UW

Her class is flipped with long lecture videos and hard quizzes, all in-class polls are graded on correctness no completion, and her midterm was bad. There was no grading scale on the syllabus, and assignment grades weren't posted until the end of the quarter. Assignments were posted last minute. I've never taken a more unorganized course.

analysis.name: Bill Howe
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Felt more like a seminar than a lecture; heads up if you hate reading/discussion. The course description can sound philosophical, but the readings were thought-provoking and (mostly) enjoyable even for a technical person. The best part was writing my own paper -- lots of flexibility and room to explore. Reasonable workload/grading if that matters.

Bill Howe is a professor who means well. However, he tends to ramble during lectures, which can leave less time to focus on the coding. I stopped attending class after week 4 because I felt I could learn the course individually, but I was wrong. He wants his students to succeed, but his teaching methods don't work for everyone (it works for me).

Bill is super sweet and cares a lot about his students. The TAs are also great and helpful. In terms of grades, there is a lot of opportunity for extra credit and to improve your grade. Sometimes he can be chaotic or disorganized, but if you put in some extra time outside of class, you can definitely learn a lot and succeed.

Seemingly doesn't know the course materials and there is always some kind of error on his part with the problems we do in-class. He is also not equipped to train TAs (as they are equally as unhelpful) and to work with students with any kind of accommodations. 99% of the course is spent on teaching yourself the content.

Bill's teaching style at UW is a mess. He's late, barely audible, and his lectures are a jumble of confusion. His speaking volume is so low that it's challenging to hear him even in a quiet classroom. Rather than offering clear explanations, he often seems confused himself, which adds to our confusion when seeking clarification. AVOID  
 HIM!!!!!!!

analysis.name: Bich-Ngoc Turner
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: As a Vietnamese person who speaks broken viet at home taking this class, taking this class was pretty easy; the same can be said if you were non-vietnamese, as those who barely show up were still able to get the lessons. Her assignments were pretty easy to do. She also provides good context about Vietnamese culture and dialect.

Cares about her students and flexible with students who communicate with her. Makes learning Vietnamese enjoyable and engaging. She enforces fair expectations and grading. The signed student projects that are presented in class are surprisingly very educational. The professor is kind and funny. Will happily take 1 year of Viet courses from her.

Just lots of vocab, she doesn't teach proper sentence structure too much. If you already know Vietnamese, Viet111 will be a breeze but if you dont, be prepared to be overwhelmed. You get 5 free attendance passes, after that she starts taking off points. There's 3 tests and 3 hw assignments, and has extra credit too. Try not to mess up too much. GL

I took this class to get a better understanding of my Vietnamese heritage and so glad I did. I was hesitant at first because it is a 400 level course but thanks to professor Turner, I did learn a lot about Vietnam's literary history, society and culture. The reading assignments, class discussions and movies are quite interesting and enlightening.

This is not an easy class for me as a freshmen, but Professor Turner made it really fun and interesting to learn. There's a lot of work but it's worth it. You learn a lot about modern Vietnam. Grading is reasonable, and the professor really loves what she teaches, cares about the students she works with. Take her Viet classes, you won't regret.

analysis.name: Billie Swalla
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The professor is very condescending and inconsiderate of her students. Gets frustrated when students don't know what is going on or what to expect grading wise despite having nothing explicitly stated in syllabus, and only gives verbal instructions for most things. Lectures are in no coherent chronological order and feel very random.

Very frustrating. "Lectures" were just copies of figures from the textbook, and she did a poor job explaining them. I had no idea what was expected of me; the midterm had obscure matching people's names to their research, along with random phylogenies, while the final was incredibly basic. Despite getting an A, I learned very little in her class.

Really poor experience. Professor seemed much more interested in having a mid-lecture conversation with the class's overqualified students instead of making the material accessible for everyone else. Tests were fair but lecture presentations were among the worst I've seen. For the first time in my life, I had no motivation to succeed in a class.

Worst prof I have ever taken at UW. Unclear grading structure, lectures are just pictures taken from the textbook & she just gives very vague descriptions of each slide w/ no teaching outline. Tested on random facts mentioned once in lect. Ignores students' feedbacks/concerns. Avoid taking, she is very condescending & is only teaching for funding.

Absolutely hated this class. Overall grade outline sucks. Treats this class as an ego boost because she had us watch biology videos she was in and mentioned a lot how she has 20 years of teaching experience but you can tell she absolutely hates teaching. I was excited about the material beforehand but she made this class unbearable.

analysis.name: Timothy Billo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Tim is the best professor I've ever met. He had the power to make every student care about the nature. ENVIR 280 is an awesome class where you go on a lot of field trips. After taking a class with him, you will wanna be out on the field all the time!
The best class you will ever take at UW. If you ever get to go bird watching with Tim, you are a blessed soul.

If you don't already know, Tim Billo literally has a cult following at UW. Seriously, search #timbillo on Instagram. By the end of the quarter (ENVIR 280) you'll literally want to BE him, and know everything he knows. He geeks out, has a great sense of humor, and is not intimidating by any means. You will be lucky just to be in his presence!

This class is NOT easy and you will have to work for a good grade. Despite that, Tim is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is a genius in the environmental field and his passion shines in lectures and the field. The exams (1 midterm, 1 final) are partially based on plant and bird identification, so be prepared to memorize a lot!

Honestly one of my favorite classes, however, the main discussions were not enviro education but enviro justice and racism. There are a couple opportunities to teach kids through outside organizations (amazing experience) and classes are student led discussions. Tim is awesome and makes an effort to learn names. Research paper is graded harshly.

analysis.name: Binh Tang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took English 131 with Mr. Binh Tang and I am so glad I got him as my teacher for the quarter. Binh took a class that has terrible layout, tons of busy work and makes writing and composition enjoyable to everyone. Binh is an amazing person who made class very engaging. He doesn't have a rubric but gives so much feedback. 10/10 class, 10/10 teacher
Very encouraging of finding your own voice and incorporating it in your writing! He always gives good feedback and genuinely wants students to do well.

His teaching takes a while to get used to because at first, there is no clear structure and instructions for essay are vague. This is done on purpose to enable students to be creative and grading is lenient with lots of good feedback. I love Binh Tang

Binh Tang is a predoctoral professor and it really shows. There are no rubrics to his essays, just general requirements that can use very strange and sometimes confusing wording. If you truly care about writing, his different perspectives could be useful, but in a STEM focused school like UW his assignments feel like a gigantic waste of time.

analysis.name: Margarite Blignaut
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This discussion-based class is graded on only a few things, making it difficult to know what the professor expects on exams, especially for both short/long answer questions. Class time is mostly spent sharing opinions, which rarely help with the exams. Assignments are not uploaded consistently and often appear at the last minute. She is kind though

Learned so much in this course. She is very smart and knows the material inside and out, often cultivating interesting class discussions.Tests are often and can be stressful, but she prepares you well for them if you come to class and do the readings. Write everything down because tests are open note. If you listen, you will learn so much!

She is nice but extremely difficult to please. Grading feels arbitrary and based on her personal beliefs rather than the actual prompt. Be prepared to lose points for "unwritten rules" not found in the syllabus, and don't expect flexibility or the chance to redo work. If you have an analytical learning style, getting a 100% is nearly impossible.

I loved taking her course. She's a great lecturer and I loved the class curriculum. However, the grading felt a bit arbitrary at times and sometimes I did not receive a lot of feedback on assignments. After receiving a grade I was unsure of how I lost points because the rubric is very subjective.

analysis.name: Michael Blake
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
A great class to take as an underclassmen before you declare a major. Very good intro to moral philosophy. Not a lot of homework outside of reading which was nice.

Tests are short-answer responses to lecture content. If you study adequately, you should have little issue.

This is a good and interesting schedule-filler / major class. I recommend!

Professor Blake was an awesome professor and taught the material especially well. The only note I really have is that there was minimal guidance on what would be on the exams and how to study for them. The quiz sections also didn't feel useful/productive for class material.

Fantastic professor he knows what he's talking about. TA's are SOO hit or miss. Since your graded on only FOUR things the entire class you need a decent TA. I got lucky with my TA so they were fair on lots of grading but I had a friend who said the class was a nightmare with a bad TA. Harsh grading overall don't take if your looking for an easy A!!

I definitely recommend this class! Prof. Blake is an incredible teacher- I've never rated a prof before but I feel like he is worth rating-- he is extremely well spoken and he keeps lecture interesting, fun to go to. Interesting topics and papers, Tests are pretty fair. Definitely worth taking a class with him!
Very interesting class, Dr. Blake does really engaging lectures, they were the highlight of my week, the quiz sections felt unnecessary but otherwise a really great class!

analysis.name: Ebru Bekyel
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 366 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Bombed her midterm (Most of the students did) Her class examples and homework are super easy compared to her tests & quizzes. I went to talk to her about my grade and she was very rude and said there was no way I could pass her class. It seemed like she was out to get us giving us 2 page quizzes and only 10 min. I would NEVER take her again.

She skips steps and messes up often when working through problems during lecture. The WebAssign homework is lengthy and 20x more difficult than what she teaches in lecture. Expect a majority of your time to be spent on WebAssign homework. Class average on the 1st midterm was an F (20/50), as well as a majority of the weekly quizzes so far.

Worst math professor at UW. She does not teach you at all. Her lectures do not make any sense and do not match the webassign homework. She sometimes gives out 3 chapters of homework out at once all due on the same day while other professors do 1 chapter due at a time. A lot better off learning the material on your own. She messes up way too much.
The disparity between the lectures and homework is a lot. Two huge assignments per week. She'll help out during office hours. Midterms aren't easy.

Bekyel is clear in her examples during lecture. Her quizzes and HW, which seem to be the same regardless of the professor you choose, are easy. However, that's where the pros of taking a class with her end. Her first midterm during Winter 2014 was not similar to last year's midterm, which she told us to use to study. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASSES.

analysis.name: Grant Blume
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: All of the questions on the midterms/final exam are on the study guides, but knowing the terms is crucial as there are lots of close multiple choice answers/matching that requires you to know the definition. His lectures are very engaging and educational. Make sure you put in effort on your group projects because they end up being worth a bit

I was super excited to take this class but it turned out to be not very challenging at all. 3 tests are super easy and you could go get an A without reading what he assigned all quarter. Pretty annoying when he answers all the questions people have in class...like cmon use office hours please but that does mean he is very approachable and kind.

Lecture style is great. Slides do not have much information on these so attendance is required for an actual understanding. There is lots of reading which aren't all necessary but helped me. Group projects are essays.

Lecture style was cool, but slides are set up with limited information so attendance is necessary for full understanding. Lots of reading which isn't required but definitely helped me. The group projects are essays.

analysis.name: Richard Block
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: His class was disorganized and unrefined. His heart doesn't seem into it and he showed up to class with 0 preparation. Despite being a class that begs for original critical thinking skills, he expects you to parrot and repeat his ideas. "Discussion" is illusory and used as a catalyst for him to lecture. Least favorite prof I've had in 3 yrs @ UW

I didn't really know what to expect from this class, I took it randomly. It turned out that I actually kinda liked it. Lectures were always really interesting. Not much homework really. You listen to the interesting things Professor Block has to say, watch films about the Holocaust and talk about them in class, the books we read pretty good too.

90% of the time, are just chatting and talking about the readings that we assigned. The reading was not easy, and if u want to be engaged, you have to be super "smart." he just thinks so deeply about the readings. His class was great, the work was not hard at all, just some writing,easy A. Love the teacher, But not take it again.

Richard knows a lot about the topics covered in the course which were interesting. I would NOT take a class with him. What was expected wasnt clear and he often went off course. He goes on a lot of tangents and is disrespectful at times. 2 people dropped the class because of him. He isnt sympathetic to students struggling with mental illness.

Block could not have been a worse teacher. Going to class meant listening to him complain about anything and everything. He doesn't know how to use modern technology and genuinely might be too old to be teaching. The only reason why I dropped this class was because of him.

analysis.name: Blake Hannaford
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is the greatest EE professor ever. He is really good at teaching. Also, he's hot!

Be prepared to be on your own during the whole 10 credit course. The professor probably knows a lot but since there are no lectures being conducted (only sporadic checkins and milestone presentations), you won't get much knowledge from this kind of teaching. When asking tough questions, you'll get redirects and no answers.

Very disorganized class, writes lab specs the week that they're meant to be released, so when they're actually released they're full of mistakes/tasks that we can't do simply because they're not possible. Lab specs change as we work on them so the requirements are always changing. His lectures are the same, he learns as he goes leaving us confused.

Hannaford teaches 447 without a lab which I think made the class a lot less interesting. Most of the stuff we learned didn't have too much application in my opinion and the Sci-lab stuff was just absolutely ridiculous. In the end the average grade in the class was a 3.7-3.8 and he had to curve down because too many people would have gotten 4.0s.

Professor Hannaford is a great instructor. His examples were fascinating and came from years of experience in the field. His coverage of the extremely diverse materials in Robotics was rigorous despite the high volume of information. The book we used aside from Craig filled in all the gaps Craig leaves out. I got much more than my money's worth.

analysis.name: Terrence Blackburne
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Easygoing and approachable. His lectures were clear and discussions were fun. No group project when I took the class. While exams were somewhat challenging (no surprise given it's Foster) , he is VERY generous with his grading. Only complaint is that he never got our assignments back to us, so I had no idea how I was doing. Otherwise good class.

Midterm, two group cases, one writing assignment, and final exam. Go to class! You don't need to read the textbook because his lectures are enough for what you need to know to prepare for the midterm and final. Do ALL the suggested hw problems because his exam questions are very similar to the hw questions.

Blackburne is one of my favorite professors that I have had at UW. He is very knowledgeable and super approachable outside of the classroom, always eager to talk about real-world accounting. The class may be one of the more difficult, as it is a "weed out" class; however, if you put in the time to read and engage in the work, Terry is great.

You're going to have to work hard, but I probably learned more in this class than any other I've taken at Foster. I didn't appreciate all the work he made us do at the time, but you'll leave his class with a solid foundation. Blackburne really cares if you learn the material and will you remember you long after the course is over.
Terrence is a good lecturer. I learned a lot. You do need to spend considerable time at home doing problems to succeed. Pre-read the chapters and do all of the suggested problems to get a 4.0.

analysis.name: Boris Blinov
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Boring lecturer, just regurgitates the textbook in the form of slides in a way that no one actually learns anything from his slides. Tries to make stupid jokes about java updates, which are soo awk. Always says "this is quantitative" or "this is quantitative." He makes you go crazy, and then when another prof makes the tests, you're screwed.

He might be a good human but teaches crap. He takes summer quarter too lightly as far as teaching is concerned but his mid-term was unfair and gave something that was not spoken about in class or in homework. Overall he is horrible!

The only saving grace of Boris' teaching style is that he has a good sense of humor. Otherwise, he teaches directly from the textbook so be prepared to enlist in external sources for help or you will regret taking physics with him. He is unprepared for review sessions as he only decided to do "easy" problems from the review material.

Boris focuses primarily on physics concepts, rather than math, and teaches straight from the textbook. Unfortunately, his style of teaching is often confusing for the average student, and the tests do include the math that he does not teach. Be prepared to do quite a bit of outside studying if you have him.

Fun and funny teacher! Excellent course if you're looking to get a general overview on Physics, which I was. IMO it was an easy A since he drops your worst pop quiz scores and takes the best 1 out of 2 midterm scores. The hardest part was the final paper, which was 5-10 pages on whatever you feel like within the physics realm, which wasn't hard.

analysis.name: Bobby Wilson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took MATH 525 with Bobby in spring 2025. MATH 524 (with Bube) was perfectly fine but Bobby made the series impossible to take. He is very smart but not a great lecturer, he is bad at explaining and his handwriting is illegible. Tests are unreasonably hard. Me and 2 other friends all ended up dropping the class.

Lectures are from the textbook verbatim, homework is often unrelated to lecture material and seem to be testing how well you understand things rather than helping students gain understanding. Strangely, midterms were much easier, though how well we did on said midterm remains a mystery due to grades still not being out by the final week of class.

Prof. Wilson is an insanely intelligent mathematician and a poor teacher. He has such a clear familiarity with the material that he forgets that students don't. Lectures are recited from the book, homework is never motivated and frequently on concepts from the book he hasn't taught. Tests are at least simple enough. It's a frustrating experience.

He is the worst prof I have ever had. Don't take him. He:

-Refuses to give study material for tests
-Gives test questions that do not resemble homework/lecture
-Is awful at explaining things
-Homework is so hard, the TA couldn't do it
-SO much more

Professor Wilson is a great professor. He is very professional. His exams are not that tough and if you attend his lectures and study from his lecture notes you'll be fine. However if you're taking the class remotely, be mindful that the final exam will be lengthy. Don't expect him to be super friendly, but overall he is a really good professor.

analysis.name: Ivana Bozic

Ridiculous amount of work. Class is supposed to be Applied Mathematics as the name implies but didn't touch MATLAB once. Lectures are very monotone and content is rushed.

Doesn't post notes or homework solutions, grades homework too harshly, tests are too long to finish. Very hard class. Homework isn't that bad, but tests are incredibly difficult. Also, going to class is next to pointless because she just copies notes onto the board.

analysis.name: Bojan Belic

Amazing lectures to be a part of. He's easily one of my favorite professors! He was enthusiastic about his students and the material. Made the class super fun with his sarcastic and sassy attitude. Just be ready to banter with the teacher - he loves to throw jokes around! Overall great (and easy) class - just study a tiny bit for tests and its good

Bojan is passionate and engaging with a quirky sense of humour.The class was mostly in Russian yet it was easy to understand him because he's so good at getting ideas across.He can be very kind and patient,but there're class rules that you shouldn't even think about breaking.Also very helpful if you ever have questions/problems.Not to be missed!
Easy class, as long as you show up and pay attention you'll do great. Prof was 10/10, lots of banter and he is the dunkmaster ��

Although, sometimes it would have been nice if he explained things in English so the class as a whole was able to get a more thorough understanding of the material.

analysis.name: Bo Zhao

The one thing I will say, sometimes the lectures can be droll and you can use the slides on your own if you don't have the attention span.
I was praying to jesus that he was a good professor, he made me lose faith in the lord.

Really enjoyed this class. I had some HTML/CSS/JavaScript experience beforehand but this class doesn't require too much previous web design knowledge - the focus is more on leveraging web design tools to answer geographical questions. Would recommend taking the class with Prof. Zhao whenever it's offered, he did a great job and is very passionate.

Bo's a very organized teacher who lays out a clear structure for the class and maintains it. The assignments are easy enough if you go to lecture. Overall, probably my favorite teacher in the geography department due to being such a kind and caring guy. Try to get to know him.

analysis.name: Karl Bohringer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

He was decent in office hours.
Challenging homework requires some serious preparation and studying. But then, one also learn a lot from the class and from further investigation! Highly recommended for those who like to learn.

Homework is also on Pearson which is just a bad platform to host assignments on. There was a difficulty mismatch between the problems taught in lecture and in hw, lab, and tests.

Lecture are excellent compared with most other. Slides give a clear outline of the material, which his commentary enhances. The class gives a comprehensive overview of MEMS processing. Four difficult homeworks, 1 midterm, and a final project (MEMS device design). He speaks with a german accent but is very easy to understand unlike many engr profs

Class is just hard but not necessary his fault, but the lectures are not really helpful, and uses Pearson to conduct all his homework which is never good as it is impersonal and contrary to what it claims does not help in learning at all. He's overall fine but just bad class structure to teach hard concepts.

analysis.name: Mackenzie Bounds

This class is heavier on the reading but it goes by pretty quick. The class is really a play analysis class and can feel more like an english class with a theatre focus. I enjoyed it but do not take it if you do not like reading plays. Mackenzie is good and teaches well.

analysis.name: Brian Curless

Very average as a lecturer: sometimes interesting, sometimes not. Mostly this class felt like a retread of what I've learned in other natural resources classes. Meh overall.

Professor Branch was great. I had him for QSCI 482 which I was pretty worried about, but he made it interesting and easy to learn the material. I barely used the text book and mainly relied on his lecture notes for learning/studying. I would go out of my way to take a class with him again.

analysis.name: Anne Bowen McCoy

review_highlights.comment: You never understand what she's talking about; it's not ENGLISH. Her slides are horrible, I really want to know who did them, extremely confusing and you don't know what she's trying to say. The TAs don't understand what's going on, and they admit it!
If you want to hate chemistry, attend one of McCoy's classes.

Her grading system is capricious and arbitrary as she set the grade lines at random numbers without statistical basis. Spent 20 minutes using confusing calculus to derive an equation, then said we don't  need it.

Her lectures are AWFUL. Although you have to go to get the participation points, she is terrible at explaining. In addition, her wording on tests is done in to try to trick you. The concepts in this class are hard enough without the smoke and mirrors act. Her class average dropped by almost 20% between the two midterms. Take with someone else.

analysis.name: Brian Harvey
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Took this class for an easy A NSc credit. Most of the material was common-sense knowledge, and the lectures were not engaging at all. If you are ok with being bored, go ahead. Weekly short quizzes and short answer video assignments. He seems like a good prof, but not for this easy of a class.

Professor Brian is great, and this class is the perfect 101 course. Easy, interesting, and very few problems overall. You can tell he really cares about what he's teaching. Some assignments might be posted late or due dates might be unclear, but so many little assignments mean one missed wont be a huge deal.

Super easy class for the most part. There are worksheets in the lecture and quiz section though that you have to fill out for participation. All the homework is super light though and there are no tests.

Harvey was sweet and knew his area of study very well! Only complaint was lectures tend to be repetitive and drag on more than it needed to (which can be expected for a 101 class), but Professor Harvey is kind and has reasonable policies! Easy A, if you're okay being a little bored now and then

Professor Harvey is very nice and excited about the material. All the coursework is easily accessible and grading criteria are clear and fair. He makes sure his student's opinions are considered and really encourages participation. Definitely recommend for a fun class!

analysis.name: Dean Bretland
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing teacher when I had him last spring quarter. He explained things in depth and understood where the students were coming from since he took the same class at UW when he was an undergrad. Hands down best office hours—so knowledgeable in the subject and if you bring him any problem he can work through it with you and make anything make sense.

Soft-spoken but gives you the ability to excel in the class if you aren't afraid to ask questions. People comment about how he doesn't give any explanations and just reads slides but any prof in the phys12x series is required to have lecture like that. If you actually have him explain you can tell that he can make any complex problem palatable.

His lectures are fantastic, and his wording and teaching style makes everything very easy to understand. Hard class for sure, but it could have been a lot worse without him teaching it. Never makes you feel ashamed of asking questions. Lots of practice material is given, curve was not very good at all though.

Worst professor I've had. I need to like visually see explanations and how to work through stuff. He reads from the slides and only the slides, never did his own work and never actually explained the correct answers, only what was on the slide. I stopped going to lecture because it was pointless. Will be retaking. Don't waste out of state tuition

real chill guy. stuff you learn and practice in lecture is very relevant to exam content. problem explanations were a bit lacking however, and a lot of conceptual learning comes from the textbook since lecture is mostly spent working on problems. overall a very approachable professor and seems like he really wants you to succeed

analysis.name: William Brown
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

Points are based on very specific answers that are not asked for nor common sense to include, which can be frustrating. Also, he is very very late on posting grades.

overall a likable and fun guy- could be a bit better at making lecture more concise but honestly I didn't mind that much
did some cool work with archaeological analysis of population numbers which was never mentioned in class but its like wow this guy is teaching stats I wish I could know more about how he used it and whatnot

Very nice guy, good content and lecture. Hard concepts but the assignments were easy, so not too hard to get an A. Was a bit disorganized / late to post things on canvas tho. A great intro class to coding on R.

Concepts were easy but his lectures were extremely dry and monotone. Sections were useful sometimes, but section activities are short and inconvenient to get to as a commuter. He's nice and offers a lot of extra credit, though, so as long as you pay attention in lecture and take notes (make sure you use the exact wording he uses) you're fine

He's a nice guy and you can tell he wants his students to learn. His lectures are easy to follow. Just not good w time- he spent the 1st half of the quarter on unit 1(1 chapter) and the other half on unit 2, (3 chapters) so a lot of info was condensed. Pay CLOSE attention to what he says in lectures-he can get specific and it'll be on the exams!

analysis.name: Nathan Brunelle

review_highlights.comment: i had him for my cse 123 class and that was the first time he was teaching it. i thought i was done for but  honestly he put in so much effort to make sure he understood the learning curve of the class and that every student understood well. he wasn't happy with the way one class went and he re-recoded and and sent us a recording too. Sweetest guy.

Dr. Brunelle is an extremely talented lecturer and gave crystal clear explanations to some of the hardest problems in DSA. Super accessible outside of class. He does have a sinister side when it comes to exam difficulty, but compensates for it with all the resources he provides.

Personally I found Dr. Brunelle's lectures somewhat boring overall, but he's a great and funny guy. The assignments are overall kinda boring, but I guess not super hard. The final exam was a bit frustrating because it was different/harder than his previous exams from previous years (which were all same style/format. Overall, not bad though.

Brunelle is by far my favorite professor. He's incredibly accessible, caring, and understanding, while also being an effective (and hilarious) professor. Practice exams directly corresponded to final exams, so I felt I was ACTUALLY learning. Projects are fun (albeit a bit hard when parsing spec) and applicable. Want to love CS? Take his class :D

Probably the best professor I've had so far. Clear lectures with examples and walk throughs. Exams are easy if you show up to lecture/quiz, do practice exams, and pay attention in class. There should be no surprises and everything is doable if you have a solid understanding of the material. Understanding of student schedules also.

analysis.name: Suzanne Brahmia
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment:

Midterms and finals were supposed to test on the fundamental knowledge (easier than past paper). Lectures are awesome; attendance is scaled.

brahmia is probably the best professor i've had at uw. teaches so well i somehow managed to ace a stem weed-out. extremely clear syllabus, engaging, interesting research, helpful and frequent office hours... what more could you ask for? never thought i'd look forward to an 8:30, and my morning commute is 90 minutes long. take intro phys w her!!

The grading is deeply unclear. Your grade in canvas doesn't reflect your grade in the class because they don't weigh exams in canvas until the end of finals. There's weekly extra credit but you get 0 extra credit at the end of the quarter unless you complete everything (this isn't in the syllabus and I only found out after emailing the prof).

Professor Brahmia is incredibly sweet and a great teacher. While this class has lots of different components, with the tutorial and lab sections, her lectures were a joy to come to. She is great during office hours and willing to help with any problems you have. She is also very understanding and accommodating to any extenuating circumstances.
Super awesome Professor who teaches even E&M well! Very enthusiastic and made this class *actually* fun to learn! Take this professor if you can : )

analysis.name: Megan Butler
