review_highlights.comment: She is an extreme hit or miss. One day she says she likes your work and the next she wants you to completely redo it. Swear she intentionally makes assignments due on the same days she KNOWS you have other shit due. Felt like a high school class and I didn't learn a single thing.

super discussion-based but everytime a student shares their thoughts, she guides their answers and opinions to match hers. It can come across as genuine encouragement sometimes lol. She's old-fashioned and doesn't allow electronics. Super tough and HARSH grader on essays. assigned 4 novels to read and articles every week. not hard, just a lot.

I really liked Professor Butler, she is a very passionate lecturer and implores students to dig deeper in analysis and discussions in class. Attendance isn't "mandatory" but strongly encouraged, although she is flexible with dates on assignments and gives lots of feedback on assignments and essays. Not a lot of work weekly other than reading.

She is an extremely harsh grader! She wants you to come up with a creative and out of the box idea but doesn't give any examples. You will be constantly reading books and will be quizzed on the smallest details. Many essays and discussion posts. She acts like her class is the only one you are taking. Students practically teach the class.

Fairly easy A, and she is passionate. But... she forces her opinions down others throats. She changed the syllabus and the entire class several times throughout the quarter and kept adding tons of assignments--don't expect to take the class you supposedly registered for. She's nice to me, but was very degrading to many other students.

analysis.name: Gust Burns
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He's not the worst teacher in the world or anything, but he's definitely up there. I will mention that this is his first year however, so who knows maybe he'll get better. All I can say however, is that he is very difficult to understand, and too abstract. In other words, don't expect anything out of going to class other than participation credit.

"Do not think of me as an obstacle to success" is what he writes in the syllabus, but I assure you, he is most definitely an obstacle. He just doesn't know what he's doing! His feedback is terrible, it's literally just him saying "redo this and that, oh and this is wrong". Period. No context, no explanation behind why, absolutely nothing.

I was excited to take English 182 as I had heard good things from friends about the class. I was especially interested in the multimodal aspect of the class. To my disappointment the class was barely multimodal was heavily focused on texts with little use of photos, videos, or audio. Overall I feel like this class was both a waste of time and money

I took ENGL&101 with him in Fall quarter and I'm currently taking ENGL&102 with him. Despite seeming intimidating at first glance and being a tough grader based on word choice, it's clear he wants everyone in the class to succeed. He's an enjoyable professor with his humor. Just don't use AI and make sure to communicate with him IN CLASS.

Easy if you actually do the work; overall, a great fella who is often caring, and his class environment is great, but active engagement during lecture is key with him. Overall, I recommend his class. A strict warning is that he's very strict on AI, and he's one of the few who actually checks everyone's work from top to bottom.

analysis.name: Brett Wortzman
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 119 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: His lectures were engaging, and the quizzes he gave were mostly easy. The programming assignments increased in difficulty and time required by quite a bit, but because you could redo many of them using resubmission forms, it was easy to achieve the maximum score. Issue: The final was longer and harder than a basic coding final should have been.

Great lecturer who explains concepts clearly but doesn't finish slides during class. Pacing can feel uneven at times, with more time spent on introductory topics and less on complex ones. Be prepared to practice independently, though there are plenty of problems provided. Grading can be strict, which is typical for this intro series.

Great professor and well-organized class but just difficult in general. The grading scale is makes it hard to determine your GPA during the quarter which is frustrating. They don't give Es generously so make sure to take lots of time on weekly assignments to build a cushion for the 3 quizzes. The final was much harder than the practice material.

I took his ethics class which is diff from 12X most students take with him. He's a great prof and he engages his students during discussion very well. You might get the sense the he's totally against AI but he encourages you to form your own opinion. The reading isn't a big deal, have a sense of what the chapter is about and you'll be fine.

Brett explained concepts well. He gave us many opportunities to ask questions and used thoughtful analogies to explain things. But, important grading criteria was unclear, so TAs graded assignments very inconsistently. This does not reflect well on Brett, regardless of who implemented this policy, because of the stress on us. Overall, he's ok.

analysis.name: Jessica Burstein
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 73 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Burstein is clearly an expert in her field & passionate. It's a shame that did not translate online. She was scattered/inconsistent, struggled to maintain discussions, never replied to emails, and graded w/o a lot of rhyme/reason. She p much clocked out by the end. Probably awesome in person, but definitely struggling with the pandemic format.

Overall, this class was kinda off. The teacher is energetic but can be passive-aggressive at times. The lectures went in circles, and when she asked questions, there didn't seem to be a right answer. The readings were interesting, but near the end, the objective of the class was unclear. Work is mostly reading responses so at least skim the plot.

Super chill professor! You can skip each class and still pass (just do your readings, please.) She posts the slides and (some) TA's give you a vocab "practice" sheet in quiz section, which is basically giving you 30% of the midterm/final exam. She doesn't tend to connect topics covered in class within class, so you'll have to do that individually.

I really enjoyed Professor Burstein as a lecturer, and found the readings and the formal analysis very interesting! However, tests (one midterm and a final) make up 70% of the grade for this class (the other 30% is quiz section participation). If you test well, this makes the class easy, but if tests are not your strong suit, it'll be a struggle

The midterm/final honestly felt totally unrelated to most skills/knowledge gained in the actual class. She would loose track of what she was saying and go on tangents. Every discussion was dominated by the same students because if anybody else spoke she was sort of rude to them? Def had favorites and wasnt very approachable. TAs were great, though!

analysis.name: Brian Buchwitz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 118 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Had him for bio 106 and I am grateful for it. He gave us groups to work in, and it helped my learning a lot more than just lecture. Everything is weighted equally including attendance so if you show up and try you should get a 4.0.  He taught us Meiosis and Mitosis but included more higher-level stuff (200/220) but it gave me a good footing for 180

Buchwitz is kind and patient when it comes to explaining things until they make sense. I personally found his lectures to be okay, though they could be better. He focuses a lot on how to read diagrams and pictures which is actually very helpful when it comes to taking his exams since the cheat sheet is very clear. Overall, not too tough on exams!

The lecture is heavily discussion-based. He expected you to know everything from the daily readings and teach nothing during lecture time. You would probably learn more from lab sessions since the TAs actually teach stuff there. Overall, I learn nothing from the class.

At first, I really hated this class because it's really discussion heavy, even in lectures. However, I actually grew to appreciate the teaching style. The course material is very fair, and the exams are alittle niche, but as long as you have a good understanding of the mechanisms its manageable. Really a great prof.

Nice guy, but get ready to learn on your own. Lectures are mandatory for participations points, but are kind of meaningless because half the time, we're doing polls and discussing with each other instead of actually learning in depth about the content.

analysis.name: Roger Bumgarner
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He's a good professor and I enjoyed this class. Very similar to Bio 200 and interesting topics covered, but coming to lecture helped a lot and the study guides he supplies on Canvas for each lecture! The exams are multiple choice and 70% of your grade. Averages around 75%.

Lectures had a LOT of content, but your grade is determined by some PollEv + at home, open-note quizzes. Super chill prof, deadpan boomer humour but interesting lectures. Wouldn't take again bc I would fall asleep, but not bad in grading + teaching.

Roger (MY WOKE KING) was such a pleasant professor who shared many personal stories and clearly is extremely passionate both about his work and his students. If your able, talk to him about his career because he has some crazy and impressive work experience!
he's a chill guy, exams require very in depth knowledge of material, so dedicate a lot of time to studying for this class

Excellent course, great professor. Sometimes moves a little fast but gives great answers to questions. Fun deadpan humor and clearly cares about his students and the content he is teaching. Tests are not gimmes but not terribly hard either. Would definitely take again.

analysis.name: Lauren Buckley
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Demoralizing class - harshest grading I've ever experienced. Would get marked down seemingly arbitrarily, despite submitting thorough/accurate work. Lectures weren't informative & instead weirdly confusing. Looked for very specific answers on exams. Even hw assignments were super difficult to 100%. She dodged questions & said to "ask your peers."

She has some aversion to making questions understandable. Everyone was confused all the time in class and these are not difficult topics, she's just bad. Two exams, a final presentation, and a final group research paper is insane for a three credit class. Grades harshly too. Don't take this class it's hard for no reason and not interesting.

Although I thought the class was okay as a whole (honesty kinda boring), Professor Buckley was not the best at teaching the material. The lectures were based on the flipped classroom model, which is already confusing for me, and she often had a hard time making simple concepts understandable. The labs and group project were pretty straightforward.

So unorganized and often contradicts herself. The questions she writes are always so confusing and she herself will tell us every time she didn't write it well and then does it again. Attendance isn't mandatory but there's usually an in class question you answer every week that's collected and graded. Group project + paper due at the end.

Prof. Buckley is passionate about what she teaches and is very approachable. Lectures though were not the greatest and I don't feel like I learned much. Kind of a flipped classroom style. Exams are closed book and all short answer. We were assigned a book but it was never brought up. One final "group" project that is mostly written individually.

analysis.name: Darren Byler
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Took this course as a “gpa booster” very disappointed, tests aren't hard at all but unless you dedicate the whole three hrs and take notes nothing will make sense. His lecture slides make absolutely no sense. He marks participation very hard so unless you talk during lecture you won't do good. Do not take this as a gpa booster.

Really intelligent and enthusiastic professor, so glad I took his class. He is very thoughtful and is great at facilitating approachable yet thought-provoking discussion in class. The class is graded on weekly grading responses and one or two essays, so going to section is helpful. Also brought us Christmas cookies, what a gem.

Two papers, midterm, and final exam, as well as quiz at end of each class. Exams were difficult and very ambiguous (lots of "all of the above"). Definitely not the class for an easy A. Still, Darren was interesting and taught using lots of first hand experience.

Great professor, you can tell he really cares about the subject matters. His lectures were easy to follow along with and he made sure to go over the concepts. Very easy to reach if you were having difficulties or need any guidance with the assignments.

Darren is among my favorite anthropology professors at UW. He cares heavily on how you learn and understand the content in the class. Would recommend him to anyone looking to learn about social issues in the US and around the world.

analysis.name: Krzysztof Burdzy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 107 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's a very nice person and passionate about his field. That said, he doesn't believe in partial credit on the weekly quizzes. Over half the class hadn't earned a single point four weeks in. There is a single midterm with not many questions. It is very easy to convince yourself of an incorrect answer. Hence, it is very difficult to score well.

His lectures are not organized at all. He doesn't explain concepts, rather just states the answers. His midterms were very poorly written and significantly harder than those of the other professors. He also has a confusing grading system in which he curves every grade but then removes the curve two weeks before finals. He's terrible.

Exams were reasonable, no unexpected content with everything being covered in lectures. Recorded lectures meant attendance was lax with the exception of a short 10 minute quiz every Friday at the end of lecture. His handwriting could be a bit hard to read sometimes but if you pay attention to his words it's easy to tell what he's describing.

I highly suggest NOT taking this guy. He literally does not care about his students, and has no sympathy for the current state of things. Look up the article about him in The Daily. He makes his tests "conceptual" which means they become way more difficult and no where near something that we've ever seen. He is not approachable and is very boring.

Exams MUCH harder than any of other prof's exams (after comparing with past archived and ppl from other sessions). Grading not lenient at all. Notes not organized and lectures hard to follow. Some useful techniques not taught (so reading textbook yourself is recommend). He answered hw questions on ed but mostly just gave the answers away.

analysis.name: Phyllis Byrdwell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Most rewarding class I've taken at UW, Professor Byrdwell is a great teacher and really gave us a thorough experience in gospel music. Organized, funny, and extremely personable!

If you do not know how to sing, then I would strongly advise you to not sign up for this class! Don't let the "no auditions required" subtitle fool you! You will be put on the spot if Phyllis catches you lip-synching or messing up the lyrics of a song. Great class overall, but too much work for a ONE credit class--rehearsals + a paper!

Singing African American church music is all we do during class. Very enjoyable for me. You only got one opportunity to skip lectures and we do need to attend two mandatory concerts and turn in a paper about African American church music to receive the credit. A little big amount of workload for a 1-credit class.

Phyllis is a legend, you gotta take this class!!! Even though this quarter was a crazy one, I always left her class in a way better mood and with a huge smile on my face. Also you don't need any singing background which i was very thankful for. Take it with friends if you can!! Live love Phyllis

This class is awesome! If you know how to sing/have prior experience then you should definitely take this class! She is strict(ish) but it's not really a problem as long as you have learnt the words - which happens naturally. It's an awesome class!

analysis.name: Caren Marzban
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 111 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The hw takes forever, you won't have weekend anymore, otherwise either get an A or F. as said below, he has some ego problem: acid, brazen, rude, sort of baseness, hauteur. He makes the students compete to each other, and fail the bottom 10%. My friends talk him for the grade, he said it was not his business, it was all about other students.

He comes off as egotistical and paranoid. He refuses to use precise mathematical terms in favor of vague gibberish even on tests, telling us "everything in life is ambiguous, so get used to it" when students get confused by it. He throws tantrums in class if you don't loudly answer his questions like "do you understand."  I would not recommend.

If you like artificial difficulty in the classroom then you'll love Marzban. One of the worst experiences at UW: useless lab section, lectures that are explicitly aimed at entertainment rather than teaching, and exams that focus on only the most subtle details of the material. Enjoy your single half-sheet of notes for the cumulative final.

Awful teacher and unorganized lecture slides. He is arrogant and his lectures make everything seem simple which is a real wake up call when his test are extremely tricky and difficult. Labs are completely useless and only go to take the quizzes. Awful class.

Probably because it was a summer course so the material was kind of squeezed.  But I didn't find that course helpful at all.  The lecture were okay, but all those stuff putted together in the exam was totally awful.  The explanation in lecture was not helpful at all. No extra practice test to practice which sucks.

analysis.name: Charles Camacho
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 106 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Not a good test writer… the 1st was too hard and involved question types never practiced in class. The 2nd he told us exactly what the questions would be, making it too easy. The order he teaches topics isn't the most strategic; my hs calc teachers structured their content better. He's also good at disappearing when people are bound to email most.

fought for my life to get a 3.7. he's really nice and decent at explaining concepts (VERY good at drawing 3D models!), but it's funny how he always says don't email me after releasing a grade💀 also the first midterm sent me spiraling and doubting my entire career like i cried several times

Charles brought a lovely attitude to math. He was consistent and always happy to help with questions if someone wasn't understanding. He creates videos to watch before very helpful lectures. While slow to respond to emails, he is about as accessible as a professor as I have had. Getting homework done timely is crucial to understanding content.

He is a good lecturer and the homework pre-lecture videos are really helpful but I have to downgrade a little for the awful first midterm that went over topics not covered in class and was worded terribly. I do believe that overall though its the the 12X series being the worst and less on the professor.
the absolute goat. actually cares about students, timely emails, so many review materials. makes everything clear. the best at uw

analysis.name: Carly Sheehan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Carly is a sweet and caring person! She is very orangized on assignments! The painting 292 was a combination of painting with printmaking. I learn lot from both subjects especially printmaking coz we spend most of time at printshop. I really appreciated her time and the class! It was what I look forward everyday to be there!

Professor Carly is amazing! She provides most materials in class which is super helpful, and gives amazing feedback tailored to your personal style. Her feedback allows you to hone your craft and push your comfort zone while also making sure your work stays really true to you. Truly an amazing professor and an amazing class!

Carly was awesome and helped me push myself creatively. She helped me discover my painting style, and I looked forward to going to class every day. She also provided materials for us to use in class, so we didn't need to buy more materials, which I appreciated.

analysis.name: Carson Miller Rigoli
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Lots of work throughout the week due on a specific due date, but there is also a 48-hour extension with no penalty, which helps a lot. The class is pretty easy if you don't make it hard for yourself. It's pretty simple; just get the final project done with a good group of 3!! Even if u know you don't want another person, add them; it would help!!.

Honestly, the only Best INFO 201 section is Carson Miller's. Trust me, someone who dropped from
Ott Toomet I can finally understand the criteria; the weekly assignments are not too heavy at all.
Midterms are just corrections; the labs are Chill. Just have a good group for the project, and you'll be fine!

Also make sure to do those lecture quizzes

Fall 25 - Pretty easy class if you've coded before. Even if you didn't make sure, you know someone who has. Honestly, if you don't know anyone there, the class will be so hard for no reason, so make new friends; He will also push that on us!!

- Every lecture he has a quiz where the prompt will be only up for 10 minutes 
- The Ta Are Tough Graders

Nice class. Attendance isn't mandatory but lectures aren't recorded so if you go the easier assignments are. Prof talks a lot during lecture but the info is good- he's also approachable & helpful. Tests aren't a huge deal, the important assignments are the bi-weekly ones and the project. Pace is good and you learn a lot of applicable things!

He and his TA are heavy graders, and they take forever to grade your assignments. Don't try using AI in his class, they would know easpacily for any data class. I wouldn't recommend ChatGPT; maybe another AI


Absolutely, build a study group where u guys can help each other out. I wouldn't pass this class if it weren't for them.

analysis.name: Carrie Matthews
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Carrie was great, and it's clear she's very passionate about what she teaches. The only thing I didn't like was that most things took a long time to grade. Everything except for the major projects is graded based on completion.
My favorite professor and class so far and Im not an english major

Very understandable, this was class is her first online class (if I remember correctly) and she very easy to communicate with. A LOT of reading fiction,if you enjoy reading or be able to read fast then it shouldn't be less of a problem. Homework and exams mostly required reading to answer questions and give thoughts, arguments and replies about it.
As long as you do all the work, you'll get a good grade. She's very passionate about what she teaches and genuinely cares that students are learning. If you speak up in class, she'll love you.

Carrie is a passionate professor who cares about her students and social justice. She does grade contracts, so as long as you do everything you sign up to, you get that grade. For papers you do intense group peer-grading, so you get a lot of valuable feedback. She isn't the most organized, but to make up for forgetting something she brought candy.

analysis.name: Cayla Key
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This professor has given me one of the most insufferable experiences of a class ever. Unfortunately, this was a class that I was excited to learn more about, however, with constant unclear assignment expectations, bad communication, and busy work rather than helpful work, I will not be missing this class at all. Please change something.

lots of homework, come with tough grader and few non sence taken off points. I was told not participate in class and been taken off up to 4 points, but I attend every class and participate in class activity. I got my p9 feedback after the end of the quarter, which cause me lose points in my p11. group work was harsh.

deduct points arbitrarily, boring lectures, and nearly 30% of the grade for the final project was docked solely due to formatting issues. Absolutely no consideration given to the students' worry on group projects and gpa

A nice professor who clearly cares and the subject -- if you make sure to set aside time and put in genuine effort you'll get a good grade. Beware assignments take longer than advertised. Moreover assignment requirements were incredibly unclear -- little communication between Cayla and TA over expectations and grading criteria led to confusion.

analysis.name: Megan Callow
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very easy to get an A in this class, but not in a "Megan doesn't care about looking into submissions" way - she genuinely looks at the effort and care put into an assignment rather than having right or wrong answers. She also gives amazing and thought provoking feedback. Would take again!

Really great professor that puts in 110% effort in all assignment feedback and comes through as a very caring professor even as our class was asynchronous. ENGL 296 was an engaging, yet laid-back class with a grading contract (putting in effort and turning things in on time gets you a good grade). I highly recommend taking it!

Megan was a fantastic professor who provided awesome and supportive feedback on all of the assignments.  There were 3 major projects, and you have a lot of room for creativity. This was one of my favorite English classes I have taken, and it is very easy to get an A as long as you participate and complete assignments on time.

Megan is SO understanding and makes an effort to reassure everyone that she's there for you not only for class assignments, but for emotional support as well. She cares about peer interaction and effort; as long as you put a fair amount of effort into the class, you'll do great! Don't hesitate to reach out to her if you need help (for anything)!!

This teacher is rude to people with disability accommodations. Any slight miscommunication and she will immediately switch her tone with you and become extremely passive aggressive. Her email was literally an essay about how she thought I was entitled and misusing accommodations. This class is an easy A otherwise. Proceed with caution.

analysis.name: Emily Carrington
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: A great upper level Biology class. Very interesting class content, no exams, and the teaching staff is very willing to help with weekly exams. She is a very engaging lecturer, and labs are low-stakes!

The class topic was interesting. The problem is that this class is a major 'You should know all this before I even teach you it' vibe and the grading reflects it, and she won't help you on any of it until after she grades it. Not to mention she just says you lost points and don't tell you what is wrong.

Emily is a no nonsense kind of person. I had her for FHL 420, and she did an excellent job of balancing out the rigor of the other courses with a more exploratory, ecology-focused program. She makes you feel like what you think a marine biologist is as a child. Highly recommend taking her class at least once for the fun of it.

analysis.name: Cecilia Bitz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is the NICEST professor that the UW has EVER had. She has AMAZING connections (having visited many top schools, I know this). With a LOR from her, I got top student fellowships into BOTH UChicago and Brown (and almost Yale) with a 3.18 GPA. Without her, I wouldn't be alive today. My biggest regret in life is that I didn't discover her earlier.

Prof. Bitz definitely leans on math in lecture, but it is very clear that she is genuinely interested in making sure everyone understands the course material (and will spend a lot of her own time outside of class helping people out). Super smart and super kind person.

shes a good person, very nice lady. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities, and a lot of dropping opportunities too which is hood. However, her slides are unorganized, too much info is on there, and completing the homework is basically like a Ctrl-F treasure hunt between slides.. Other than the fact that this is not a GPA booster, not bad.

One of the best lecturer at UW! It's 2hrs long, probably why ppl would say it's boring, but I found the material very interesting! Clicker q's help boost grades, gives extra credit on top of that, and many many opportunities to get a good grade. DEFINITELY RECOMMEND for this class and if she taught other ATMS classes, I would take them with her!

Easy teacher, many grade booster opportunities. Yes there's a lot of "facts", but nothing too hard to remember if u go to class. She puts up summaries every week, even podcasts online if u miss lecture or want to review! Quizzes r tough, but not THAT bad. She curves the grade with other scores so no complaints here. Book = interesting read.

analysis.name: Leah Ceccarelli
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Not the best lecturer she hops around & seriously not good public speaking skills BUT her class wasn't terribly hard. If you came to class & took notes on what was going on you were going to do well in the class because she allows open notes (SO TAKE NOTES) Honestly the class was mostly boring but if you want a good grade it's a good class to take.

One of the best professors at UW in terms of grading clarity and genuine engagement with the class. The structure of each class is roughly the same, but every session is different and focuses on a different speech, and its so clear that the professor understands the material inside and out. Always urges participation in the lecture.

She is alright, the video clips are a little rediculous at times. I did reasonably well in this class, but I had to work for it. There is alot of stupid busywork, pretty much due every other day. You need to go to class, as pop quizzes will happen the day you skip. real talk.

by far the worst class ive taken at uw. boring lecturer. too much reading. difficult tests. and so inflexible when it comes to grading. it makes all the work you do not worth it. i personally will never be taking a class with her again lol.

Repetitive, kinda boring. Quiz every lecture, lots of reading. No rubric for papers. Doesn't use slides, writes on whiteboard with bad, sometimes illegible, handwriting. Easy to get a good grade in the class, the process is just annoying. Content isn't worth the time spent.

analysis.name: Celia Lowe
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She cares a lot about her political views, but she doesn't seem to care much about students.  Lacks charisma to excite students.  Slipshod feedback.  Seems overly reliant on guest speakers, film, and group activities, making it seem as if she doesn't like teaching.  One of the worst teachers I've ever had.

Lectures are boring. There are long essay assignments, quiz, discussion post due almost weekly. You can only miss 5 points out of 400 points to get 4.0 in class. Asked her respectfully if she would consider rounding 0.08 points up so I could get 4.0, and she was passive-aggressive: "I will not respond to a plea." I would've taken no as an answer...

I took Celia's  "Climate Change and Global Health Class." It was horrible. My group was amazing, but they were the only good thing about the class. The lack of information pertaining to our essays and projects made it twice as hard for each student. I never knew what my papers were suppose to be about and had to "wing" it each time.

I'm kicking myself for taking her again (I took JSIS351 too). Like before, assignments have vague descriptions, so it's hard to know what to do. She offers little feedback on assignments. A module assigns 75 pages of textbook reading with no heads up, so then you're scrambling to keep up. Boring professor, not engaging at all. My worst class ever!

The worst class I have ever taken. Lowe is uncaring and unkind and lacks the motivation to see her students succeed. Her assignment instructions are unclear and confusing and she is unwilling to explain without a disgusting attitude. You read a very packed online blog this course it seemed which is hard to follow and never-ending. don't take her.

analysis.name: Luis Ceze
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Luiz is an excellent professor. CSE 351 has some very fascinating content, which Luiz explored in a way that helped students understand. He used metaphors and analogies effectively to help me get complicated topics. 10/10 would take again.

His lectures are amazing, clear, and precise, and he is enthusiastic. He even recorded an additional lecture for us to help us better understand an especially confusing topic.  He is ready helpful, friendly, and accessible outside of class. If you can't attend his office hours, he will find time for you, even if it means staying late on Friday.
Great lecturer, very clear explanations, would take again.

analysis.name: Dantzel Cenatiempo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dantzel was a wonderful teacher. I had a lot of fun in her class and even though the class was mostly review for me, I felt that I actually learned quite a bit. She is very kind, helpful, and her expectations as well as her accent are clear and easy to understand.

This class was really great. It was really obvious that she wants you to succeed and if you show up the quizzes and tests are not difficult because she reviews what will be on the test with the class throughout the unit. I really enjoyed this class and the other reviewers probably didn't go to class which is why they found it difficult.

She is very good at what she does. If you ask for help, she's willing to be there, and she makes an effort to interact and connect with students. Sometimes, her grading techniques are a little unfair (on presentations/interviews), but overall, she's very generous with grades. As long as you study and participate, the class is doable.

Great French teacher, definitely cares about her students and you will learn a lot. However, if you don't show up for practically every class you won't pass. A bit of a tough grader as well, and won't give you the information you missed if you were absent. That being said, great teacher and she cares.

Easiest class I have ever ever taken. She doesn't teach anything though, only the numerous online assignments do. All the guys think she's hot, so they like her.  To be honest, she's not even that good at french and makes mistakes all the time. She ruined my favorite subject for me

analysis.name: Celeste Manoucheka
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the worst classes I have ever taken at UW. The difficulty level is that of a high school class and her course content is merely a painful repeat of everything you learn in 201 and 202. The busy work is outrageous, her lectures are unorganized and explanations are not clear. No one ever knows what she is looking for. Waste of your time!!

Dr. Celeste is awesome! She is ridiculously intellectual and hilarious. Lots of reading in this class but it is all interesting and fun. I don't usually feel comfortable speaking up in classes but she is so sweet, open, and insirational that I felt totally comfortable raising my hand to answer questions when I knew the answers. Love her!!

She was really nice and when she actually was teaching she was really good, but a lot of the time she just read off of the slides, and it would get really boring. The tests are really long, and I think kind of hard. There are some really obscure questions about the texts.
Manoucheka has great energy, very clear, and is great to be around.  Her test are a little to long for my taste, but what is on the test is what she covers in class.
Bad and irresponsible Pro.. Avoid her at all cost !!

analysis.name: Cecilia Strettoi
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Cecilia is awesome. She is funny, kind and tells great stories to mix things up. She went out of her way to set up review sessions before every test and she is super helpful if you need it. She teaches to all levels of learners and gives chances for those doing well to move ahead and for those struggling to catch up. Could not recommend more!

Cecilia is by far the best instructor in the italian department. it is clear that she enjoys coming to class everyday, she talks to students as if they are her colleagues. Not only did I learn a lot, but she takes the time to get to know each student and recognize what their strengths and weaknesses are. you have to do the work though, its hard!

harshest grader in the department, but not unfair. she seems scary because she's loud and has a strong personality, but i liked her a lot. she's very kind and caring, but she will not take any crap from you.

I took her a few semesters ago, students would run through a brick wall for her, she is incredibly respected and by far the best professor in the Italian&French department at UW. If you not only want to learn a language but also want to learn about Italy and it's culture take her. She's passionate and will do everything she can to get you an A.

Few professors have the ability to capture & maintain the classes respect and attention like she does. What I like most about Cecilia is that she goes great lengths to ensure the success of her students. Not only is she insightful and know the material brilliantly but she is also hilarious (which makes the class fun and enjoyable). Highly recommend

analysis.name: Sophia Cisneros
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Syllabus did not outline units or due dates. Due dates changed frequently, mismatches homework and units. Scattered unlocking of assignments problematic as a full time worker. Assignments nearly entirely multiple choice, with correct answers never provided. Be prepared to do your own research constantly. Textbook had errors, lacks accessibility.

Cisneros is a very flexible professor & wants her students to succeed. The syllabus  lays out all work for the quarter with due dates. Sometimes assignment explanations can be confusing and in-class discussions are kinda pointless, but the lectures are helpful for the homework. Not really about the planets, moreso a physics class.

I liked the content of this class, but some of the assignments were annoying. A discussion post due every week in which you have to post your own response at least 24 hours before responding to 2 other people, sometimes I would forget since Canvas would show the due date as being on the Friday (when in reality it is a Thursday). Busy but easy work.

Super easy class. Good as an intro to the subject if you care, and good for an easy A if you don't. But some assignments are weird and rely on material not taught in the course. Online class so I didn't get to know her, but she seemed nice enough.

The class is extremely easy, but Prof. Cisneros' contribution to the class is nonexistent. The answers to quizzes aren't in her lectures, you have to google them, so I eventually stopped watching the lectures. Only the TAs grade, so she adds nothing to the class. It's a shame, because the content is fascinating, but I learned nothing despite a 4.0.

analysis.name: Barbara Citko
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I was expecting the class to be much harder but professor Citko is very nice and helped a lot during office hours which made the quarter a lot easier to get through. There are some big concepts in syntax but the professor is easy to get along with so I definitely recommend taking this class (even for fun! yes! syntax can be fun!)

I loved Prof. Citko! Syntax isn't my strong suit and we sometimes moved through topics quickly, but she did her best to keep the entire class on pace. Grading was super lenient, but the professor and TA gave good feedback, so it didn't feel as if I wasn't learning anything. Played livestreams of puppies during the 10 minute breaks!!!

I very much enjoyed Professor Citko's class. She is very friendly and approachable and does her best to help all her students. The way the class is structured is very forgiving in terms of grading, so it is quite easy to succeed. (All quizzes are open note with unlimited attempts and she drops the lowest quiz and HW score).
Really good professor for a difficult subject. Barbara did a great job this quarter

Difficult class but Citko is super good at presenting the content clearly. Class is mostly her lecture with a little bit of group work but she provides correct answers/explanations/alternative examples as much as we need. Grading on the weekly homework is really easy as long as it seems like you tried

analysis.name: Cindy Aden
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class (Community Engagement), seems to be way better for her to teach than the management one. Cindy definitely knows her stuff and is one of the nicest people I've ever met but her grading is...interesting. I like the way she encourages student interaction on Canvas. Class was not hard and had 3 very engaging assignments. I'd recommend her!

She seems like a perfectly nice person but she's off her rocker as an instructor. Very disorganized and goes on long tangents. We only had around 10-20 minutes of ACTUAL lectures a day in a 2 hour long class, the rest was completely useless. The essays were just busy work that didn't show what we learned at all.

Very, VERY nice person who is able to help you if you need anything, but the class content is awful and should not be required in the MLIS program. While management is relatively important to learn, the curriculum itself is outdated and does not take into consideration new developments.
Nice person teaching horrible content. Assignments are not useful. Goes off-topic a lot. Appreciate, however, that she is willing to talk about anything and help you with ANYTHING.
Online Fall 2022 - Cindy is SO nice but I really don't like how she teaches

analysis.name: Marika Cifor
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is super kind, caring, and a wonderful person. The class I had with her was really disorganized, but that was because we were figuring things out as a class. There weren't many assignments and not a lot of work in general, mostly the final project. One of the nicest professors I've experienced in terms of patience and friendliness alike.

She is very scattered with her lectures and slides. Most topics presented were extremely interesting, especially the readings, however her lectures are hard to follow because of how fast she talks. She does make an honest effort to meet with students and get to know them, especially with group projects. Easy on grading. Interesting class at least.

Dr. Cifor is amazing. She's so sweet and kind, and she's literally always ready to help you if you need it. This class was online when I took it and for a graduate class was very manageable. Readings were excellent. A must-take for MLIS students interested in archival services/administration. My one criticism is that she responds slowly to emails.

Marika is great. She's super helpful and cares a lot about student success. Only reason why I'm not giving her a 5 is because of some issues I had with this class's hybrid structure. Do the work, attend and participate, and be creative on assignments and you will be MORE than fine. Visit her in her office, she's very approachable in 1-1 settings.

My advice: take this class if you are an INFO major looking for an easy major elective. Assignments are very easy and readings are interesting enough to make you want to do them. Marika is a slow grader and responds slowly to emails, but she is a really friendly person and a good lecturer.

analysis.name: Christina Mastrangelo
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I had INDE with her Spring quarter. I thought lectures were helpful and tests were fair. I didn't love the required quizes but in the end they didn't impact my grade that much. Christina herself is approachable and kind.
This class was a lot more reading-heavy than test-heavy. Professor Mastrangelo is incredibly understanding and easy to talk to. Just be ready to read and write a ton about the textbooks!

Mastrangelo is by far the worst professor I have ever had. Regularly wrong answers, defensive and doubles down, wasting time and confusing students. Lies that topics will not be on midterms. Required in-class online quizzes despite lectures being a waste of time. No recordings. No exam prep materials. Use GPT to learn.

If she is the only option wait and take Patty Buchanan(greatest prof ever).She doesnt upload solved examples in class even though you may have illness or family emergency. She herself gets many of the examples wrong. Her lectures have a negative effect on understanding. She expects a 77 percent to be a 2.3. Best of luck(trust me you will need it).

Hands down the WORST professor I've had the displeasure of having. Unhelpful teaching style, little materials to prep for exams, and doesn't believe in recording lectures. Genuinely sorry for anyone who decides to take this class with her.

analysis.name: Rachel Cichowski
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cichowski has a fun and witty sense of humor, she definitely knows her stuff and is passionate about it, her lectures are very organized and are at the perfect speed for note taking, her study guides are a huge help for exams. She really wants her students to learn.

This is my favorite class that Ive taken. At the end of the day, Prof C really just wants to share her passion with us & get us interested in constitutional law & courts! You get plenty of time to work on the research paper, and the study guides prepare you perfectly for the tests. The lectures are well organized & interesting. TAKE THIS CLASS

Professor C was absolutely amazing! I signed up for this course on a limb to explore law, and was blown out of the water by how well the content was laid out, how helpful, knowledgeable, and kind Professor C was. You have to really study the study guide to do well, but if you do you'll be very successful. ASK FOR HELP FROM HER EARLY FOR UR PAPER!

I would recommend this professor to absolutely anyone! She is so smart and genuinely cares about what she is teaching and that the students are understanding it. The research paper was assigned super early and the midterm and final were completely based off the study guide. Took her remotely and all her lectures are pre-recorded. Amazing prof!

Most important tips to succeed in this class: go to class and write down the lecture slides, don't procrastinate on the research paper - start at least 2 weeks before and you will feel much better, and completely fill out the midterm and final study guides and then review them. If you do this a 4.0 or at least a good grade will be in reach! :)

analysis.name: Heather Clark
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Clark is one of the best professors that I have ever had. She is so passionate and knowledgeable about what she does and during discussions she is so eager about our own thoughts about class material. Some participation point assignments and one large group project, she gives you all the material but you have to keep yourself on track.

Dr. Clark is very welcoming & engaging. My only issue is that when it comes to the 3 big assignments her instructions can be vague and misleading (this caused issues for people at multiple points) and based on the feedback she doesn't seem to be actually reading the essays and is just spotchecking/skimming, which isn't fair to students.

Heather is the most enthusiastic teacher I have ever had. She really loves what she teaches and makes it engaging.  This class was LING203 and ANTH203. The only homework was one paper and it was relatively easy. This class was definitely geared toward freshman though. Overall she was a joy to have as a professor and I would love to take her again.

Really great class! Professor Clark is passionate about what she teaches and I learned a lot in her class. Participation is not mandatory, but she does have random participation assignments throughout the quarter. As long as you go to most of lectures, you should be fine! Plus, she offers extra credit. Highly recommend her and this class.

The class was really fun and Heather was a pretty good teacher. The final was really really hard though, but I still ended up with a decent grade. Not much homework at all, I got the textbooks and read them just because they were interesting and I think it helps to do so. It was overall a fun and great class.

analysis.name: Tai-Chang Chen
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Will need a good ta to understand concepts thoroughly. Lectures are very simplified and difficult to follow (do the readings before lecture to understand). Will test on niche topics that were covered very briefly in class. Nice and funny professor but not very effective, especially for a slower learner. Didn't record lecture or post correct slides

Tai Chen genuinely cares about his students, but he's definitely lacking as a prof. His final exam had a 21.2% STD— it's clear that he left a large portion of the class behind. For me, I found that most of his explanations were oversimplifications and didn't reflect the difficulty of exams. Find a good TA to make labs bearable if you take 215

Wish I could give this guy 6/5 to boost his average rating. Absolutely wonderful man that made sitting in the front row enjoyable and is a good reminder that you can absolutely get a lot out of lectures. He met with me regularly outside of office hours bc of class conflict and could take a concept I was stuck for hours something I could do 10 mins.

Very funny guy. Lectures were not always super helpful but generally got the job done, just make sure you can do the practice worksheets for the tests. Tests were not that hard and honestly very fair to the material he was teaching.

Pretty chill professor, gave good lectures with lots of information. Exams were straightforward, and he was very responsive through email and very accessible outside of class. Will take time to speak with you about class outside of office hours.

analysis.name: James Clauss
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Hands down one of the nicest professors I've had at UW. He has the energy of a goofy high school English teacher, which is incredibly refreshing and makes for a class room environment in which I don't feel nervous at all to speak or share my thoughts. The class itself is easy but very interesting/engaging, especially if you're into classic myth.
Clauss truly cares about his students and making sure his lectures are engaging!

Super kind, knowledgable, and encouraging. He wants you to think outside the box of typical classroom learning(ex. memorization vs. self reflection). Provided lots of interesting random facts at no extra cost! I didn't read The Iliad and still got 100% on the midterm, but I read the Odyssey and got 80%, so be thoughtful in your work.
an absolute cutie, knows his greek and roman mythology for sure.

Fun fun fun class.  Great prof, he's hilarious, he jokes around, really has fun with the class, which of course makes it more interesting to you.  I'd highly recommend this class to anyone and everyone.

analysis.name: Clint Robins
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I had him spring 2025, his first quarter teaching. Was a little unstructured bc it was his first quarter teaching, but you could tell he really liked his field and it was interesting hearing about his personal research. Expect to show up for every class with some readings before and talk in small groups over it. Def go and talk to him, W guy

Honestly very kind and genuine teacher that wants you to succeed. He's very good at answering questions and helping you workout thoughts. I think his tests may need some work as they are very reading oriented, like direct thoughts from reading which can be difficult with you know memory and such, but with that they are open note open reading tests.

Though it was his first time teaching, he cared about students, the material, and his work. While his lectures could feel a bit monotone, he brought in personal interests that added life to the class. The quizzes were oddly specific at times, but with more experience, he's sure to grow into a stronger and more engaging instructor.

He was a very nice teacher and accommodating. There wasn't a lot of homework, and was very lenient when grading. Assigned 3-5+ readings with some being up to 20 (or more) pages. Tested on specific things from reading, but all (+final) were open note.

analysis.name: Clara Wilkins
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Clara is a very nice person. However, as a professor, the same can't be said. She shows up to class unprepared, her slides are very disorganized and minimal, and she relies too heavily on studies to make sense of concepts. Her exams consist of memorizing various studies as opposed to theories related to social psych. Plus grading scale is tight.

I really enjoy her lectures, she seems like she knows what she's talking about and really engages with the class. She makes you feel like you can ask any questions. There's only 3 tests but the top two are averaged and lowest is dropped, so it's not that bad. I'd take a psych class with her again.

This class had the potential to be excellent, and I am sure it would have been better in person. The class is graded on mostly exams with a few assignments graded out of a couple points, so be wary of hitting EVERYTHING on the rubric or your grade will hurt. Lectures were just a past quarters recordings which got really annoying really fast.

Super easy class with very few assignments. Self-grading accounts for 40% of the total. 
It's definitely better to attend in person, as the class is discussion-based.
Also, she's cool.

analysis.name: Ellie Cleasby
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The lectures were super engaging and interesting! While they are recorded and the slides are posted online, attendance is pretty much mandatory because 8 random lectures (which you don't know beforehand) will have an assignment worth 1% of your grade. Overall easy and fun class, two open note online tests and one big final project.

Ellie is great! Her lectures are clear and informative, I was never bored. She's very responsive and helpful. She does give small participation assignments during lectures sometimes. Workload is very reasonable, moderate amount of reading (you can skim), with a research project at the end. Def my favorite class this quarter

The instructor is nice and good with feedback. One discussion post and one short (3-5 question) quiz per week, with midterm and final essays (4 pages minimum so pretty fair). There was some nitpicky grading here and there, but overall I enjoyed this course and was not overwhelmed by the workload.

Very accessible outside of class. Gives great feedback. Only minor problem I had was the weekly quizzes sometimes had unclear questions with no ability to get clarification. Other than that, awesome professor, loved her class!
Ellie helped make the material easier to understand

analysis.name: Claire Wagenseil
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you are wanting to take french take it with Claire. She is really nice and a very light grader, not saying studying is not neccesary because it is but she gives half credit for most questions on the quiz. She is really funny and got my french skills to advance quicker than any other langauge ive taken before.

Claire really helped me progress quickly in French. The class itself moved pretty quickly, but it was easy to catch up. She really emphasizes talking with a partner in French for a good portion of class, which I found challenging at times, especially because the class was every day.
Considerate and knowledgeable professor, runs a very straightforward and participation heavy approach to learning that helps students pick up languages surprisingly quickly.
Claire is super caring and wants her students to succeed. Her lectures and expectations are very clear and organized. Be sure to go to class and get ready for a lot of group work.

She is very good at teaching beginner French! I like how she does engaging activities that force us to speak in and listen to the language. She is super sweet and wants her students to succeed. I definitely recommend her!

analysis.name: François Clément
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Clement is a brilliant professor with a fairly ruthless grading style. Minimal partial credit is awarded (not zero but much less than average). His weekly quizzes are predictable and fair, focusing more on reciting his work than original thought. Exams are rough, but they are rough for all students. The curve is good.

The class was very hard and annoying because there were quizzes every single week, but I got the sense that he truly understands what it is like to be a student and only does this out of our best interest, forcing us to study the whole quarter, which actually makes the midterm and final much easier.

Agreed with the previous review. 4 Homeworks, 2 Exams, 1 Group Project. Good lectures, nice grading, but the course was just too hard and too fast, especially if you don't already have background knowledge like me. DP done by the 2nd week and Graph in 2-3 weeks. I took CSE 373 simultaneously and this course covered 2x the content in half the time.

Great at explaining concepts in lecture. Course is structured logically, fair difficulty.

Quizzes often based on minor proofs or theorems shown in class, which sometimes verge on memorization, so revise the notes before you come.

In office hours, he is more than happy to go over things you missed or clarify concepts in more depth, so use them.

François is great. He's honestly kinder than he needs to be. Makes difficult tests to encourage students to actually think critically. Scores will be low but the curve makes up for it. One of the most caring and attentive instructors I've had at UW. Highly recommend for a good learning experience.

analysis.name: Claudio Mazzola
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I liked his lectures a lot and he has a lot of good insight on his subject. He is not easily accessible outside of class and grades are not updated on Canvas, but he is very passionate and wants to engage students in dialogue and make the class fun. If students did their homework and were respectful, it was smooth sailing. He was fantastic!

Claudio is one of the sweetest professors at UW and genuinely cares about the content he is teaching! He does a wonderful job presenting the films in an interesting way yet sometimes he would get onto a tangent and the information would be unhelpful. He also does not provide grades until the very end so I had no idea where I stood.

My only complaint is that the class is graded on a few things, and he can be unclear about expectations for assignments, reflections, etc and can grade very subjectively. Other than that, he is terrific. He gets sad when people don't go to lectures, so please do!!!!!!!! it's so sad when he's sad. HIGHLY recommend him!

I enjoyed taking this course with Claudio. The expectations were pretty manageable, only watching films, a reading of 5-6 pages on each film, and an evaluation of each film. However, my only nitpick was the canvas was not very helpful, assignment grades were not posted on there so I don't know what my grade for the paper, presentation, etc. were.

He does not update your grades on canvas, I had little idea on how I was doing until final grades posted. Unreachable outside of class - did not check his email. He does not teach very well in class. He expects you to memorize your vocab the night before and then he quizzes you during class (with public shaming if you get the answer wrong).

analysis.name: Colin Marshall
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: More assignments than I expected. Just expect a bunch of weekly long reading assignments and reading responses. Three major papers. Small assignments are due in class, so quiz section is mandatory to attend. What annoyed me was getting randomly selected in class for discussion. Great professor though.

He had really interesting lectures, and he's funny. He answers questions well, and he's overall very understanding. He does do random call during lectures, but they're all easy questions. You might never even get called at all. The work load isn't bad. There's only one or two readings or videos to watch before lecture. I had fun in this class.

Colin's lectures are very intellectually engaging and well-organized. He's also very accommodating, easy to reach, and has a great attitude. Probably my favorite professor at the philosophy department!

Marshall is able to lecture in a very interesting and clear way. He obviously enjoys what he does and wants to share that with the students.  I only have two criticisms: (1)his left-wing politics enter the class more than should be the case. (2) Some topics we discussed would have been better for other classes, eg race, the second amendment.
Prof Marshall makes lectures engaging and personalized, and you can't help but laugh at his quippy jokes.

analysis.name: David Collingwood
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 78 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I was good at math in high school. I got an A in calculus, but it didn't count for college credits, so I had to take it here. DO NOT TAKE CALCULUS FROM COLLINGWOOD, ESPECIALLY ONLINE. There is so much homework, the tests are ridiculously hard, the lectures aren't very clear, and basically, I've never felt more dumb in my life.

I don't think he really cares about his students.  He seems like he's been doing this for long and maybe he's a little jaded?  His Midterms are ridiculous though, the concepts are applicable but he finds new and creative ways to bust you up. Maybe he's better in person but on-line?... Just don't do it.
The tests don't cover what he goes over in lecture. Seems to take pride in making his exams incredibly confusing (to the point where the average is a 40%). Do not take this class if you can help it.

Exams worth 80% of your grade. Course entirely based on lectures he recorded in 2020. Exams have an insane amount of questions, no partial credit, no note sheet, and sections where you can earn negative points for wrong answers. One office hour per week. Answer keys often have sections where he simply didn't feel like writing out the entire answer.

Terrible class. Tests include material that have never been mentioned anywhere. Lectures are not clear and when attempting to do homework there is a fair amount of material that you never went over. To add to it all, he does the classic assigning a ton of homework during dead week because he didn't assign it earlier. Avoid if possible.

analysis.name: Ryan Creedon
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: it's a huge loss to UW that he left. simply GOATED on all accounts. can only wish him the very best.

I would go over RMP's limit to try and get out everything I loved about this man. My only complaint is MATLAB only works the way you want it to about 20% of the time, no matter how experienced of a programmer you already are. But that is UW's fault, not Creedon's. Take him and you'll be one of the few UW students who didn't completely hate 301.

honestly just such a great guy above all else. he's enthusiastic about what he does, and it really shines through in his lectures. class is super well-structured and he's very clear about what you need to do to succeed. lectures are always recorded and homework is directly correlated to what's covered in class.

Good lecturer, clear expectations, has note sheets with everything written, no curveballs, lots of opportunity for extra credit, extremely flexible for late or missing assignments. You have a week to do all homework - plenty of time to get help. Open note tests and more time than necessary - low stress.

Very caring prof! He knows that there are issues with the accessibility with the topics often covered in math, and is making a HUGE contribution toward the change of that. Easily the best math prof that I've ever had, and will happily chat about topics not covered in the scope of the course :)

analysis.name: Jacob Cooper
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 155 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Biol 356 was the second class I've taken with Jake and it was probably the best decision I've made this year. I felt like I learned something new every lecture and the workload was very reasonable (The tests are way easier than 180). Also Jake brought the whole class Macaroons for Passover because he's the best.

Update: I actually ended up doing fine in his class, but omg it stressed me out so bad. Cooper has really hard tests, & I feel like he didnt accept my alternate explanations until later in the quarter. He is an AMAZING lecturer who makes sure his students have good understanding and feel cared for. Ultimately though, if good grades are hard, I hate

I went into the class thinking it would be the easiest of the intro series, but it was honestly the hardest. Every exam question felt like a trick question, and I don't think my grade reflected my understanding of the material. That said, I did enjoy the content, but the class structure was not my favorite.

Dr. Cooper is very likable and engaging but his tests suck. It's very unclear what content from the slides he actually tests you on, there are few practice problems, and he goes very big-picture when talking but is very detail-heavy on tests. Also, his exams have the same issue as other bio series and focus too much on keywords and not concepts.

He teaches on niche scenarios and doesn't explain broader concepts and then tests on other niche scenarios that have nothing to do with either. You get graded on how well you can read his mind. He puts out four poorly worded practice questions. This class is impossible, and I did well in 180 and 200, I am not fluent in mind reading.

analysis.name: Brock Craft
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Disorganized, seems to not know what's going on in class. Instructions not clear, written on assignments differ from the verbal ones given in class- also change on the day/person asking. Very little time to do assignments. The Mill can get very busy, when everyone is trying to complete things on time, often staying very late. Content was good tho

Took this class in fall of 2019. Lectures are engaging and fun, takes the time to know every student and remembers them. Ive had three classes with Brock and love his style of teaching! He doesnt believe in memorizing and spitting out info on tests; instead he has quarter long projects that are fun and help you learn hands on! My favorite prof!

This was my third class with Brock and honestly I hate information visualization. Stats, data, and graphs are all boring to me but somehow Brock made lecture interesting and engaging! Learned a lot from this class and Im glad I took it. Brock makes you feel like a friend rather than a teacher talking at you, genuinely wants to help you learn.

Brock's a cool professor who clearly has a lot of knowledge and experience in the field of physical computing. The classwork is understandable and very doable even though I wasn't very familiar with the subject matter. Grading techniques were effective and he allows for people to work together through the class.

Brock is amazing! I took this class in 2019 and his lectures are never boring. He actively asks for student feedback on his teaching methods and immediately implements them. Makes you feel like he genuinely cares about your learning! Highly recommend.

analysis.name: Juliet Crider
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Juliet is a very fair teacher. Her lectures were interesting and her availability for help is impeccable. Lectures never felt rushed, the class was very engaged asking questions, and she was always happy to answer them. She was able to help me with stuff from outside of class 1:1. You will have to put in time to study, but it's all reasonable.

ESS 212 was a fairly chill class; all of the exams were online and open-note. However, Juliet isn't engaging as a lecturer since she speaks slow, and the first five weeks of the class were basically repeats of the assigned pre-lecture videos. She is more than happy to schedule office hours outside class and was very helpful with the final project.

I loved Prof. Crider! Her class led me to the decision to minor in ESS at the UW. She didn't post lectures online so you have to attend class if you don't want to fall behind. She gives great study guides before each test. Really spend time studying them and you'll be fine! Only used textbook for clarifying certain topics, but never read it for hw.

This class is the most awesome and inspiring class ever in ESS. Topics are interesting and easy to manage if you like geology. Labs are great, fun and easy if you work hard. TA taught extra informations during labs, love it. Tests every 2-3 weeks, but they are all MC questions, not that hard. Best prof + TA ever!!! Recommend if you like geology.

If you're expecting a remotely easy class, look elsewhere. Despite poring over the textbook and studying extensively from the study guides, there isn't much to be done as far as getting a good grade goes. Lectures touch on unrelated topics often, and points are taken off exams at will. Labs are impossible to get full grades on.

analysis.name: Cristina  Sanchez-Martin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Interesting content, but poor grading. The grade conversion is very strict, and there are few assignments. Losing even 3-4 points in the entire class can drop your grade significantly. There are no rubrics for assignments, so grading is a guessing game. Professor can also deviate from grading scale and assign lower grades.
A really sweet professor, who is encouraging. She was welcoming and made sure everyone had a chance to contribute.
the only drawback of this class was the group project. otherwise cristina is so kind, caring, and knowledgeable, and can't recommend her enough.
I love Cristina she is awesome.

Really sweet and super nice,
Some group projects and she loves to listen to outside perspectives.

analysis.name: Cristen Harris
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Such a sweet prof who's always happy to chat with students and answer questions. Content was interesting and I overall loved the class. There was one project that felt a little disorganized and was graded harshly that I know most people didn't like (pop. diets one) but other then that workload and exams are fair!

I took nutr 415 in winter it was mainly group work reading. I took nutr 406 in au 25 very easy, there's a group project and online multiple choice exams. poll ev in class as participation. She is very nice she reopened an exam since I forgot to take it

i LOVED dr. harris! her lectures were super welcoming and her course was well organised. there's no hw assignments (only weekly quizzes), and that + exams are online open notes (hard to fail!). she is super friendly. she does use pollev for participation but there are drops! would 100% take again

Easy A+. Was free to talk with after every class and can talk about applicability of certain foods to your own diet that she is happy to explain. Extremely easy course, classes went over readings that took 15-25 minutes. Exams and quizzes are online and open note and textbook.
Dr. Harris is a great professor who taught me a lot of valuable information. Super great and engaging lectures. I recommended this course to all my friends.

analysis.name: Cricket Keating

Literally the kindest, most accommodating  prof you will have. Easy assignments lowk a lot of reading but you'll be okay. Just truly very kind person and you can feel that she cares about you personally

Cricket is the epitome of the word flexible. They really care about creating the best learning environment possible.
