Listening to them think and speak brought me so much inspiration as an activist and feminist scholar.

She really grew on me! Extremely flexible to students needs. Reach out for accommodations and she will meet u with understanding. Genuinely cares about their students which feels very rare at this school

There is no structure. We read feminist theories and discussed them all day every day. We were told to lead discussions, create "class rules", and even create prompts for our papers. Cricket's a lovely woman but the class was boring and long. We are graded on 2 essays, participation, classwork, and final project (AND ALL ARE WORTH 20% EACH)

Leaving this review while currently in the class because wow. I've had my share of tough professors/classes but this is by far the worst. You NEED to do all the readings and also recommend watching vids ou

She does not teach. Although she may be nice, everything you learn from the class will either be from the textbook or simbio. I repeat, she does not teach. Yk that one meme where a student interrupts his high school teacher by getting up and telling her that she should actually be teaching and connecting with the students face to face instead of just handing them a packet yo

That's this class

analysis.name: Larry Cushnie
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Larry was a FANTASTIC professor, his lectures are incredibly engaging and he obviously very deliberately chooses our class readings. As a hard core STEM student that hasn't taken a liberal arts class in over two years, I appreciated how much feedback he gave, and that he was always available to answer even the stupidest of my questions.

Professor Cushnie took over 318 for the last few weeks of the quarter after our original professor had a family emergency, and he could not have done a more amazing job. He is funny, caring, understanding, and incredibly intelligent. It was obvious he worked incredibly hard to make the transition of professors seamless, and he did a phenomenal job.

Professor Cushnie is a fantastic lecturer. He's hilarious and engaging, but still gives you tons of information in a very digestible manner. Guest speakers were cool, but they were hit or miss. Easy grading, no tests, and you can skip most of the readings if you pay attention during lecture. Super nice guy and would definitely take again!

Great class, I learned a lot about labor studies, very informative. I love his lectures, he kind of sounds like the Khan Academy person. One thing, he grades kind of tough. Definitely follow the rubric, if anything strays from the rubric, it's usually marked off a few points. Maybe even go above and beyond.

I highly recommend Dr. Cushnie's class. His lecture always makes students focused and interested. Be sure to take the course during the regular quarter because the course load will be slightly heavy during the summer A/B term.

analysis.name: Kyle Crowder
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Crowder is one of those tough professors. Will not take any late work. Must do the extra credit and class is highly competitive for grade. He speaks so quickly about complex terms that it was hard for me to understand and apply. Seems to be more concerned with his research than teaching.

Prof Crowder taught this course in a manner that was satisfactory for an introduction to sociology class. He definitely knew most of the class was not Soc majors, and the course content reflects that.

Literally I love prof. Crowder so much. He's super nice and his lectures aren't boring. His tests are lowkey easy if you go to lectures and do the readings. He is so organized it's so amazing!!! DEF recommend him!!

Crowder is a mediocre professor compared to other professors in the department. Warning, if you take the class, be sure to do the extra credit. Even though he claims not doing the extra credit won't affect your grade, the final grade percentages are curved to factor in the extra credit, so if you don't do the extra credit you will get a lower GPA.

I don't usually write reviews unless I've had an awful or exceptional experience with teachers. I am happy to say, that Crowder is one of the great ones. It is rare to find teachers whose number one priority is the learning of the student. He truly wants you to get a lot out of his class and not just a grade. I really appreciated his motivations.

analysis.name: Jeff Curtis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Isn't 1 level class supposed to be an introductory appreciation course? The workload feels like a Harvard graduate seminar. Most students taking this class aren't even dance majors, they're either just casually interested or short on credits, and you still expect academic rigor as if you're the only serious professor in online education

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I'm a senior about to graduate with honors, but the time commitment demanded by this class will bring your grades down significantly. HOURS of busy work per day for "study guides" where he wants you to search readings for minute, specific quotes. Don't be fooled by other students' claims that the class is easy - it's not

Take this class only if u've no other choice. This isn't ordinary DANCE 101A Class but more like Dance&History,senior level. Every week you gotta:Read lots readings;Watch many&long videos;Submit study guide wmany QS;Participate in Discussions,3writing papers,quizzes,mid&final exams wessays submissions;Extras.  Very tough if u'r not a dance major!

I'm halfway through the quarter and regret this class.  The workload is really high even for a typical overzealous online class.  I expect to get a B in this class, but if you do not have time for a solid 15 to 20 hours per week on one class I advise you not to take this one.  The topic is amazing, but the approach is overwhelming.

Took this class for VLPA thought I should write a review on why you should not take this class. This is not your usual VLPA class. 2-3 study guides a week which take a long time to complete, hour long videos that can't be sped up with no captions. There is a lot of busy work that will affect your other classes.

analysis.name: Curtiss Lyman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I've never met a professor who cares as deeply as Curtiss does about the success of each and every student both in and out of the classroom. His lectures are amazing and energetic, his exams are fair and well-written, and he will go out of his way to give you every opportunity to succeed. I haven't had a better mathematics instructor!

Curtiss is a fantastic professor. His lectures are helpful and spaced out well. He is very caring for his students and made an 8:30 class something to look forward to. Coursework is not very hard as long as you space things out. Would highly recommend.

This class was one of the easiest math classes I've taken at UW thanks to Curtiss. I heard many stories about professors being tough graders, but for this class the homework was very straightforward and exams quite manageable.

Curtiss is such a great teacher and person! You could tell he cared about his students and looked forward to teaching us, even if our class was super dead (to no fault of his). He never gave up on trying to communicate with the class and keep us upbeat even during an 8:30. Loved having him as a teacher and I'm going to miss him. Totally recommend!

Curtiss was very passionate about his teaching, therefore always happy to help students further understand the material. He was always happy and upbeat, even though it was 830. He also responded to emails within minutes which is always very helpful. if you have a choice, choose Curtiss, he's great.

analysis.name: Rebecca Cummins
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: This class is based on a very subjective criteria. Although it's an intro to photography class, you're expected to know how to photograph professionally. I dont recommend taking this class it's not within your major. Also, Rebecca couldn't have a care in the world for her students. The lectures are pointless, I have yet to learn anything...

This class actually stressed me out because I didn't really know anything about the techniques of a camera. And to have all of the people who do makes it intimidating. Rebecca is an amazing prof; extremely nice! In class you have to critique your peer's work, and vice versa. This is a little nerve-racking too. Overall fun class. Got a 3.4.

Rebecca was a really great prof, and I would highly recommend to incoming art students. Sometimes she didn't always give feedback, but she was really receptive and helpful when I reached out to her. She definitely cares about her students, and her assignment outlines were very clear. Lectures were interesting and useful.

She is an amazing professor and is very accommodating. Extra credit is offered, and she reminds when the opportunities arise. She warns that 4.0 is a harder grade to receive (she associates it with graduate and professional level work). She responds quickly, and offers help/feedback outside of office hours.  She brings a lot of energy with her.

The lectures of this class are extremely boring. She has no organization whatsoever. It's not a good class to take since everything is based on opinion- I'm surprised rebecca hasnt changed her class structure despite all the negative feedback. The interest level of the class is extremely low. Oh well...

analysis.name: Asher Curtis
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class was entirely case based. No tests. Each case takes A LOT of time (especially the group cases) so be prepared to spend about ten hours a week just on those. Most cases had very little to do with accounting, more on data analysis. He is a slow grader which can be frustrating since your whole grade is just based on cases and participation.

He's a Masters in Data teacher. I don't know why he teaching undergrad!!! He cruises through the lectures and answers questions like we're already supposed to know. The material itself doesn't seem that hard but the way he teaches it is hard to understand. The IS kids in the class are going to do well but the finance/accounting kids are screwed.

This class is a lot of work, but Asher makes that very clear. I did not think that I would enjoy this class, but for what it is worth, Asher makes it a lot better. He is very funny and engaging and loves what he teaches. The only thing is that he is a slow grader, so it is hard to gage where your grade is at.

analysis.name: Cynthia Chang

review_highlights.comment: I have taken Bio 180 before and gotten a 4.0, I was barely passing this class after Bothell did not accept my previous course. None of the study guides prepare you for the exams. The exams are all fill in blank and short answer, no multiple choice. I heard from another student she was not in her office during office hours.

Dr. Chang seems like a nice person, but she's very disorganized and a poor lecturer. Her tests aren't hard per se,  but they're very poorly worded. I already knew most of the information due to having taken this course at another university, but if I was coming in blind like most of my classmates, I would have been super confused.

Lectures are so confusing and she goes way too fast. Expectations are really unclear for exams and the fact that theres no multiple choice makes it nearly impossible to succeed. Even if you do all of the reading, there will be plenty you dont understand. Take another professor.
I wish I could take Dr.Chang again for future lectures, she's super sweet and her lectures go by so fast. Her exams are basically all things from lecture so attend them!! 10/10 prof

Prepare for a quarter of confusion and frustration. Clickers are graded, reading quiz before each lecture. Just do the worksheetsshow up to lab to keep your grade up. Exams are brutal. Class averaged 42% on the first exam, and it didnt get much better after that. Also, dont buy the book! This class asks for 5th ed but you need 4th ed for Bio200

Stanich was fine, theres no chem 110 option but thats what I had her for. Stanich is fine no complaints I suppose very middle of the road lecturer

Professor Stanich was great for Chem 110. Lectures were clear and taught the material well. She also provided practice tests for all the exams (including the finals) which was incredibly helpful. Very approchable and willing to answer questions.
I took CHEM 110, which was an easy class in general. HW was significantly harder than the exams, which meant that succeeding was easy. So the curve was also crazy and you need above 90% to get 4.0.
Doesn't teach tbh. Reads off slides and is not helpful. Exams are harder than practice exams.

One of the better math professors, mostly because most of them suck. She's a good lecturer, the homeworks are pretty reasonable, and the tests aren't too bad. Overall she's a solid choice.
Class was hard but Vinzant did very good lectures, very clear at teaching hard stuff

Read the textbook, but the Supreme Conflict book isn't really needed. I didn't mind the name tags and sitting with my section, I got to know people better that way. Moot court was fun too!

Cindy was great, really personable and fun. This was a negotiation class and the material was interesting and useful for every day life. My only complaints were that her lack of organization and strict guidelines was sometimes distracting. She is laid back, but more expectations from here would have been nice. Otherwise, great prof!

I took a special topics class with her (negotiation) and i LOVED it. it was a 4 hour class once a week and she actually made it work! her assignments were totally reasonable (reenacting negotiation scenes! and some writing) and she wasn't picky about turning things in on time. The material was interesting, the book wasn't bad, and her tests were straight off the practice tests. The portfolio grading system meant that you were practically guaranteed a 4.0. I was thinking about going to law school and this class convinced me that I should. Definitely take this class.

analysis.name: Dave Montgomery
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: one of hardest and least rewarding class I have ever taken. The workload was well over 30 hours a week, for the 100 level course. Exams are quite difficult and can drop your grade so definitely study.

I love Dave so much. He is such a genuine human being and really loves his job. Who knew soil could be so interesting. BUT BEWARE. He lectures ESS230 with Chuck Nittrouer who is a bad lecturer. It's almost not worth it to take this class because Chuck makes it extremely hard. The field trips (3) were fun but 12 hours each. Dave is in a band! WOW

Not an easy 4.0 if you are looking for an easy class for gen-ed credit. However, Dave is very intelligent and thought-provoking & there's easy homework. Insightful class just oddly difficult for being 100 lvl.

Hands down the worst professor I've ever had at the university. While my grade in the class was fine, it was not worth the struggle. analysis.name: David Mukasa
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Terribly structured course. Group project for a 6-10 minute present that you can't choose group members for an async class. 3000 word draft of final project + a random 500 word writing on the same week instead of moving the writing to the next week with the peer review. Grading rubrics unclear and expect to lose ~5-10% on HW to nitpicky grading.

I made an account specifically to rate this class. Do not take it. I read the reviews here and thought I'd manage but no, this class expects way too much out of you for a 101 "introductory" course. Apparently the coursework is *easier* from the last quarter it was taught, which has me praying for the poor souls of the past. 

Avoid like the plague.

This is by far the toughest class I've taken and you'll spend too much time just completing assignments. There are required readings, which are a minimum of 6 hours a week on top of 2 hours of lectures, a quiz, and an assignment that takes hours to complete. 
This class is interesting, but save yourself the stress and find something else.

There are 2 exams (4 questions 200 words each), 1 group project (auto assigned groups, requires a video and slides), quizzes every week, and a write up assignment requiring citations every week until a final paper (also requires 6 min video). There is a lot of reading to do as well as video lectures (not made even made by the professor). Terrible.

Had to take this class to get into my major—take something else if you can. Lectures are overly long and dull, and the assignments are more time-consuming than you'd expect for an online introductory class. You only get a week per module, but not much flexibility to work ahead. TAs also aren't very helpful and are just there to take points away.

analysis.name: Ann Culligan Voorhies
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 284 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The worst teacher I had in UW. She didn't prepare for the classes, no logic, just scattered aroud. Funny tones, speaking fast. DON'T TAKE HER CLASSES.

The only thing that really sticks out to me is that Dr. Culligan talks SO FAST. It's so hard to catch what she says because she doesn't even stop to take a breath. I would definitely recommend taking this class with a different professor.

I initially took this class because everyone told me it was an interesting, easy A. Don't get me wrong, it was an easy A, but I just don't think Psychology is my cup of tea; at least, not the way Culligan teaches it. She drags ON and ON and makes you despise the content SO MUCH that you get sick of it. I suggest you take it with someone else.

Assigned over 250 pages worth of articles in the last two weeks that were going to be on the final. Doesn't respond to students in regards to grades received. Lectures are virtually obsolete but you get forced to go because of poll questions. Leaves poll questions open for two seconds so be careful on your bathroom breaks
She can be very demeaning and condecending to her students at times. She often tried to force comedy that doesnt always work. She she talks very very fast and will use 2 slides in one hour.

analysis.name: Stephanie Deumer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Easy class for requirements since it's mostly discussion posts. I don't know how the TAs were, but I was assigned to her group and the quizzes were easy and doing the art projects can be straightforward if you watch all the lectures. People interested in modern art would really find this interesting. Attending office hours was not mandatory

She doesn't actually teach. Course content is from 5 years ago, and it is a few people (who aren't even involved in the course anymore) just reading off papers. She only interacts with you via grading and the occasional canvas announcement, and my friends and I noticed she would copy and paste the same vague comments on all of our assignments. Lazy

This was an amazing course! I loved learning about new media art. Before this course I did not care about art, especially modern art. But now, I love it! This course is marked by weekly discussions, 2 quizzes, and 3 large assignments. I encourage everyone to take this course, because artwork delves into all fields of science and expertise. Awesome!

I loved this professor! The course was inspiring and eye-opening. I didn't know anything about new media art before taking this course and now I feel like I am an expert. This course will challenge your curiosity and writing skills. The three major assignments were my favorite. Writing heavy, but the ability to create my own artwork was fulfilling

Considering this is a generic gen ed that most do for just the credits, it's quite tedious. TAs grade unnecessarily harshly and mark points down to avoid giving out 100s. In my case, TA docked me 1 point for final assignment for a rather stupid reason just to avoid giving a 4.0. In the end, the class is still pretty straightforward and easy.

analysis.name: Debbie Kelley
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Kelly is very kind and caring, but not the best teacher. Her lectures are hard to follow and the quizzes arent very easy. Its clear she really cares about the topic, she just doesn't teach it very well. Assignments are given in each class and due at the end of class. There's extra credit and 3 quizzes.

she was a decent prof, not the best but def not the worst. i took it as an easy A which it was but the tests were like 10-20 questions and simple but if u don't pay attention then it would obvi be bad. participation/credit is taken by writing down 6 facts from the lectures and turning it in at the end of class.

Deb doesn't organize well, but she is very supportive and obviously wants you to succeed. This class was less of a class and more of a weekly check-in meeting, and I would've appreciated more structure with it. What Deb lacked in teaching, she made up for in enthusiasm and caring.

Deb means well and is a nice person. However,she should not teach this class. Lecture was the most boring part of my week and her TA's graded papers so harshly. Deb does offer a lot of extra credit, but good luck getting help with finding information! Do not take this class, unless you like  torturously boring material. Worst class I've ever taken.

Deb is very inspiring and kind.  She's willing to help explain anything that you are confused on (which ends up being a lot) and cares about the students more than any professor I have ever had. That being said, the class is extremely confusing.  Nothing is clear and I didn't learn much.  Each 3.5 or above with minimal effort. I got a 4.0

analysis.name: Delancey Wu
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Wu is amazing! She goes really in depth with her explanations which is really nice. I can tell she really cares and wants her students to succeed. She also never really judged students for answering her questions incorrectly, and also made an effort to learn names. I would 1000% take a class with her again!

I LOVE DR. WU. This class has a lot of writing, but it is super interesting, and she is super accommodating of student needs and preferences in the class. She is all around caring, sweet, and knowledgeable on the subjects she teaches. Her answers to your questions are also super good and promote further learning. Love her.

Dr. Wu is really good! The exams aren't hard at all. You can use index cards, so as long as you study, you'll be fine. Just be aware that there's a big group project throughout the quarter during quiz section.

Dr. Wu's lectures were very informative! It's very clear she is passionate about her work and helping others succeed. There are a few readings every week to help understand lectures. You definitely need to internalize the information given in lecture but with the way the class and lectures are structured, you're pretty much set up for success.

Wonderful and passionate about her work. Multiple opportunities for extra credit. Connects textbook material nicely to lecture content. Canvas and lectures well-organized. Easy to talk to if you have any questions in office hours! Does include a quarter-long group project w/ presentation, but as long as you keep on top of the work you'll be okay!!

analysis.name: Deborah Porter
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The class is all about learning about what the professor wants. It's very objective learning and you don't have room to create your own idea because she shuts you down. It's not fun. If you respect yourself do not take this class.

The worst professor I have ever encountered. very not clear on what she wants out of the assignments, and grades you down if you don't get her expectations. a very strange setup of her "three sentences" practices and tests. Her tests are hard, long, and answers are usually very subjective. Her subjective grading is very frustrating.

Unfortunately this class isn't what I expected. We have to watch 7 films, several of which are horror or psychological thrillers (not fun). Additionally she is very unclear and even changes what she wants for an assignment after the fact. She is also too involved in discussion forums. This class is for her interests and I'm finding it frustrating.

Honestly I regret taking her class. Yes she is very knowledgeable when it comes to Chinese history. But her lack of knowledge and attention on other Asian cultures really bothers me. And keep in mind that She is very, very, very subjective. So wanna pass? Agree with her points. And beware that her tests are hard and she is a really tough grader.

Professor Porter loves the sound of her own voice. Her lectures are half common sense and half word vomit. There is almost no effort put into the lectures and assignments. All the tests are multiple-choice, but all of the questions are deeply subjective. Assignments are hard to understand, and she is hard to reach with no weekly office hours.

analysis.name: Matthew Depies
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 83 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Autumn of 2025: one of the best professors I have had at UW. Was very worried about doing well in this course but professor depies explained every concept from ground up, not proceeding until he was aware of everyones understanding, office hours were amazing (recommend) and lectures were perfect! Emphasized understanding over test taking skills

Very kind and funny professor who wants his students to learn and understand. Easy 100% in the 40% category of pre-lectures and clicker questions so mainly graded on the 60% category for exams which can have tricky questions. If you pay attention and practice the concepts, you'll succeed.

Never took physics in high school & was super scared for this class. Dr DePies is one of the best profs i've ever had & made it very clear what it takes to succeed. Great in lecture & easy to get a hold of outside of class. Helped me one on one several times and seemed like he cared about my success. Tests typically easier than practice questions.

didn't like how all sections are combined for tutorial, makes it hard to ask questions. clearly depies doesnt make the slides so hes lowkey confused/unprepared during tutorial. but hes truly truly a wholesome guy. he has funny (and slightly concerning) life stories that he relates to lecture content. anyways tutorial meh but lectures informative!

Very engaging and fun lectures; gives real-life examples and lots of practice. He actually remembers what it was like being an introductory physics student and actively tries to improve our experience. Go to his office hours! He talks about not just physics, but also just goes on random tangents, and everyone has a great time.

analysis.name: Debbie Paulsen
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Debbie Paulsen I am such a huge fan. There are few words to describe how iconic and amazing this woman is. I love Dr. Paulsen, she is a fantastic (and hilarious) lecturer who does a phenomenal job of explaining concepts and preparing students for exams. The structure of the class is easy to follow and I feel like I've actually been learning.
she lectures wih a teleprompter and writes things out while explaining them. Very easy to understand and gives you the resources to do suff on your own. One of the best lecturers ive had.
Professor Debbie is the BEST PROFESSOR at UW. I LOVE HER CLASS, wish she could open more classes. MAKE me love stats. SHE IS AWESOME!!!! explains everything so well, so nice and kind

I LOVE DEBBIE! She is one of the best professors at UW and you can tell she genuinely cares so much about teaching and her students.The BS seems scary because of stats but Debbie makes it all so much easier to understand! She will always stay after class to answer questions and will literally be awake at 2am answering questions on ed discussions.
A great approach to teaching statistics, and a reasonable set of expectations, content, and lecture style that helps you use this course as a resource in later work.

analysis.name: Santosh Devasia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Santosh is a great lecturer, he gets a 4 because his notes are pretty poorly organized, but he tries to connect what he's teaching to the real world at all times and all the content in his class seems directly useful. His homeworks and tests are fair, I didn't do very well in them but they were fair
Vibrations with Devasia was difficult, but I learned a ton and the topic really resonated with me.

Devasia is a pretty cool guy but his lectures are fairly useless in the context of the class- any understanding I have gained from this course is just from reading and re-reading textbook sections. In addition, homework is poorly connected to the lectures and exams are even further disconnected from the whole class.

analysis.name: Vinod Dharmarajan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Vinod is a good professor, especially for a grad student. His lectures can be confusing as individual practice problems get expanded, but he still teaches the material effectively. His tests are very challenging, as they are all written answer questions (no multiple choice), but he offers lots of office hours and is good at clearing up confusion.

Vinod is very helpful and accessible. Even though his accents is hard to understand sometimes, he did a good job to clarify(but remember to ask during class so that you can get participation points). I would say his grading is strict but you should be okay as long as you follow the lecture and do the worksheets.

Vinod was adored by a lot of my peers; he clearly cares a lot about student success! He's very accessible outside of class and will give you very detailed explanations even if you email at odd hours. He's a good lecturer and his accent is easy to understand. Office hours are even more helpful! Tests are an okay difficulty and are weighed fairly.

Vinod is excellent at teaching Econ 200 subject matter. If you want an interactive learning environment in a classroom instead of Kane and want to learn the subject matter, you should take his class. He gives individualized feedback on every homework and his lectures are exceptionally organized. He provides you with everything you need to excel.
I would say he is one of the greatest teachers in UW! He's really responsible and helpful! Every time I got stuck , he would give fast and efficient feedback! Highly recommend for sure.

analysis.name: Purnima Dhavan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The best and most lyrical and energetic lecturer in possibly the whole world. Makes sure students are engaging with recent scholarship and debates about historiography and challenges you to make original historical interventions. Emphasizes class issues, the complexity of religious conflict, gender. Very smart and serious but approachable, kind!

Excellent professor!  She knows everything there is to know about south Asian history; her lectures are dense but well-organized, and she is a very engaging speaker.  She has clear expectations, and is always happy to answer questions.  I had very little interest in this region prior to the course, but she manages to make the topic fascinating!

Brutal, covered a lot at top speed (even she admitted it's more like a grad class)--and funny as hell. "Now that the sultan was dead, everyone got along like one big, happy family, yes? Of course not! His successor killed his uncle and blinded his brother," she says, chipper & smiling.  Loved her. All original source readings, hard going.

She is a very good teacher.  Of all the teachers at UW, she's the one who actually cares about what you get out of the class, and How you do in the class. I thought she was awesome. She is lenient on grading, and lectures are engaging. I would love to take her again.

She is extremely passionate and actually cares about how you do in her class. But do NOT take unless you are really into South Asian history.  If you need a writing credit this is a good class.  You can write two 7 pg papers (vs the mandatory two 5 pg papers).

analysis.name: Dinuka Sahabandu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Bro knows how to teach. He goes at a very good pace knowing that the subject is not easy, connects class principle to how they are used in engineers. Very active on discord, will answer any question you have promptly. Gives a ton of resources to practice for midterms and finals. Holds online review sessions for even more practice and clarification.
Professor Sanabandu does not give the best lecture but he personally is an easy-going and helpful instructor and the course contents were pretty clear with flexible course pace and rules.

Goated first year professor. he cares about the student so much that he does problem reviews for homework and exams outside of class every week. is not a harsh grader. available all ways on discord even lat at night.

Least enjoyable EE class I have ever taken--probably mostly due to the content, but Sahabandu was not helping. Lectures were poorly paced, his work often had mistakes, and course policies kept changing.

That said, he clearly cares a lot and will try to help you succeed. I have full faith that he'll become a better prof, but he's not there yet IMO.
Really goated professor, always available. Did really bad because of personal matter but can't recommend him more than enough

analysis.name: Gregory Diggs-Yang
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Greg is great. Took his EDUC 310 class on Identity Development Theory. He is very passionate and insightful about what he teaches. Will answer questions and is really nice and accommodating! He really cares about the wellbeing and mental health of his students. Also has funny stories. Encourages you to explore identity and how it affects all of us.

Very picky about how students work in a completely student led class. Complained that we did too much work for our group presentation. Lowered the maximums each time we communicated with him, despite the syllabus stating otherwise. It is absurd how an College of Ed professor doesn't have a clear syllabus and activly discourages student involvment.

He has unclear expectations and high expectations. The class had a lot of work weekly for being a 1 credit pass/fail. Honestly the worst professor I have ever encountered and I strongly recommend you take a class from literally anyone else. He didnt grade anything until 2 days before the quarter ended which makes it hard to know where you stand.

Proceed this professor with caution.

It's an easy to pass class with minimal effort work, but if you're not ready to deal with conflicting  & confusing messaging of class instructions, having mandatory weekend (Friday night, Saturday morning) meetings, and dealing with a professor who's ego is larger than your tuition...

Don't take this class.

There were many mixed reviews about this professor, so I started the course with an open mind. However, for a course that is completely online and you engage with him maybe twice, he is a strict grader with little to no guidelines on what he wants from his students. Awful communicator. Would not recommend this course.

analysis.name: Ben Dittbrenner
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Class mostly graded on labs w/ attendance on poll everywhere & 20% final. Wording/grading on final wasn't the clearest bc it was the only test in class. Most/all grading is by TAs. Dittbrenner mentioned using ChatGPT for a lab guide once when a mistake was found in it but is otherwise a solid lecturer, passionate about beavers, & generally affable
Ben is awesome. He's a great professor and knows a lot and does what he does best (which is GIS)

The class time was very valuable. Ben was very good at explaining concepts and processes in a way that everyone could understand and when there were people having problems he was always able to help them work through it, whatever the issue. Ben also did a great job at making ArcGIS exciting.

analysis.name: Dinara Storfer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: ~60% of required ALEKS homework wasn't taught in class or tested on.  I took HS chem 5 years ago & lectures felt excruciatingly slow – maybe a good pace w/ 0 chem knowledge. Tests are fairly graded & Storfer seems very kind & passionate. 110 is definitely worth taking if you need a chem refresher but can basically be self-taught to little detriment

Exams are ez she gives previous exams that are exactly like the exams she gives. As long as your doing the wkshts she gives out/prac the prev exams you will 4.0 the class. Aleks questions don't show up on the tests so don't waste your time practicing those cause theyre super tedious, material is easy to teach urself if you dont understand lecture

I lowkey feel bad writing this because she is very nice and definitely cares about chem, but her lectures are soooo bad. I got an A in the class, but that's only because I had to teach MYSELF everything. She didn't have clear slides or anything to go over and would basically just yap about chem for an hour and go on hella useless tangents.
explained things in a way I understand

Professor Storfer is a good person, just a terrible teacher. She as an accent which makes everything so much harder to understand. Despite this, if you are going to take 142, take this class first. Her lectures are useless and the textbook is bad(don't buy it), but make sure you go to each test review lecture. 
Tests are wayway easier than the hw.

analysis.name: Veronica Di Stilio
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Honestly she's chill, gets a lot of hate from what I've seen in the other ratings. If you show up and are respectful she also is. This was my 2nd ever plant class and it was honestly completely reasonable for a 5 credit class. There is a lot of reading, but this is a 400 level class, so like you know what you're signing up for lol.

Took her for BIOL442, horrible teacher, not accommodating, rude and passive-aggressive towards students. Confusing, disjointed lectures. Quizzes are made to trip you up, with lots of "half-correct" answer options. I came into this class with prior experience with plant biology, but she expects you to know as much as a grad student. Don't take.

One word horrible! She messes up on grading and has to fix it afterward. Her canvas course is disorganized as are her lectures. She is not good at explaining the content. Her panapto recordings are muffled and hard to understand. It's a complete nightmare. Do not take this course. This is coming from a student that consistently gets great grades

I would not wish my worst enemy to take a class taught by distillio. I have sufficient background in plants and evolution and was still constantly in a state of confusion throughout the course. She was condescending, expected graduate level understanding of plant genetics and graded harshly. For the sake of your mental health, do not take this

This is my second time taking Biol 180 & trust me she is one of the better Biology professors at UW. She has study questions & practice exams, & they're similar to what the midterm looks like. She's extremely helpful during her office hours & she seem to care about the students. Her test was easy compare to the first one I took 2 quarters ago.

analysis.name: Frank Dimaio
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor DiMaio was a wonderful lecturer and professor, but the exams presented felt a little bit unfair or extremely detailed for something that wasn't covered as excessively as it should've been. However, he's incredibly intelligent and does well in responding to students questions clearly and really does care if we understand the material.

Very sweet and very nervous when lecturing in front of students. Knowledgeable when answering questions. His lecture videos were just his slides and him on a separate screen talking at you. Clear, but not as engaging as Neil King's. All test questions are material from the slides, so if you just memorize the slides, you'll ace this class.

Professor Frank was a really sweet guy who is very energetic about the topic of biochem. Although Biochem may be very boring at times and the lectures project this unfortunately, Frank tries his best to make it easy to follow along. Office hours were very helpful to me. This class also does only focus on exams so make sure that you are prepared.

Cool professor! Maybe his lectures are a bit drier than Neil King's, but his slideshows are really easy to follow (Anki image occlusion enhanced - thank me later). Certainly cares about the topic and is approachable outside of class.

Exams are based 100% of stuff on lecture slides, but make sure you know every little detail on the slides, no need for textbook. Pre-lecture quizzes, TA questions, and practice exams are pretty reflective of real exams. A TON of material, review material as you go and start studying wayyy in advance.

analysis.name: Diana Ruiz
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I revised an essay from this class for my grad school app. I got in! I still think about the films in this class and the readings were heavy but you can get by skimming. Office hours were so helpful. I think only one other CMS prof goes by Prof/Dr instead of their first name, but that's always felt more respectful to me and what I would want tbh

Professor Ruiz's class was just okay. It wasn't exactly what I was expecting and I sometimes didn't attend class. Content wasn't super interesting for me personally, but Professor Ruiz made every effort to invest us in the course. Projects were super fun, however.

If you want to watch really interesting films & read literature surrounding diverse topics we do not discuss enough in American education, this is a fabulous class. However, the prof is extremely rude outside of lecture, has a superiority complex, and does the bare minimum when it comes to explaining assignments. Praying I never have her again.
Her class is interactive, and she really encourages you to participate in the discussion. I like taking her class. You learn a lot in taking her class.

analysis.name: Ananya Diwaka
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor is very kind. She is young and a recent grad student, her info is BASED macro. She doesn't make things overly complicated. You don't really need to attend in person if you're good at teaching yourself. She does not record lectures and sometimes opens zoom if ur sick. I would take again. She really cares about her students.

Super sweet teacher overall, she explains everything super in depth. Only complaint is that she uses a third-party software that is a little pricey for the homework, but you don't need to read the textbook at all, only study the slides. If you go to lecture easy 4.0

Talked about basic macro econ information. Used examples to explain the concept. Had midterm and final. But the professor didn't have the past exam. And she did it in a different way than the other professors before.

analysis.name: Dmitriy Drusvyatskiy
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Worst, really tough grader, no hw and exam answers posted, unclear lecture, unclear grading scale, no one answering questions, worst class that I have ever take.

The professor follows very closely to the textbook. It's as if he copied the book into his lectures verbatim. Oh wait, that's exactly what he did. The tests are based on the HW but no answer keys for the HW provided so we don't even know if we did it right. No answer keys for the exams either. You'd be better off reading the textbook by yourself.

His explanations of topics are very unclear and he expects students to know a lot of information from classes that are not prerequisites. Lectures are very confusing and have little value when doing the homework and exams. If you want to read from the textbook and teach yourself all the material then this is the class for you.
Obviously he put very little effort in teaching. The lectures are a mess. I did learn nothing from him.

If he will be teaching something you've never learned before, definitely avoid him. He teaches as if his students are already aware of all the materials. His homework problems are ridiculous since they're nothing like what we do in class. Tried to get help on homework through email, but all he said was we know enough to finish them. avoid him

analysis.name: Madeleine Dong
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Kind professor who knows a lot of information about Chinese History--the information flow can be a lot to process in lecture. Class is organized on doing the textbook readings, and there's a lot of supplemental reading as well. Quizzes have some pure recall elements, so make sure you get your facts and dates down. Good class if you're passionate.

STAY AWAY FROM HER CLASS UNLESS YOU ARE A CHINESE HISTORY EXPERT AND FLUENT IN MANDARIN Have no idea what she expects, no clear rubric on how she grades. Lectures are hard to follow No midterm & finals but 3 paper, 25% each, 10% reading notes (which I think is stupid), 15% active participation. 7 books to read, plus readings on canvas. TOO MUCH!

Very unorganized. Learned nothing. Got poor grades for the papers because she does not give clear directions. Lots of reading, it's a 400-level class but it doesn't mean I need to finish at least one thick, dense book a week. Have no idea what's going on in this class. You can't disagree with her, she'll argue with you, or you get bad paper grades.

Professor Dong is INCREDIBLY intelligent; you'll find that all of the class material connects at the end. Her lectures tend to run long and sometimes don't include breaks. She doesn't rely on powerpoints and instead gives papers with notes outlined. Make sure to raise your hand at least once a class for participation points and for discussion.

This was one of the best classes I have taken at the university. Prof has real insights. The amount of reading is serious, but it is not 7 full books, just 200 pages/week. There are no exams, just three papers, and the topics are all discussed in detail in class meetings. If you are serious with studying, she goes extra mile to help you.

analysis.name: Douglas Anderson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The assignment budget he offers is very forgiving. However, you will probably need to attend every lecture to have a firm grasp of the type of film analysis he wants you to employ—I was mostly fine with just the readings, but if you are unfamiliar with esoteric philosophical concepts and abstract thinking you may find this course challenging.

He is super nice and friendly always available when I need help discussing class materials and assignments. I also did writing credit with him. He cares about students' progress and well-being. He is kind of verbose but it's for the clarity of the content. I think he is still experimenting with his teaching methods, but he is very easy to talk to.

Lecture heavy but I personally enjoyed every part of it! He assigns about 1 film and 1 reading per class which is super doable. You can even go without it because he will go over it during class. He's passionate and you can tell he really knows what he's talking about. No graded homework, 1 group project, and 2 exams that are all straightforward.

He's nice, but his lectures are SUPER dense. Bi-weekly essays had flexible due-dates but were graded pretty harshly. The material he taught was interesting but the way that it was taught wasn't engaging at all; just lectures, readings, and essays. Highly recommend going to his office hours; he's down to earth & helpful in smaller groups.

This was a very challenging course because the lectures were pretty dense, but I found them to be very engaging. He clearly cared about his students' success and I greatly enjoyed the way he structured the course.

analysis.name: Dongsheng Zang
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Not good. You don't know his grading criteria and he could ruin your GPA. Just run away as far and quickly as you can.

This professor set out to understand his students. He provided a coffee with the professor and two to three students sign up to have coffee with him after class for half an hour. At that meeting, he finds out from the student how their learning experience can be improved. The students had expert days and we had visiting speakers. Id take the class.
The scoring is very strange and there are no scoring criteria.

He's really accessible and invested in the students learning. There are visiting speakers too and expert days. the slides are very helpful and so are the videos. The exam preparation is adequate. I would take the class again.
not easy to do with and weird professor.

analysis.name: Dong-Jae Eun
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class is very lax u just do your own thing for the quarter with a few presentations and a longish paper at the end. He knows his stuff and i really enjoyed talking with him. Def does interrupt people when they are presenting, but i would say the presentations are just a more casual thing than people realize. Still annoying.
Professor Eun is really easy to contact and reply Email in a pretty fast pace as well. In addition, class was heavily project based and if you follow the rubric, it should be a straight A.

Worst prof i've ever seen..........grade came out at last minute and there is no time to argue. HE DID NOT COMMENT ON YOUR PAPER AT ALL, just threw at you a range of grade...did nothing at all. irresponsible.... If there are any other course you can take, don't take his:))))))

He is a great professor who encourages students to explore topics as much as we want. He is also very helpful and accessible outside the class. Even though there is a long paper to write, you can get an A easily if you satisfy all requirements.
Disrespectful and irresponsible. Always cut people off when they are speaking and did not make the scoring clear....

analysis.name: Drew Gorman-Lewis
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Drew explained all the topics well and kept your interest. The tests took a lot of studying in order to do well. A couple of the labs were challenging, but the majority of them were easily understandable. Drew set clear expectations and gave plenty of time and prep for the final project.

Such interesting class; Prof really wants you to succeed and love the material. Lectures are pretty straight forward but in order to fully understand assignments, ATTEND OFFICE HOURS. I switched to the ESS major physics option because this class really captured my interests to earth and space. Assignments 100% of grade. No tests, 1 assign/week.
Good lectures, but difficult assignments which are generally a lot of work.

analysis.name: Dru Williams
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I love Dru, His lecture might seem a bit long but the class was very easy. Just do the homework and assignment, you will pass with flying grade. I had him for CMST 101. We had a presentation for our final and it was really easy, we are getting graded on whether or not we tried to present, not the fact if our presentation was good enough.

Although Dru puts forth LOADS of effort to make sure his students understand important concepts, he is overly aggressive and intense. He uses intimidation as a technique to maintain order. Having rules is respectable, but making your students feel like they have run over a kitten when -for example-arriving late is unnecessary.

Overall, Dru is great.  He cares about if we learn, allows for class input/creativity, and is very clear and articulate.  He can be harsh at times though, both in grading and personality, but no reason not to take a class from him.  I learned a lot and really improved my public speaking!
His class is interesting, but a lot of work. He really challenges you and can call on you to answer questions at any time. But, he has a good humor. He has good explanations and very articulate.

analysis.name: Andrew Gibbon
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My blue hair king, Fitz was my first CSE class and while it was hard he was there and present in helping students, fast emails, and clear directions on homework. Though, I hated the in person tests that were a little nitpicky, but he does help you prepare well and owns up to his own faults as well.

Yes, the course can be a bit challenging, but it's compared to my other courses like organic chemistry, microbiology, endocrinology, its nowhere near that level of difficulty. If you are interested in the content and show up, you should do pretty well. In my opinion, Fitz is an amazing professor, really loved taking the class with them.

Prof gives you an ez practice quiz and then pulls the rug from under ur legs during the actual quiz. Tries to put trick questions that has more to do with syntax issues rather than the logic of course content. If possible, please for your own sake avoid this prof at all costs.

lectures dont do much at all besides basic python when the homework is expecting much more and only gives vague instructions after the first 2. class as a whole isn't terribly difficult if you use outside resources to help learn. and this is different for every quarter I assume but the TAs were awful; took over a month to grade homework
Not really good at covering concepts. Just skims through the minimum and kinda just expects you to know everything for hw and quiz. The quiz is 40% btw. Definitly NOT a class for beginners.

analysis.name: Andrea Durant
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The absolute GOAT. Amazing lecturer with great informative slides. She is very accessible outside of class and you can tell she really cares about your success. Class material isn't hard and make sure you answer everything using flux reasoning. Ask questions, review notes and homework and you're pretty much set. If you can take her, DO IT!

Dr. Durant has no reviews on RMP so I thought I would leave her one! BIOL350 is my first "in-my-major" course and I'm very pleased with how it's going! She is very accessible outside of class and is happy to answer questions in class. The exam material is straightforward, relating to lecture slides, peer-facilitating hours, and discussion section.

Out of my harsh quarter this was a class I really enjoyed! The content is a lot but I would say it's manageable and she makes it easy to understand. The tests are actually based on the content and not curveballs. Your effort is definitely reflected, if you study good you'll get a good grade for sure.

Dr. Durant is a good and fair teacher. She expects you to know content from class and draws from practice questions to make exams, which I appreciate it. She is always willing to help you succeed as long as you make the effort to go to her. The content fascinates me and wish I could take again.

analysis.name: Gary Drobny
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took him for the B-term summer quarter which was waaaay easier than normal full term pchem one. His quizzes were super easy, way easier than homework it was almost unbelievable. BEWARE OF HIS FINAL. You may fall into a false sense of security but the average grade on the final (w/curve) was a 2.3 and worth 45% of our grade.

Very chill professor and is easily accessible outside of class. He is a very classic lecturer and does all his work on the whiteboard/chalkboard - so it's recommended to print out his lecture notes (or read them beforehand) to follow his lectures. Quizzes are pretty fair - easier than the homework but still tough. Brush. Up. On. Calculus.
He is Gandalf reincarnated! Extremely wise and expert in his feild, take a class and you will learn a lot

Weekly online homework (done on mastering chemistry), in-class quizzes (every other week), organized and clear lecture notes posted online, answers homework questions during tutorial (optional class). Professor Drobny is very intelligent, knowledgeable, and humorous.

Amazing professor!!! Always makes time for students and wants them to do well in class. You can tell that he is passionate about what he does, which makes the lectures interesting. Would 10000% recommend.

analysis.name: Shannon Dudley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He doesn't know what he is teaching about.

his "lecture notes" are just dash facts, no slides, so when the 3 exams come up you have NO IDEA what's suppose to be on the exam. He says you don't need the $200 book but writes questions based on the book.

I took this class for the easy 4.0 but let me tell you, it is not an easy 4.0! there are 3 tests and one tiny essay, the essay is easy but the tests are very specific and cover a lot of material that he had NEVER once gone over in class. To make things worse, he doesn't require the textbook so you have to know things without having heard them

I expected this class to be a gap booster, but it was the exact opposite. Your entire grade is based on three tests because there aren't any homework assignments and the class is not curved. He expects you to know details about songs that he barely talks about or doesn't even mention in class on the tests. I would not recommend this class.

The class used to be known as an easy 4.0 but now it is nothing close. His tests are not fair and have very specific questions on things he barely mentioned in lecture while not including questions on the important main ideas. Tests are also the only part of the grade. Would not recommend. Made me dislike music.

analysis.name: Andrea Duncan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: memorize names, monkeys, phylogenies, and random facts! She posts ALL 6-7 poll Q's at 8:32A SHARP. 1stQ checks if you are physically present -- if you miss this, you get 0/6 for poll that day. No mercy if you have a 1.5hr commute and are late 5 mins. terrible wording on exams. avg70% (W/extra credit), NO CURVE. Would NOT recommend to anyone.

Very interesting class. Great lecturer. The classes were engaging and you can tell there was passion about the subject. Very hard to get a 4.0, but still my favorite class. The exams we had were the most challenging. My biggest critique for the course were the study guides, which were pretty vague.

Very nice and approachable but her class was disorganized and expectations weren't clear. She tried to use poll everywhere but didn't know how so they were few and unpredictable, and same for panapto. Hard to get a good grade bc only grades are one midterm and one final which she expects you to memorize very specific and unnecessary info for

She's a very nice person, is very straightforward with her expectations, and is extremely passionate about the subject. The only thing I will say is that it's difficult to feel fully prepared for her exams--the study guide for both the second midterm and the final did not include a single practice question and her averages are ~70% per exam.

This class is a standard 200 level class. Duncan likes averages to be ~70% and will curve it up to 70 if it's lower. Questions were fair. Content was kinda hard, but not because of her. It's a mix of in-depth biology, math, and history. Dawgpath says only 3% of students 4.0 this class, but if you genuinely study hard it's possible!

analysis.name: Scott Dunham
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Exams were challenging with 60-70% averages on the midterms and 50% average on the final, but partial credit grading was very fair. Reading the textbook is essential and you can do well on the exams with lots of practice problems from the textbook. Explanations in class were not always clear which makes the book so important.

A nice person, but an oblivious professor. Doesn't explain concepts clearly in class, so individu learning from the text is essential. Class organization with labs is also poor: Labs will often require use of new tools with no documentation or guidelines. In last quarter of class, the textbook is no longer used, so lecture notes are all you have. D
I think he knows his stuff but I know he does not know how to teach. You leave class confused wondering what you did in your life to deserve him. Avoid if you can!!!

Read the Book. And start your homeworks as early as possible and get as much help as you can get. If you come in armed only with the stuff you know from EE215 and general EE knowledge, this won't be an easy class. The content itself is actually pretty easy, but if you depend solely on lecture and quiz section, you are not going to succeed.
He gives practice exams that are similar to the real exam but the answer key is often incomplete

analysis.name: Jennifer Dubrow
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Long drawn out boring lectures with talking and rambling that goes in circles. Even worse is that participation is graded. Some of the material is interesting and she is very enthusiastic about it, but her shrill voice is unbearable. Only take the class if you truly love the subject.
Super energetic! Very passionate. Weekly "journal" entry, but it can be anything from a written reflection to a creative project. You get what you put into the class. Def recommend!

Dubrow is knowledgeable and passionate. This is my second time in her class and I enjoyed it just as much the second time. The assignments were very reasonable (borderline easy) and she makes any readings available online in PDFs. She does ramble sometimes but it is interesting. You can skip class but you will be behind in the readings/discussions.
mind numbing subject coupled with a really overbearing annoying professor.

She is well-versed in the content she teaches and is extremely enthusiastic about it. Assignments were manageable but she's a hard grader for a class that is only an A&H credit and discussion based. No recordings and the class is longer than necessary. She has high expectations on essays with little guidance and rubric. Good readings though.

analysis.name: Dwayne Arola
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Arola is one of the best lecturers I have had during my entire undergraduate career here at UW. His ability to speak clearly and explain concepts in an easy-to-understand manner makes his lectures engaging. On top of that, he knows his stuff and is able to answer students' questions in great detail. I only wish I had more courses with him.
He is new in the department and actually graduated from UW.  The course was valuable and I can say he is definitely one of the better speakers in MSE.  Has high expectations.

Dr. Arola is a great and charismatic professor. This class was super interesting - I was never bored during lecture. You can tell he is passionate about the subject and cares for his students. Highly recommend!!

One of the best professors at UW. 
Everything is very straight-forward.

analysis.name: Anne Dwyer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Dwyer's class, The Politics of Imprisonment, is highly recommended. If you want to find out what's actually happening in our society, you must attend. It's a transformative experience. Anyone interested in social justice must experience this class.

This class I did terrible in. It wasn't like "hard" or anything, the topics were a little difficult to understand but the discussions during class helped. The reason why I got such a crap grade was honestly because of how badly I did on the papers, and for missing a few classes. She takes attendance each class.

Politics of Imprisonment was an eye-opening class. Prof. Dwyer wasn't afraid to talk about tough topics, but always went out of her way to make sure everyone felt comfortable. Very supportive for outside-the-box final projects. 10/10 would highly recommend!
In-class discussions were phenomenal, and she is very open to student ideas.  That being said, nothing was graded until the final week of the quarter, which was stressful.

analysis.name: Dylon Chow
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: If I had to be in dylon's class again, I would drop out. Frankly, he seemed like he couldn't care less for his classes. Many professors grade by few things however they do show you steps on how to succeed but Professor Chow never really cared. He would only teach his material and would never want to solve extra doubts.

Surprisingly I really liked this class! Prof Chow has really clear lectures with lots of example problems, and he doesn't make things too conceptual. Grading was test-heavy, but he wasn't a super harsh grader and tests were just like the practice tests. It was 90% for the 2 midterms and final, and 10% for homework, with 1 WebAssign homework weekly.

There are only four assignments for the gradebook (3 being exams) so it is hard to recover your grade in this class. The exams were pretty difficult but people did pretty well so its not curved much. He teaches really fast and and often seems confused on the material himself and when students ask questions. If you're a poor tester you may struggle

Lectures and notes are very unorganized. Goes back and forth with course material. Writing was illegible at first, but got better as the quarter went on. Homework and midterms are pretty easy. There are not a lot of study material available. Final was a lot harder than the midterm and had questions about something he mentioned in a lecture once.

He wasn't very good at explaining the material. Also, 90% of your final grade depends on 2 midterms and the final, so don't mess up! The remaining 10% is homework. He said at the beginning of the quarter that he COULD add weekly quizzes to divide up the grade, but he "didn't want to". I recommend looking for a better-rated prof if you get him.
